| `calibration_precision_relative_fatol` | 2.0.0 | numbers | metrics | calibration.precision writes a relative fatol, so Nelder-Mead stops on the same simplex two trials earlier. On example 04 the calibrated Sy goes from 0.04411 to 0.04296 and 1 - nse_log from 0.083976 to 0.083988, with two solves less. K does not move. |
| `calibration_cache_keys_change_once` | 2.0.0 | identity | none | Every cache key of a calibration changes once, so the trials of a session of a pre-release are solved again. |
| `old_figure_ledger_entries_skipped` | 2.0.0 | refusal | none | hmp export –regen figures skips a figure that figures/index.json records from a figure of a pre-release, with the command that draws it now, and draws the other entries. It used to redraw it from its old options. |
| `geotiff_resolution_in_the_output_crs` | 2.0.0 | layout | none | A GeoTIFF of a field exported into another CRS reads resolution in the units of that CRS, as the reference says. The mesh is rasterized at its own pixel, the side of its smallest cell, then reprojected onto pixels of resolution. resolution was applied in the units of the model CRS before the reprojection, so resolution = 0.0005 with crs = “EPSG:4326” asked for 23 100 000 by 20 850 000 pixels on a 120 km2 model and the export failed. An export in the model CRS does not change. No value of a run changes. |
| `figures_after_a_failed_export` | 2.0.0 | layout | none | An export that fails after the seal no longer stops the figures: they are drawn, then the run exits with the export error. A figure with engine = [“static”, “interactive”] writes its PNG and its HTML page during a run, where it wrote the PNG alone. A series of one period, on a steady run or in a window of one month, is skipped with its reason, where it drew an empty panel. hmp show <run> –figure <name> –time <date> draws that date and records it in figures/index.json, where it drew the default instant. No value of a run changes. |
| `dates_are_iso_8601_only` | 2.0.0 | refusal | none | A date of [simulation.time], of a steady_window and of a calibration window is a TOML date, a TOML datetime or an ISO 8601 string. start_datetime = 2003 and “2003” were read as 2003 seconds after 1970-01-01, and a window bound “01/02/2003” as 2 January. All three are refused with the form a date takes, and so are two bounds of which only one carries a UTC offset. No valid date changes. |
| `monthly_edges_counted_from_the_start` | 2.0.0 | numbers | heads@modflow6, fluxes@modflow6, heads@modflow_nwt, fluxes@modflow_nwt, heads@boussinesq, fluxes@boussinesq, metrics | Each edge of a time grid with a step in months or years is the start plus k steps. A start on the 29th, 30th or 31st drifted, because each step was added to the previous edge: from 31 January the periods began on 28 February, 28 March and 28 April, and they now begin on 28 February, 31 March and 30 April. A start on the 1st to the 28th, and a step in days or hours, give the same grid as before. |
| `protocol_1_4_draws_the_map_as_given` | 2.0.1 | numbers | metrics | map.drawn_by defaults to “crossing”: the mapped network is drawn on the cells as the data gives it, the rule of the paper, still cut to the catchment. It defaulted to “heads”, which kept only the stream heads of the map and drew the rest down the model’s own descent. A calibration with no pin on the protocol follows 1.4, which differs from 1.3 by this rule alone. A pin on 1.3, or map.drawn_by = “heads” in the network output, gives the heads rule back. A run that sealed no network output draws its network figures by the crossing rule too. A file of edition 2.0 that writes no drawn_by moves with it, at the request of the owner, so its K and costs change wherever heads and crossing draw different cells. |
| `lake_keeps_the_cells_it_covers` | 2.0.1 | numbers | heads@modflow6, fluxes@modflow6, metrics | On a mesh whose faces follow the lake shores but leave the ring open somewhere (an arm narrower than a cell, a wall that leaves the shore), a lake owns the cells its polygon covers for more than half of their area, each cell whole. It owned every cell the polygon touched, so a ring of land cells one cell wide joined the lake and had its top carved under the highest stage of the abacus. On a reservoir of 200.3 ha whose shore the faces cover at 99.45 %, the lake goes from 1 256 cells and 296.3 ha to 885 cells and 201.3 ha, and the cells it leaves keep their terrain and get their drain back. A mesh that closes every shore, and a mesh without lake faces, do not change. |
| `uniform_recharge_written_as_constant` | 2.0.2 | numbers | heads@modflow6, fluxes@modflow6, metrics | A recharge or soil ETP period with the same rate on every cell, such as the recharge of one station spread over the catchment, is written to MODFLOW 6 as one CONSTANT line with 16 significant digits. A chronicle of 64 periods or more wrote it in one binary file per period, read at full precision, so its rates move by at most 2 units in the last place: 4.4e-16 in relative terms, on 3 288 of 12 418 daily rates. A daily run of 34 years on 28 545 cells writes 2.4 MB of input in 25 s instead of 2.7 GB in 84 s. A shorter chronicle and a rate that varies over the cells do not change. |
| `lake_and_sfr_observations_read_in_binary` | 2.0.2 | numbers | fluxes@modflow6, metrics | The observations of the LAK and SFR packages of MODFLOW 6 are written in binary and read at the double precision of the solver. They were written as CSV text with 10 significant digits, so a lake stage, a lake flow or a reach flow moves by at most 5e-10 in relative terms. The files are lake.lak.obs.bin and model.sfr.obs.bin instead of .csv. The CSV form came out garbled once MODFLOW runs with FORT_BUFFERED. |
| `specific_yield_ceiling_at_one` | 2.0.2 | refusal | none | A specific yield is accepted up to 1, in a field and in the bounds of a calibration. The ceiling was 0.5, so a calibration that searched Sy up to 0.8, as some v1 scripts did, was refused when the file was read. The floor stays at 1e-4. A value that was accepted reads as before. |
| `specific_yield_floor_at_1e_6` | 2.0.2 | refusal | none | A specific yield is accepted down to 1e-6, in a field and in the bounds of a calibration. The floor was 1e-4, so a search could not go below 0.01 per cent, while a sparsely fractured bedrock drains some 1e-5. A value that was accepted reads as before. |
| `interval_end_at_the_bound_when_nothing_lies_beyond` | 2.0.2 | label | none | An end of the cost_profile interval of a calibrated value is marked as reaching the bound of its range when no solved trial lies beyond it. It was marked only when a trial sat exactly on the bound, which a design drawn over the whole box (lhs, lhs_zoom, random_search, scipy_de) never does, so a band that ran to a bound was reported as closed. A local search (scipy_nelder_mead, cma_es) keeps the old rule, since its band may stop where it stopped looking. The interval itself and the calibrated value do not change, and a session sealed before keeps the flag it was written with. |

## Key moves

One key or one value that moves, in the configuration or in a stored document. A live configuration loads a move with a warning until the version in the column Refused from, and is refused with the new name after it. A sealed run reads the row in silence for the whole major line. A key that left is refused at once, with what to write instead.

# What changed in the TOML

Fields added, renamed, removed or changed between two versions. Pick the two versions below; the page opens on the newest release against this documentation. Each released version keeps a snapshot of its fields, built from its git tag, and the page compares the snapshots. Nobody writes this page: a new key, a removed key, a new default or a field moved to another profile shows up here on its own. A key shows as renamed when the new field declares its old path in `renamed_from`; otherwise a rename shows as one removal and one addition.

From 2.0.0 to this documentation.

Defaults that changed

A file that does not write these keys gets a different run.

- `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.drawn_by``"heads"` to `"crossing"`

# `hmp calibrate`

Uses hmp.calibrate().

```
$ hmp calibrate [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--profile [HTML_PATH]] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--phase PHASE] [--resume] [--dry-run] [--no-report] [--list-phases] [--expand] [--case NAME] [--overlay OVERLAY] [--set PATH=VALUE] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] config
```

Run a calibration from a TOML config

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | Path to a calibration TOML file |
| `--phase``PHASE` | Run only this phase of a staged calibration, in the session of the case. Its dependency must have completed there, otherwise the phase would calibrate against un-frozen parameters. |
| `--resume` | Reopen the latest session of the case: the phases that completed with the same fingerprint are read back, the cut phase is solved again with its trials preloading the cache. |
| `--dry-run` | Say which case, which session folder and which phases would run, and write nothing. |
| `--no-report` | Do not write the report of each session once the search is over. hmp show SESSION --report writes it later. |
| `--list-phases` | List the declared phases and exit without running anything. A file without phases gets one line for its single search. |
| `--expand` | Print the [calibration] section a protocol writes, as TOML, and exit without running anything. A file naming no protocol prints its own section. Refused together with --phase, --list-phases, --resume or --dry-run. |
| `--case``NAME` | Name of the case: its session is sessions/<name>. Defaults to [simulation] name, else the stem of the TOML. A calibration launched with --set or --overlay keeps that name; use --case to name the variant. |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--profile``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--overlay``--set``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --dry-run
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --resume
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --list-phases
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --resume --phase phase_name
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --expand
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --set calibration.seed=7
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --overlay daily.toml --case calage_daily
$ hmp calibrate calibration.toml --format json
```

Every launch, --dry-run included, runs the checks of hmp check calibration.toml before anything is prepared. --format json prints the result, the phases or the plan once the command is over, as the page on what a program reads describes them.

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10 14 21. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/campaign.html -->
# `hmp campaign`

```
$ hmp campaign [-h] <action> ...
```

Run a project of many cases, collect it, keep what a calibration found

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp campaign array` | Write the array job of the current plan for a scheduler (SLURM) |
| `hmp campaign case` | Print the case file of task N of a job (jobs/<job>/cases.txt, task 1 first) |
| `hmp campaign collect` | Write summary/ of a project: tables by case and by site, map, figures, exports |
| `hmp campaign promote` | Promote one trial of a calibration session to a run under runs/ |
| `hmp campaign prune` | Move the kept trials of a calibration session to the trash, all but the best |

## `hmp campaign array`

```
$ hmp campaign array [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] --scheduler {slurm} [--partition PARTITION] [--time WALLTIME] [--threads-per-case THREADS_PER_CASE] [--prepare-parallel PREPARE_PARALLEL] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] [project]
```

Write the array job of the current plan for a scheduler (SLURM)

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | Project directory, or its project.toml (default: -w, else the current directory) |
| `--scheduler``SCHEDULER` | Scheduler the job scripts are written for one of `slurm` · required |
| `--partition``PARTITION` | SLURM partition of both arrays |
| `--time``WALLTIME` | Walltime of one task (M, H:M:S, D-H:M:S); longer than the 600 s warning |
| `--threads-per-case``THREADS_PER_CASE` | Threads of one case (default: [sites.run] threads_per_case) |
| `--prepare-parallel``PREPARE_PARALLEL` | Cases prepared side by side (default: [sites.run] prepare_parallel) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp campaign array . --scheduler slurm
$ hmp campaign array . --scheduler slurm --partition normal --time 12:00:00
```

Writes jobs/<stamp>-slurm/{prepare.sh, array.sh, cases.txt} once, from the plan written by `hmp project plan`. Not verified on a cluster yet.

An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.

## `hmp campaign case`

```
$ hmp campaign case [-h] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [-w WORKSPACE] job task
```

Print the case file of task N of a job (jobs/<job>/cases.txt, task 1 first)

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `job` | Folder under jobs/, or its path |
| `task` | Task number, 1 for the first line of cases.txt |

Also takes the shared options `--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--workspace`.

Example

```
$ hmp campaign case 20261020-143000-slurm 3 -w .
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2. All exit codes.

## `hmp campaign collect`

```
$ hmp campaign collect [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--write-sites] [--mixed-windows] [project]
```

Write summary/ of a project: tables by case and by site, map, figures, exports

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | Project directory, or a folder inside it (default: -w, else the current directory) |
| `--write-sites` | Also write summary/catalog.csv, the sites as a site table (SiteRow columns) |
| `--mixed-windows` | Rank scores computed on different windows or rules together |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp campaign collect
$ hmp campaign collect projects/bretagne_k --write-sites
$ hmp campaign collect . --mixed-windows
```

## `hmp campaign promote`

```
$ hmp campaign promote [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--trial N] [--name NAME] case
```

Promote one trial of a calibration session to a run under runs/

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `case` | Case of the session, <case> or <case>_vN |
| `--trial``N` | Trial number, as trials.jsonl of the session lists it (default: list the best) |
| `--name``NAME` | Run name to take (default: the case, paired with the session when free) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

The case names the session: sessions/<case>[_vN].

Examples

```
$ hmp campaign promote calibration
$ hmp campaign promote calibration --trial 12
$ hmp campaign promote J0014010-calage --trial 4 --name k_high -w projects/bretagne
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp campaign prune`

```
$ hmp campaign prune [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--keep {best}] case
```

Move the kept trials of a calibration session to the trash, all but the best

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `case` | Case of the session, <case> or <case>_vN |
| `--keep``KEEP` | Trials left in place (default: best, the trial session.json points at) one of `best` |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--yes``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp campaign prune calibration --keep best -y
$ hmp campaign prune calibration --dry-run
$ hmp campaign prune J0014010-calage -w projects/bretagne -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10 130. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/catalog.html -->
# `hmp catalog`

Uses hmp.trash().

```
$ hmp catalog [-h] <action> ...
```

Maintain the index of a project and its runs

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp catalog query` | Run a SQL statement against the project index |
| `hmp catalog gc` | Maintenance: measure the project, close dead attempts, trash old versions, purge fields |
| `hmp catalog reindex` | Build the project index from what the run and session directories declare |
| `hmp catalog delete` | Move a run or a session to the trash (reversible); --now to remove it for good |
| `hmp catalog restore` | Move a trashed run or session back to the directory it came from |
| `hmp catalog trash` | Move a run to the trash, list the trash, or remove its entries with --empty |
| `hmp catalog tag` | Add or remove tags on a run (reserved tag: pinned, kept out of trash and gc) |
| `hmp catalog note` | Append a timestamped note to a run |
| `hmp catalog rename` | Rename a run: runs/<old>/ and sessions/<old>/ move to the new name |
| `hmp catalog watch` | Show the running attempts with the age of their heartbeat |
| `hmp catalog import` | Import a run written by 'hmp publish' (directory or tar), with the data it read |
| `hmp catalog rerun` | Launch a run again from its frozen config.toml, with --set path=value overrides |

## `hmp catalog query`

```
$ hmp catalog query [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--limit LIMIT] sql
```

Open the index read-only and run one statement. The tables are those of the index (simulations, cases, attempts, sites, parameters, metrics, calibration_sessions ...) and its views (v_cases, v_simulation_summary).

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sql` | SQL statement to execute against the index |
| `--limit``LIMIT` | Wrap the SQL in a LIMIT clause to cap the result set |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Example

```
$ hmp catalog query "SELECT case_id, label, nse FROM v_cases" --format json
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 1 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp catalog gc`

```
$ hmp catalog gc [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--keep-versions N|all] [--max-age-days DAYS] [--trial-fields-days DAYS|never] [--solver-files-days DAYS]
```

Maintenance: measure the project, close dead attempts, trash old versions, purge fields

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Carry the plan out. Without it the verb prints the plan and changes nothing |
| `--keep-versions``N|all` | Versions kept per run name; older ones go to the trash (default: 5, 'all' disables the rule) |
| `--max-age-days``DAYS` | Also trash runs started more than DAYS ago (default: no age limit) |
| `--trial-fields-days``DAYS|never` | Remove the fields of kept trials older than DAYS, all but the best (default: 90, 'never' disables the rule) |
| `--solver-files-days``DAYS` | Remove the solver/ folder that keep_solver_files kept in sealed runs older than DAYS (default: never, the folders stay) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

A directory tagged 'pinned' is never collected. Trash entries are removed 30 days after their deletion. The fields of a kept trial leave after 90 days, all but the best.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog gc
$ hmp catalog gc --dry-run --format json
$ hmp catalog gc --keep-versions 3 --max-age-days 180 -y
$ hmp catalog gc --trial-fields-days never -y
$ hmp catalog gc --solver-files-days 30 -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp catalog reindex`

```
$ hmp catalog reindex [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--incremental]
```

Read every directory under runs/ and sessions/ and write .hmp/index.duckdb from them: the sealed runs with their label of the day, the attempts that failed or are running, the calibration sessions with their trials. The index is written to a staging file and published in one atomic step, so a reader keeps reading until the new one is there, and building twice yields the same index. With --incremental only the directories that appeared, changed or disappeared since the last pass are written.

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--incremental` | Write only what changed since the last pass; a full rebuild otherwise |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog reindex
$ hmp catalog reindex --incremental
```

## `hmp catalog delete`

```
$ hmp catalog delete [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--site SITE] [--now] [--force] SIM_REF
```

Move a run or a session to the trash (reversible); --now to remove it for good

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |
| `--now` | Remove the directory for good: a tombstone keeps its name from being reused |
| `--force` | Go past the pin and the stale attempt: act on a pinned directory, or on one whose attempt stopped beating |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--yes``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--site`.

The reference is the directory: a bare name is runs/<name> exactly, and a bare name whose stem has other versions is refused with the list.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog delete baseline_v2 -y
$ hmp catalog delete sessions/calibration -y
$ hmp catalog delete baseline_daily --now -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 130. All exit codes.

```
$ hmp catalog restore [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] SIM_REF
```

Move a trashed run or session back to the directory it came from

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | The name 'hmp catalog trash' lists, or the directory the entry came from (baseline_daily, sessions/calibration) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog restore baseline_daily
```

## `hmp catalog trash`

```
$ hmp catalog trash [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--empty] [--force] [REF]
```

Move a run to the trash, list the trash, or remove its entries with --empty

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `REF` | Move this run or session to trash/. Without it, list the trash. |
| `--empty` | Remove every trashed directory for good (frees disk, leaves tombstones) |
| `--force` | Go past the pin: remove the pinned directories too when emptying |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--yes``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Each removed entry leaves a line in trash/tombstones.txt, so its name is never given to a new run.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog trash
$ hmp catalog trash --empty --dry-run
$ hmp catalog trash --empty --force -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 130. All exit codes.

## `hmp catalog rename`

```
$ hmp catalog rename [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--site SITE] SIM_REF new_name
```

Rename a run: runs/<old>/ and sessions/<old>/ move to the new name

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |
| `new_name` | New directory name |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--site`.

The directory is the name, so a rename moves runs/<old>/ and, for a calibration, sessions/<old>/ to the new name. Links between them are ids and stay valid. The new name must be free: a live directory, a trashed one or a tombstone holding it is refused.

Example

```
$ hmp catalog rename baseline_v2 baseline_k2e5
```

## `hmp catalog watch`

```
$ hmp catalog watch [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--stale-minutes STALE_MINUTES]
```

Read the outcome.json and logs/heartbeat.json of every run directory and list the attempts that are running. The index is never opened: this answers while a solve is going on and on a project that has no index yet.

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--stale-minutes``STALE_MINUTES` | Heartbeat age (minutes) beyond which a running attempt is flagged stale default `5.0` |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Example

```
$ hmp catalog watch --stale-minutes 5
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp catalog import`

```
$ hmp catalog import [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--name NAME] source
```

Import a run written by 'hmp publish' (directory or tar), with the data it read

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | Directory or tar written by 'hmp publish' |
| `--name``NAME` | Name of the imported run (default: the published name without its _vN) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

The run lands under runs/ with the next free version of its name, read without its _vN: a published x_v2 becomes x in a project that has no x. Pass --name to give it the name other documents cite.

A copy carries its inputs unless it was published with --without inputs, so it installs every file the run read into data/ of the workspace: identical bytes already there cost nothing, other bytes at the same path are refused by name, and nothing is written.

Examples

```
$ hmp catalog import baseline.tar
$ hmp catalog import ../published/baseline --name lab_copy
```

## `hmp catalog rerun`

```
$ hmp catalog rerun [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--site SITE] [--set PATH=VALUE] [--name NAME] SIM_REF
```

Launch a run again from its frozen config.toml, with --set path=value overrides

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |
| `--set``PATH=VALUE` | Dotted config path override, repeatable (e.g. flow.param.K.field.value=2e-4) The grammar of a key path and a value |
| `--name``NAME` | Name of the new run (default: the name of the source, next version) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--site`.

The new run keeps the name of its source and takes the next version; its manifest names the source in lineage (parent_sim_id, kind = rerun). A key that differs from config.resolved.toml of the source gets a warning and is recorded in lineage.drift.

Example

```
$ hmp catalog rerun baseline --set flow.param.K.field.value=2e-4
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/check.html -->
# `hmp check`

Uses hmp.check().

```
$ hmp check [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--partial] [--inputs] [--lang {en,fr}] [--overlay OVERLAY] [--set PATH=VALUE] file
```

Check a run, a calibration or a whole [sites] project, every fault at once

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Path to the TOML configuration |
| `--partial` | Check a draft: a required key not written yet is to_fill, not an error |
| `--inputs` | Also read the header of each input file, local or by its final URL (downloads nothing) |
| `--lang``LANG` | Language of the phrase of each diagnostic (default: en) one of `en` | `fr` |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--overlay``--set`.

Examples

```
$ hmp check run.toml
$ hmp check draft.toml --partial
$ hmp check calibration.toml -v
$ hmp check project.toml --inputs --lang fr
$ hmp check project.toml --overlay sites/canut.toml
```

Every fault is listed at once, one line each. A key the file does not write yet is an error, or with --partial a to_fill that stops nothing. A calibration is read by its preflight and says which published method it runs and where it departs from it (-v adds the stages and the references). The last one expands a [sites] project and checks every case. -v also says which workspace the file resolves to, with its folders.

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/completion.html -->
# `hmp completion`

```
$ hmp completion [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] {bash,zsh,fish}
```

Print a shell completion script for bash, zsh, or fish

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `shell` | Shell flavour to print completion for one of `bash` | `zsh` | `fish` |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace`.

Examples

```
$ hmp completion bash
$ hmp completion fish
```

In bash or zsh, load the script in the current shell with eval "$(hmp completion bash)", or add that line to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc. In fish, pipe it to source. The script asks hmp for the commands each time you press TAB, so it follows the commands that exist.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/data.html -->
# `hmp data`

```
$ hmp data [-h] <action> ...
```

Data cache of a workspace and the lockfile of a project

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp data ls` | List the rows of the workspace data cache |
| `hmp data get` | Serve a data request: one file per variable, cut to the extent and period |
| `hmp data remove` | Remove cache rows for a variable/provider/station |
| `hmp data prune` | Drop cache rows older than N days, except the files a run or a lockfile cites |
| `hmp data lock` | Write the lockfile that pins the data of a project, or check the files against it |
| `hmp data archive` | Archive the cache (files, sidecars and lockfile) to a portable file |
| `hmp data restore` | Restore a cache archive into the workspace |

## `hmp data ls`

```
$ hmp data ls [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--variable VARIABLE] [--provider PROVIDER]
```

List the rows of the workspace data cache

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--variable``VARIABLE` | Filter by variable |
| `--provider``PROVIDER` | Filter by provider |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp data ls
$ hmp data ls --variable dem --provider bdalti
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp data get`

```
$ hmp data get [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] --to DIR [--bbox MINX,MINY,MAXX,MAXY | --mask MASK | --stations STATIONS] [--crs CRS] [--start START] [--end END] [--source SOURCE] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] REQUEST_OR_VARIABLE
```

Serve a data request: one file per variable, cut to the extent and period

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `REQUEST_OR_VARIABLE` | a request document (.json) or a variable name (e.g. dem, hydrometry) |
| `--to``DIR` | folder that receives the files required |
| `--bbox``MINX,MINY,MAXX,MAXY` | box in the CRS --crs names. When minx is negative, write '--bbox=-1.17,48.4,-1.0,48.5' (= sign). |
| `--mask``MASK` | vector file bounding the request |
| `--stations``STATIONS` | comma-separated station codes, for station variables |
| `--crs``CRS` | CRS of --bbox, as EPSG:<code> |
| `--start``START` | first date of the period (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--end``END` | last date of the period, kept whole (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--source``SOURCE` | source to ask, when the variable has several |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp data get dem --source bdalti --to data/dem --bbox 340000,6780000,350000,6790000 --crs EPSG:2154
$ hmp data get precipitation --to data/precipitation --mask catchment.gpkg --start 2015-01-01 --end 2020-12-31 --source sim2
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14 16. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.

```
$ hmp data remove [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--variable VARIABLE] [--provider PROVIDER] [--station-id STATION_ID] [--delete-files]
```

Remove cache rows for a variable/provider/station

| Argument | What it does |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--yes``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Example

```
$ hmp data remove --variable precipitation --provider sim2 --delete-files -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10 130. All exit codes.

```
$ hmp data prune [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--older-than OLDER_THAN] [--delete-files]
```

Drop cache rows older than N days, except the files a run or a lockfile cites

## `hmp data lock`

```
$ hmp data lock [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--project PROJECT] [--check] [--strict] [--to FILE] [--lockfile LOCKFILE]
```

Write the lockfile that pins the data of a project, or check the files against it

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |

| `--lockfile``LOCKFILE` | Lockfile to check (with --check) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples


Exit codes it sets itself: 2 16. All exit codes.

-w takes a workspace root or a project inside it; without it, the workspace that holds the current directory. It has to exist: run `hmp workspace init` first.


# Exit codes

A command ends with the code of its outcome. Codes 0, 1 and 2 keep their usual meaning, 130 is the POSIX code of an interrupted process, and the codes from 10 name the category of the failure. An exception that a command does not catch ends with the code of its class.

| Code | Name | Raised for | Set directly by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | `EXIT_OK` | Nothing: the command succeeded. | |
| `1` | `EXIT_GENERIC` | Any exception that no other row maps. | 4 commands `hmp catalog query`, `hmp export`, `hmp publish`, `hmp doctor` |
| `2` | `EXIT_USAGE` | - | 19 commands `hmp project delete`, `hmp campaign case`, `hmp campaign prune`, `hmp example add`, `hmp catalog delete`, `hmp catalog trash`, `hmp catalog tag`, `hmp catalog rerun`, `hmp data remove`, `hmp data prune`, `hmp data lock`, `hmp ls`, `hmp show`, `hmp export`, `hmp publish`, `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp site import`, `hmp doctor` |
| `10` | `EXIT_NOT_FOUND` | `FileNotFoundError` | 32 commands `hmp workspace list`, `hmp workspace clean`, `hmp project new`, `hmp project delete`, `hmp project list`, `hmp project import`, `hmp campaign promote`, `hmp campaign prune`, `hmp example add`, `hmp catalog query`, `hmp catalog gc`, `hmp catalog watch`, `hmp data ls`, `hmp data get`, `hmp data remove`, `hmp data prune`, `hmp data archive`, `hmp data restore`, `hmp ls`, `hmp show`, `hmp diff`, `hmp check`, `hmp publish`, `hmp run`, `hmp replay`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp spinup`, `hmp site add`, `hmp site import`, `hmp site ls`, `hmp site show`, `hmp doctor` |
| `11` | `EXIT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` | - | |
| `12` | `EXIT_WRITE_CONFLICT` | `FileExistsError` | 1 commands `hmp project delete` |
| `13` | `EXIT_READ_ONLY` | - | |
| `14` | `EXIT_CONFIG` | - | 13 commands `hmp workspace init`, `hmp workspace clean`, `hmp project plan`, `hmp data get`, `hmp show`, `hmp check`, `hmp config`, `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp spinup`, `hmp site add`, `hmp doctor`, `hmp install-binaries` |
| `15` | `EXIT_SOLVER_ERROR` | - | |
| `16` | `EXIT_VALIDATION` | - | 3 commands `hmp data get`, `hmp data lock`, `hmp diff` |
| `17` | `EXIT_CROSS_PROJECTS` | - | |
| `18` | `EXIT_BACKUP_FAILED` | - | |
| `19` | `EXIT_MIGRATION_FAILED` | - | |
| `20` | `EXIT_AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE` | - | |
| `21` | `EXIT_CALIBRATION` | - | 2 commands `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate` |
| `22` | `EXIT_CATALOG_UNREADABLE` | - | |
| `23` | `EXIT_CASES_FAILED` | - | 1 commands `hmp run` |
| `130` | `EXIT_SIGINT` | `KeyboardInterrupt` | 7 commands `hmp project delete`, `hmp campaign prune`, `hmp catalog delete`, `hmp catalog trash`, `hmp data remove`, `hmp data prune`, `hmp run` |

## The code of a failure

A failure prints one line on stderr that starts with its `HMPY.Exxx` code: `HMPY.E002: File not found: run.toml`. Exceptions and error codes lists the classes and their codes. A refusal the command writes itself takes the code of the class of its exit code. `HMPY.E000` is a failure with no category of its own, most often a bug of ours. What a program reads says what a failure prints under `--format json`.

## What is promised

Inside a major version an exit code keeps its number and its meaning, and an `HMPY.Exxx` code keeps its meaning. A new category comes with a new number, so a program reads a number it does not know as a failure. The words of a message can change in any version, so a program reads the codes and never the words.

## Codes each command sets itself

Read from the code of each command: every refusal and every `sys.exit` it reaches. A command that is not listed ends with 0, with 1 for an error, or with the code of an uncaught exception.

# `hmp export`

Uses hmp.export(), hmp.open().

```
$ hmp export [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--list] [--regen [{all,exports,figures}]] [--deliver] [--time TIME [TIME ...]] [--period START END] [--as FORMAT] [--to DEST] [--crs CRS] [--resolution RESOLUTION] [--layer LAYER] [--nodata NODATA] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] SIM_REF [VARIABLE ...]
```

Export data of a run: fields, series, layers, the budget, or the whole run

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SIM_REF` | Full sim_id, unique hex prefix, name, or an @-selector (@last, @best:METRIC, @worst:METRIC, @running) |
| `VARIABLE` | What to export: names from --list, or "all" for everything the run holds, each in its natural format |
| `--list` | Print what this run can export, by kind, and write nothing |
| `--regen``[REGEN]` | Write again what the run recorded: its exports (exports/index.json), its figures (figures/index.json), or both, the default one of `all` | `exports` | `figures` |
| `--deliver` | Send once more the files the [[export]] blocks of the sealed run name, and every file whose bytes changed since. Takes no variable and no export option |
| `--time``TIME [TIME ...]` | Instants to write: dates (2002-10-15), "first" or "last". A date takes the stress period that holds it. Default: the whole simulation |
| `--period``START END` | A window of the simulation, two dates. Every period it overlaps is written |
| `--as``FORMAT` | File format, a name the export registry serves: netcdf, geotiff, csv, a view format like rocrate, or one an installed package adds. Default: the natural format of each data, or the --to extension |
| `--to``DEST` | Where under runs/<run>/exports/: a name with an extension is one exact file, and gives the format; any other is a folder, with automatic names (default: runs/<run>/exports/) |
| `--crs``CRS` | Output CRS of rasters and vector layers, e.g. EPSG:4326 (default: the model CRS) |
| `--resolution``RESOLUTION` | Pixel size of a GeoTIFF, in units of the output CRS (default: the side of the smallest cell) |
| `--layer``LAYER` | Model layer of a field of several layers (0 is the top one) |
| `--nodata``NODATA` | Fill value of the cells a GeoTIFF has no data for (default: -9999) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp export my_run --list
$ hmp export my_run all
$ hmp export my_run head watertable_depth --time 2002-10-15
$ hmp export my_run discharge discharge_obs --period 2001-01-01 2002-12-31
$ hmp export my_run watershed hydrographic_network_reference
$ hmp export my_run watertable_depth --time last --to watertable.tif --crs EPSG:4326
$ hmp export my_run head --to maps/ --as geotiff
$ hmp export my_run --regen
$ hmp export my_run --regen figures
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 1 2. All exit codes.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/machine-output.html -->
# What a program reads

This page is the interface of `hmp` for a script or a platform. `--format json` and `--format csv` print the result of a command in a shape that does not move inside a major version. `--format table`, the default, is for people and promises nothing.

## The envelope

`--format json` prints one JSON object on stdout, and nothing else. It has two keys:

```
{"schema": "hmp.catalog.ls.v1", "data": []}
```

`schema` names the command and the version of what `data` holds. `data` is an array of rows for a command that lists, and an object for any other. A listing with nothing to list is an empty array, never a sentence. Everything else a command says, a solver and a library included, goes to stderr, so stdout always parses. The result is written once the command is over. A value that is not a number in JSON, NaN or an infinity, is `null`, and a path or a date is a string.

`--format csv` prints the same rows with a header, and an empty listing is the header alone. An object is `key,value` lines, or its own table when it holds one: the cases of `hmp ls --plan`, the files of `hmp example show`, the states of `hmp catalog reindex`. A list in a cell is joined with `;` and a mapping is written `key=value`, so a cell is always one line.

## What is promised

Inside a major version a field keeps its name and its meaning. A new field can come in a minor version, so a reader ignores what it does not know. When a field has to change or leave, the number in `schema` goes up and the rules of Versions and stability apply. A command marked experimental below follows the experimental rule of that page. A row marked open can hold more columns than the ones listed: the columns of a query, a metric the command was asked to rank by.

## When a command fails

A command that fails ends with the code of Exit codes and prints its `HMPY.Exxx` first on a line of stderr. Under `--format json`, stdout also holds an envelope of its own, unless the command had a result to write:

```
{"schema": "hmp.error.v1", "data": {"code": "HMPY.E002", "title": "...", "detail": "...", "exit_code": 10}}
```

A mistake on the command line itself, such as a flag that does not exist, is found before `--format` is read, so it only has its line on stderr and exit code 2.

A command that reports a result and a failure writes both: `hmp doctor` lists its checks and exits 1 when one is `KO`, `hmp publish --verify` lists its differences and exits 1.

## What each command writes

The commands that are not listed print a document that is the result itself, and an envelope would break it: `hmp config template`, `hmp config resolve`, `hmp config schema`, `hmp config wizard` and `hmp completion`.

The JSON Schema of the result of `hmp calibrate` ships as `hydromodpy/schema/results/calibrate.v1.json`.

| Command | `schema` | `data` | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hmp run` | `hmp.run.v1` | object | `workflow`, `config`, `dry_run`, `result` |
| `hmp replay` | `hmp.replay.v1` | object | `ref`, `source`, `sim_id`, `name`, `rel_dir`, `class`, `basis`, `differs`, `added`, `removed`, `changes`, `strict` |
| `hmp calibrate` | `hmp.calibrate.v1` | object, experimental | `session_id`, `method`, `status`, `n_trials`, `best_cost`, `duration_s`, `save_runs`, `promoted`, `best_cases`, `best_sim_id`, `best_rel_dir`, `cost_name`, `cost_label`, `best_trial`, `best_parameters`, `windows`, `parameter_uncertainty`, `cost_block_fractions`, `workspace`, `session_dir`, `phases`, `frozen`, `reused_from_disk`, `restart_spreads`, `steady_window`, `protocol`, `methods_paragraph`, `methods_path`, `extra` |
| `hmp calibrate --list-phases, --expand` | `hmp.calibrate.phases.v1` | object, experimental | `protocol`, `phases`, `calibration` |
| `hmp calibrate --dry-run` | `hmp.calibrate.plan.v1` | object, experimental | `case`, `session_dir`, `run_dir`, `save_runs`, `phases`, `solves_in_parallel` |
| `hmp spinup` | `hmp.spinup.v1` | object | `applied`, `converged`, `n_cycles`, `cycles`, `restart_from`, `warning`, `production_sim_id` |
| `hmp export` | `hmp.export.v1` | object | `files`, `regenerated` |
| `hmp export --list` | `hmp.export.list.v1` | rows | `name`, `kind` |
| `hmp export deliver` | `hmp.export.deliver.v1` | object | `deliveries` |
| `hmp publish` | `hmp.publish.v1` | object | `applied`, `copies`, `left_out`, `package`, `next` |
| `hmp publish --verify` | `hmp.publish.verify.v1` | object | `copy`, `members`, `problems` |
| `hmp workspace init` | `hmp.workspace.init.v1` | object | `path`, `workspace_toml` |
| `hmp workspace list` | `hmp.workspace.list.v1` | rows | `project`, `name`, `site`, `solver`, `nse`, `created_at`, `sim_id` |
| `hmp workspace clean` | `hmp.workspace.clean.v1` | object | `workspace`, `applied`, `results`, `indexes`, `caches` |
| `hmp project new` | `hmp.project.new.v1` | object | `path` |
| `hmp project plan` | `hmp.project.plan.v1` | object | `plan_hash`, `path`, `n_cases`, `n_sites`, `n_recipes`, `n_sealed` |
| `hmp project log` | `hmp.project.log.v1` | rows, open | `at`, `event`, `case_id`, `status`, `exit_code`, `signal`, `rel_dir`, `error`, `log`, `log_tail` |
| `hmp project list` | `hmp.project.list.v1` | rows | `name`, `path`, `has_project_toml`, `run_tomls` |

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/privacy.html -->
# `hmp privacy`

```
$ hmp privacy [-h] <action> ...
```

Remove a run for good with a purge certificate, and verify one

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp privacy purge` | Remove a run for good (its name stays taken) and write a JSON purge certificate |
| `hmp privacy verify` | Verify a purge certificate JSON |

## `hmp privacy purge`

```
$ hmp privacy purge [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--reason REASON] [--archive-pii] sim_ref
```

Remove a run for good (its name stays taken) and write a JSON purge certificate

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sim_ref` | Run directory name, rel_dir, sim_id or unique prefix |
| `--reason``REASON` | Free-form reason recorded in the certificate default `'unspecified'` |
| `--archive-pii` | Also write the snapshot to a sibling 0o600 archive |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--yes``--dry-run``--format`.

Example

```
$ hmp privacy purge ab12cd34 --reason "data withdrawn" -y
```

## `hmp privacy verify`

```
$ hmp privacy verify [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--strict] certificate
```

Verify a purge certificate JSON

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `certificate` | Path to a purge certificate JSON file |
| `--strict` | Require POSIX 0o600 permissions |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format`.

Example

```
$ hmp privacy verify purge-certificate.json --strict
```

# `hmp project`

```
$ hmp project [-h] <action> ...
```

Manage the projects of a workspace and plan a [sites] project

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp project new` | Create a new project inside the workspace |
| `hmp project plan` | Write the plan of a [sites] project: every site crossed with every recipe |
| `hmp project log` | Print the journal of the latest launch (--failed: one line per failed case) |
| `hmp project delete` | Delete a project directory: its configs, runs, sessions and trash |
| `hmp project list` | List projects available in a workspace |
| `hmp project import` | Install a package written by 'hmp publish --package' as a project of the workspace |

## `hmp project new`

```
$ hmp project new [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] project
```

Create a new project inside the workspace

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | Project name (under projects/) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Example

```
$ hmp project new my_project -w ~/hydromodpy
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp project plan`

```
$ hmp project plan [-h] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [-w WORKSPACE] [--recipe FILE] [--set PATH=VALUE] [--force] [project]
```

Write the plan of a [sites] project: every site crossed with every recipe

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | Project folder or its project.toml (default: -w, else the current directory) |
| `--recipe``FILE` | Plan one recipe file alone on every site, instead of project.toml |
| `--set``PATH=VALUE` | Dotted override rendered into every case. Repeatable. The grammar of a key path and a value |
| `--force` | Go past the running case: write the plan while a case of the current plan runs |

Also takes the shared options `--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--workspace`.

Examples

```
$ hmp project plan .
$ hmp project plan . --recipe calage.toml
$ hmp project plan . --set flow.param.K.field.value=2e-5
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 14. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.

Print the journal of the latest launch (--failed: one line per failed case)

| Argument | What it does |

Also takes the shared options `--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--workspace`.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/publish.html -->
# `hmp publish`

Uses hmp.publish().

```
$ hmp publish [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--to TO] [--container {dir,tar}] [--package] [--without {results,inputs}] [--with {results,inputs,runs,sessions,mesh,fetched}] [--public] [--verify DEST] [REF]
```

Copy a run, the summary or the project out of the tree, with PUBLICATION.json

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `REF` | A run (name, id or @-selector), 'summary', or '.' for the whole project. With --package, a project name or a path (default: the project of -w or of the cwd) |
| `--to``TO` | Destination: a new directory, or a .tar file |
| `--container``CONTAINER` | Write a directory or a tar archive (default: dir, tar with --package) one of `dir` | `tar` |
| `--package` | Write the project with its data in one package, which 'hmp project import' installs |
| `--without``WITHOUT` | Leave 'results' (fields.zarr, tables.parquet, final_state/) or 'inputs' (every file the run read, with INSTALL.toml) out of a copy; repeatable. A copy takes both by default one of `results` | `inputs` |
| `--with``WITH_` | With --package only: take along 'runs' (the sealed runs with their results), 'sessions', 'mesh' (the mesh products the runs cite) or 'fetched' (the files a provider delivered to the runs); repeatable one of `results` | `inputs` | `runs` | `sessions` | `mesh` | `fetched` |
| `--public` | Mark the copy public. Warn when the project declares no [publication] license or an input has no known licence. |
| `--verify``DEST` | Compare a published copy with its PUBLICATION.json and write nothing |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp publish calibration --to ~/deliverables/my_catchment
$ hmp publish baseline_monthly --to baseline.tar --container tar
$ hmp publish baseline_monthly --to light --without results
$ hmp publish . --to /srv/deliverables/bretagne --public
$ hmp publish my_catchment --package --to my_catchment.tar --with runs --with mesh
$ hmp publish --verify ~/deliverables/my_catchment
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 1 2 10. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/replay.html -->
# `hmp replay`

Uses hmp.replay().

```
$ hmp replay [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--strict] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] REF
```

Play a sealed run or a published copy again, and class the values it computes

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `REF` | A sealed run directory or its config.toml, a bare run name under runs/ when -w is given, or a published copy. |
| `--strict` | Refuse a value that does not reproduce the source, before the seal. The attempt keeps its fields and tables, sealed as neither. |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

The new run keeps the name of its source and takes the next version; its seal carries lineage.replay, with the class, the keys that moved and the build drift. A moved input is refused before anything runs.

Examples

```
$ hmp replay runs/baseline_v2
$ hmp replay copies/baseline --strict -w .
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/run.html -->
# `hmp run`

Uses hmp.check(), hmp.run().

```
$ hmp run [-h] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--profile [HTML_PATH]] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [-w WORKSPACE] [--base DIR] [--resume [REF]] [--from STEP] [--until STEP] [--dry-run] [--frozen] [--force] [--only WHAT] [--site SITE] [--parallel N] [--fresh] [--case NAME] [--no-display] [--overlay OVERLAY] [--set PATH=VALUE] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] [config]
```

Run a workflow from a TOML config or a JSON run request

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | Path to a TOML config or to a JSON run request (omit when using --resume REF) |
| `--base``DIR` | The folder the relative paths of the configuration are read from, and the project the run is written in. It wins over -w and over the project root above the file. |
| `--resume``[REF]` | Continue an interrupted case in place, from the journal of its directory. With a TOML config, REF is the case name to continue (bare: the case the file names), or <chain>_w<N> for one window of a chain (island_w3); without a config, REF is the case name and the run replays its own runs/<name>/config.toml. A calibration takes a bare --resume and reopens the latest session of its case. On a [sites] project, bare --resume starts only the cases with an unfinished attempt. |
| `--from``STEP` | Start from this pipeline step, by its name. |
| `--until``STEP` | Stop after this pipeline step, by its name. On a [sites] project, --until data stops after the prepare phase. |
| `--dry-run` | Print the resolved workflow plan without executing it. |
| `--frozen` | On a project TOML, reject any fresh download: every file must already be in the data cache and match hydromodpy.lock. The config.toml of a sealed run is refused: hmp replay plays a run again. |
| `--force` | Go past what the command refuses because of what is there: recompute when a completed run with an identical resolved config and the same name already exists, and claim a stale case whose process cannot be proven dead. Without it an identical run is not recomputed: the command stops and names it. A calibration searches again instead of giving back its completed session. Not for an overview. On a [sites] project it also lifts the budget ceilings (parallel, prepare_parallel, calibrations, cores), takes over the lease of a launcher still alive and plans over a running case. |
| `--only``WHAT` | [sites] project: start only these cases, named by status (failed, stale, partial, aborted, planned, completed) or by case id (shell patterns allowed). Repeatable, or comma separated. |
| `--site``SITE` | [sites] project: start only the cases of this site. |
| `--parallel``N` | [sites] project: solves side by side, a calibration counting its own [calibration] parallel. Defaults to [sites.run] parallel. |
| `--fresh` | Start the case over: everything the previous attempt left in runs/<case>/ is filed under attempts/<k>/ first. Without it a retry resumes in place. |
| `--case``NAME` | Name of the run. Defaults to [simulation] name, else the stem of the TOML. A run launched with --set or --overlay keeps that name; use --case to name the variant. |
| `--no-display` | Skip auto-rendering of the figures listed in [display].figures. |

Also takes the shared options `--format``--profile``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--workspace``--overlay``--set``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp run run.toml
$ hmp run run.toml --dry-run
$ hmp run run.toml --set flow.param.K.field.value=2e-5
$ hmp run run.toml --overlay daily.toml --case baseline_daily
$ hmp run run.toml --from setup_process --until run_solver
$ hmp run --resume baseline_monthly
$ hmp run run.toml --fresh
$ hmp run request.json --base /project
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10 14 21 23 130. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/show.html -->
# `hmp show`

Uses hmp.show(), hmp.open().

```
$ hmp show [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--profile | --point | --rank METRIC | --figure NAME | --report | --table NAME] [--detail] [--to FILE] [--var NAME] [--xy X Y | --cell CELL] [--layer LAYER | --depth METERS] [--label LABEL] [--timestep TIMESTEP] [-n LIMIT] [--worst] [--mixed-windows] [--time TIME] [--opt NAME=VALUE] [--engine {static,interactive}] [--data DIR] [--overview RUN] [--preset {research,management}] [--station ID] [--strict] [--open] [REF ...]
```

Show a run, a session or a project: summary, profile, point, rank, figure, report

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `REF` | A run (directory, name, sim_id prefix or @-selector), a session, or '.' for the project. Several runs are read by --point only. Default: the project. |
| `--profile` | Print where the time went, not the summary |
| `--point` | Read variables in one cell (--var, then --xy or --cell) |
| `--rank``METRIC` | Rank the runs of the project by METRIC, best first (-n, --worst) |
| `--figure``NAME` | Draw one figure: a name 'hmp config figures' lists, a registered variable or a preset |
| `--report` | Write the report of a run or of a session |
| `--table``NAME` | Print one sealed table |
| `--detail` | With the summary of a run, print the facts of the index and the Zarr layout |
| `--to``FILE` | Write the figure, the point table or the sealed table here |
| `--var``NAME` | Field to read, persisted or virtual. Repeat for several fields. |
| `--xy``X Y` | Coordinates in the simulation CRS |
| `--cell``CELL` | Zero-based cell index |
| `--layer``LAYER` | Zero-based layer index |
| `--depth``METERS` | Depth below the local model top |
| `--label``LABEL` | Name of the point reported in the table |
| `--timestep``TIMESTEP` | Keep a single timestep (negative counts from the end) |
| `-n`, `--limit``LIMIT` | Rows to show (default: 1) |
| `--worst` | The worst runs, not the best |
| `--mixed-windows` | Rank scores computed on different windows, stations or rule versions together |
| `--time``TIME` | Instant a map draws: a date (2002-10-15), "first" or "last" |
| `--opt``NAME=VALUE` | Request field of a variable or a preset, repeatable (station, layer, scale): a TOML value (false, 12, [8, 4], "text") or bare text |
| `--engine``ENGINE` | Engine of a variable or a preset figure (default: its own) one of `static` | `interactive` |
| `--data``DIR` | Write the tables behind a variable or a preset figure to DIR, one <stem>_<key>.csv each, and draw nothing |
| `--overview``RUN` | The sealed overview of the site. Default: the overview of the same site. |
| `--preset``PRESET` | research writes report/ with three levels, management a one-page sheet one of `research` | `management` |
| `--station``ID` | Station of the report series and metrics, or of the ranking (default: the gauge) |
| `--strict` | Fail when the report misses a figure it requires, once it is written |
| `--open` | Open the report in the default browser once it is written |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug`.

Examples

```
$ hmp show base_v2
$ hmp show calage --format json
$ hmp show base_v2 --profile
$ hmp show base_v2 --figure watertable_depth_map --time 2002-10-15 --to map.png
$ hmp show run_a run_b --point --var head --cell 5000 --to point.csv
$ hmp show . --rank nse -n 5
$ hmp show base_v2 --report --preset management
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10 14. An exception it does not catch ends with the code of its class. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/site.html -->
# `hmp site`

```
$ hmp site [-h] <action> ...
```

Declare the sites of a workspace

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp site add` | Declare one site in data/sites/catalog.csv |
| `hmp site import` | Declare sites from a table, a vector layer or Hub'Eau stations |
| `hmp site ls` | List the sites declared in data/sites/catalog.csv |
| `hmp site show` | Print one site of data/sites/catalog.csv |

## `hmp site add`

```
$ hmp site add [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--outlet X Y] [--crs CRS] [--label LABEL] [--gauge GAUGE] [--uri URI] [--tag TAG] [--force] name
```

Declare one site in data/sites/catalog.csv

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Site name: letters, digits and underscores |
| `--outlet``X Y` | Outlet coordinates in --crs |
| `--crs``CRS` | CRS of the outlet (default: EPSG:2154) |
| `--label``LABEL` | Readable name of the catchment |
| `--gauge``GAUGE` | Station that measures the catchment |
| `--uri``URI` | hubeau:<code> or bdtopage:<code> |
| `--tag``TAG` | Tag of the site; repeat for several |
| `--force` | Go past the refusal: replace a site of the same name, accept an outlet close to another |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format`.

Example

```
$ hmp site add couesnon --outlet 377120 6831410 --gauge J017000001 --uri hubeau:J0170000
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14. All exit codes.

## `hmp site import`

```
$ hmp site import [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--hubeau] [--layer LAYER] [--bbox XMIN YMIN XMAX YMAX] [--crs CRS] [--min-years MIN_YEARS] [--snap-network SNAP_NETWORK] [--snap-max-m SNAP_MAX_M] [--name-field NAME_FIELD] [--gauge-field GAUGE_FIELD] [--label-field LABEL_FIELD] [--layer-name LAYER_NAME] [--tag TAG] [--force] [table]
```

Declare sites from a table, a vector layer or Hub'Eau stations

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `table` | CSV site table in the columns site, label, gauge, uri, x_outlet, y_outlet, crs, tags |
| `--hubeau` | Hub'Eau discharge stations inside --bbox |
| `--layer``LAYER` | Vector layer of outlet points |
| `--bbox``XMIN YMIN XMAX YMAX` | Box searched, in --crs |
| `--crs``CRS` | CRS of the box and of the outlets (default: EPSG:2154) |
| `--min-years``MIN_YEARS` | Keep stations open at least this many years (opening to closing, or today) |
| `--snap-network``SNAP_NETWORK` | Snap each outlet onto this river network: a vector file, or bdtopage |
| `--snap-max-m``SNAP_MAX_M` | Farthest snap in meters; a station farther away is skipped (default: 200) |
| `--name-field``NAME_FIELD` | Field holding the site name |
| `--gauge-field``GAUGE_FIELD` | Field holding the station code |
| `--label-field``LABEL_FIELD` | Field holding the readable name |
| `--layer-name``LAYER_NAME` | Layer of a multi-layer file |
| `--tag``TAG` | Tag added to every site; repeat for several |
| `--force` | Go past the refusal: replace sites of the same name, accept outlets close to others |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format`.

Examples

```
$ hmp site import stations.csv --tag bretagne
$ hmp site import --hubeau --bbox 150000 6700000 420000 6900000 --min-years 10
$ hmp site import --layer exutoires.gpkg --name-field code --gauge-field station
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 2 10. All exit codes.

# `hmp spinup`

Uses hmp.spinup().

```
$ hmp spinup [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--profile [HTML_PATH]] [--verbosity {quiet,normal,verbose,debug} | -q | -v | --debug] [--then-run] [--credentials PATH] [--allow-host HOST] [--max-download-bytes N] config
```

Cyclic spin-up: restart each cycle until heads and lake stage converge

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | Path to a simulation TOML file |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format``--profile``--verbosity``--quiet``--verbose``--debug``--credentials``--allow-host``--max-download-bytes`.

Examples

```
$ hmp spinup run.toml

```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14. All exit codes.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/workspace.html -->
# `hmp workspace`

```
$ hmp workspace [-h] <action> ...
```

Scaffold, list and clean a workspace

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `hmp workspace init` | Scaffold a HydroModPy workspace (data + projects). Default: ~/hydromodpy/ |
| `hmp workspace list` | List the sealed runs of every project under a workspace, from their directories |
| `hmp workspace clean` | Trash the results of a workspace and remove its rebuildable caches |

## `hmp workspace init`

```
$ hmp workspace init [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--force] [--project-name PROJECT_NAME] [--creator-name CREATOR_NAME] [--creator-email CREATOR_EMAIL] [path]
```

Scaffold a HydroModPy workspace (data + projects). Default: ~/hydromodpy/

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Workspace path, or give it with -w |
| `--force` | Go past the refusal: reuse a workspace that exists |
| `--project-name``PROJECT_NAME` | Project name written to workspace.toml (default: the workspace folder name) |
| `--creator-name``CREATOR_NAME` | Creator name written to workspace.toml |
| `--creator-email``CREATOR_EMAIL` | Creator e-mail written to workspace.toml |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format`.

Examples

```
$ hmp workspace init ~/hydromodpy
$ hmp workspace init ./ws --project-name my_project
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 14. All exit codes.

## `hmp workspace list`

```
$ hmp workspace list [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [--format {table,json,csv}] [path]
```

List the sealed runs of every project under a workspace, from their directories

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | Workspace or project root (default: -w, else the current directory) |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--format`.

Examples

```
$ hmp workspace list
$ hmp workspace list ~/hydromodpy --format json
$ hmp workspace list -w ~/hydromodpy/projects/demo
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10. All exit codes.

## `hmp workspace clean`

```
$ hmp workspace clean [-h] [-w WORKSPACE] [-y] [--dry-run] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--all] [--results] [--data-cache] [--runtime] [--scratch] [--force]
```

Trash the results of a workspace and remove its rebuildable caches

| Argument | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | Carry the plan out. Without it the verb prints the plan and changes nothing |
| `--all` | Clean every group below |
| `--results` | Move every run and session to the trash of its project, remove the index |
| `--data-cache` | data/blobs and the data cache database that a pre-release left in data/ |
| `--runtime` | The .hmp/ runtime folder |
| `--scratch` | The scratch folders (.hmp/scratch) |
| `--force` | With --results: go past the pin and the stale attempt, and trash those runs too |

Also takes the shared options `--workspace``--dry-run``--format`.

Examples

```
$ hmp workspace clean --results --dry-run
$ hmp workspace clean --all -y
```

Exit codes it sets itself: 10 14. All exit codes.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/data-sources.html -->
# Data sources

Every data section of the file, and the sources its `source` key accepts, with who publishes each one and under which licence. Read from the configuration models and from the source registry of the code (`hydromodpy.schema.sources`), which carries one entry per source. A field added to an entry shows up here on its own.

A source marked “licence not determined” has no licence recorded in the code. The reason sits in the details of the source, and a run that reads it does not claim a licence for its outputs.

The keys that declare the data of a project are in [data]. A new provider is added by registering a source: Add a data source.

By section

| Section | Accepted values of `source` |
| --- | --- |
| `[data.crossings]` |
- `file`: built or read locally · licence not determined User-provided crossings file (SHP/GPKG/GeoJSON). Details
  - Why this licence A file the user supplied. Its licence is the user's to declare, in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
- `url`: built or read locally · licence not determined Remote crossings file, pinned by its sha256 when `https` is not used. Details
  - Why this licence A remote file downloaded by URL. Its licence is declared by the user in the 'license' key of the section or sidecar.
- `bdtopo`: downloads from `data.geopf.fr` · IGN · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Roads and railways of the IGN BD TOPO, from the Geoplateforme WFS. Details
  - Attribution Source: IGN, BD TOPO roads and railways
  - Hosts contacted `data.geopf.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-topo-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/bd-topo-r, https://cartes.gouv.fr/cgu
  - Coverage Metropolitan France and several overseas territories. The adapter reads the road and railway layers over a box in EPSG:2154.
  - Resolution 3D vector objects of metric precision.
  - Period Editions from 2008-03-18 to 2026-09-15; the code pins no edition.
  - Update Quarterly editions, with a weekly BDTOPO Express edition since May 2025.
  - Authentication None sent by the adapter.
  - Limits cartes.gouv.fr terms: WFS 30 requests/s, WMS-Raster 40 requests/s, download 5 requests per 5 s with a 5 minute ban; over the limit the service answers 429.
  - Cache folder: data/crossings, pattern: crossings_bdtopo_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: crossings_bdtopo_<bbox hash>.gpkg. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence IGN, publishing on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation, gives BD TOPO the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'. The WFS capabilities point to the cartes.gouv.fr terms and state 'Fees: none'.
- `roe`: downloads from `services.sandre.eaufrance.fr` · Sandre / OFB · licence etalab-2.0 assumed Obstacles to flow of the Sandre ROE (dams, weirs, bridge sills), from the Sandre WFS. Details
  - Attribution Source: Sandre (OFB), ROE obstacles to flow
  - Hosts contacted `services.sandre.eaufrance.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.sandre.eaufrance.fr/atlas/srv/api/records/070df464-73d3-4c00-be2f-93f2a97ef8f5
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://www.sandre.eaufrance.fr/atlas/srv/api/records/070df464-73d3-4c00-be2f-93f2a97ef8f5, https://services.sandre.eaufrance.fr/geo/obs?SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=2.0.0&REQUEST=GetCapabilities
  - Coverage Metropolitan France (layer sa:ObstEcoul_FXX), one point per obstacle.
  - Resolution Points, equivalent scale 1:50 000.
  - Period The record gives no temporal extent; it was revised on 2026-10-08 at the check.
  - Update Weekly.
  - Authentication None: free access.
  - Cache folder: data/crossings, pattern: crossings_roe_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: crossings_roe_<bbox hash>.gpkg. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence The Sandre atlas record 'Obstacles à l'écoulement - Métropole' lists 'Licence Ouverte Etalab' as its use limitation and 'Pas de restriction d'accès public'. The WFS capabilities state 'Fees: no conditions apply'.
 |
| `[data.curve_number]` |
- `file`: built or read locally · licence not determined User-provided raster of the SCS curve number (GeoTIFF/ASC), AMC II, such as GCN250. Details
  - Why this licence A file the user supplied. Its licence is the user's to declare, in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
- `url`: built or read locally · licence not determined Remote curve number raster, downloaded into the data cache by the `url` source. Details
  - Why this licence A remote file downloaded by URL. Its licence is declared by the user in the 'license' key of the section or sidecar.
- `land_cover`: built or read locally · licence not determined A land cover raster of a named legend, turned into the curve number. Details
  - Why this licence A land cover raster the user supplied, turned into a curve number with the GCN250 table (Jaafar et al. 2019, CC BY 4.0). The licence of the raster is the user's to declare in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
- `worldcover`: downloads from `esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com` · ESA WorldCover consortium (VITO) · licence CC-BY-4.0 assumed ESA WorldCover, its classes sent to the ESA CCI pivot, 10 m over the world. Details
  - Attribution ESA WorldCover project / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data processed by ESA WorldCover consortium
  - Hosts contacted `esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com`
  - Licence pages https://raw.githubusercontent.com/awslabs/open-data-registry/main/datasets/esa-worldcover-vito.yaml, https://esa-worldcover.s3.amazonaws.com/readme.html
  - Licence checked 2026-11-21
  - Facts pages https://raw.githubusercontent.com/awslabs/open-data-registry/main/datasets/esa-worldcover-vito.yaml
  - Coverage The world, in tiles of 3 by 3 degrees.
  - Resolution Raster land cover at 10 m in EPSG:4326, eleven classes; the adapters read class 50, built-up, as sealed, or send every class to the ESA CCI legend for its GCN250 curve number.
  - Period Two maps, 2020 (algorithm v100) and 2021 (v200).
  - Update Yearly in the registry entry; two maps published so far.
  - Authentication None: the adapter reads the window of its box from the public bucket.
  - Cache folder: data/impervious, pattern: impervious_worldcover_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: impervious_worldcover_<year>_<hash>.tif. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/curve_number, pattern: curve_number_worldcover_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: curve_number_worldcover_<year>_<hash>.tif, the GCN250 curve number of one request, soil group and class table. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence The Registry of Open Data on AWS entry of ESA WorldCover, maintained by VITO, gives 'License: CC-BY 4.0'; the bucket readme gives the attribution text.
- `ocsge`: downloads from `data.geopf.fr` · IGN · licence etalab-2.0 assumed OCS GE of the IGN, its covers sent to the ESA CCI pivot, 10 m, France. Details
  - Attribution Source: IGN, OCS GE
  - Hosts contacted `data.geopf.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/ocs-ge
  - Licence checked 2026-11-21
  - Facts pages https://data.geopf.fr/telechargement/resource/OCSGE, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/ocs-ge
  - Coverage France, one archive per department and edition; 98 departments listed by the download service on 2026-11-21, with 2.0 editions from 2017 onwards.
  - Resolution Vector land cover at large scale; the adapter burns on a 10 m grid in EPSG:2154 either the covers CS1.1.1.1 (built) and CS1.1.1.2 (unbuilt sealed) as the sealed share, or the infiltration ratio the section writes for each other cover.
  - Period One edition per department every three years or so, named by its year.
  - Update Departments are delivered edition by edition; the year is pinned in the config.
  - Authentication None: the adapter fetches each department archive by plain HTTP.
  - Cache folder: data/impervious, pattern: impervious_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: impervious_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m sealed share of one request. The department archives (about 200 MB each) stay once per machine in the ocsge folder of the HydroModPy user cache, shared by every family and project. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/infiltration_ratio, pattern: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m ratio of one request and one table of ratios; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/curve_number, pattern: curve_number_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: curve_number_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m GCN250 curve number of one request, soil group and class table; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence IGN publishes the dataset 'OCS GE' on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation with the licence 'lov2', the Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0. The metadata shipped in each archive set no use constraint ('Aucune contrainte, ouvert a tous').
 |
| `[data.dem]` |

  - Why this licence IGN, publishing on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation, gives BD ALTI the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'. The cartes.gouv.fr terms add that a Geoplateforme dataset without another licence falls under the Licence Ouverte Etalab.

  - Licence checked 2026-10-09

  - Coverage Metropolitan and overseas France except French Polynesia, New Caledonia and Wallis and Futuna. It holds nodata over the zones closed to aerial capture. The adapter takes a box in EPSG:2154.

  - Cache folder: data/dem/processed, pattern: dem_ign_geoplateforme_rgealti_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: dem_ign_geoplateforme_rgealti_<resolution>_<hash>.tif is one request.
  - Why this licence IGN, publishing on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation, gives RGE ALTI the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'. The cartes.gouv.fr terms add that a Geoplateforme dataset without another licence falls under the Licence Ouverte Etalab.
