| `[data.geology]` |
- `file`: built or read locally · licence not determined User-provided geology file (SHP/GPKG/TIF/CSV). Details
  - Why this licence A file the user supplied. Its licence is the user's to declare, in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
- `url`: built or read locally · licence not determined Remote geology file, pinned by its sha256 when `https` is not used. Details
  - Why this licence A remote file downloaded by URL. Its licence is declared by the user in the 'license' key of the section or sidecar.
- `brgm_1m`: downloads from `infoterre.brgm.fr` · BRGM · licence etalab-2.0 assumed BRGM 1:1M national geological map (CODE_LEG legend). Details
  - Attribution Source: BRGM, 1:1M geological map of France
  - Hosts contacted `infoterre.brgm.fr`
  - Licence pages https://infoterre.brgm.fr/page/conditions-dutilisation-donnees, https://infoterre.brgm.fr/formulaire/telechargement-carte-geologique-metropolitaine-11-000-000
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://infoterre.brgm.fr/formulaire/telechargement-carte-geologique-metropolitaine-11-000-000
  - Coverage Metropolitan France.
  - Resolution Vector map at 1:1 000 000, 6th revised edition, six information layers.
  - Period One edition of a map, not a time series.
  - Authentication None: the adapter fetches the archive by plain HTTP.
  - Cache folder: data/geology, pattern: geology_brgm_1m_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: geology_brgm_1m_france.gpkg is the whole country, built once from the archive FR_vecteur.zip kept beside it; geology_brgm_1m_<bbox hash>.gpkg is the crop of one request. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence BRGM states on InfoTerre: 'Les Données disponibles sur le site InfoTerre sont soumises à la licence Ouverte / Open Licence Etalab Version 2.0', unless an exception is shown, with the source (BRGM) and the date of last update to cite and the data not to be altered. The 1:1M download form points to those terms and links the archive the adapter fetches (data/variables/geology/apis/brgm_1m.py).
- `brgm_50k`: downloads from `infoterre.brgm.fr` · BRGM · licence etalab-2.0 assumed BRGM 1:50K departmental geological map (CODE_LEG legend). Details
  - Attribution Source: BRGM, BD Charm-50 harmonised geological map
  - Hosts contacted `infoterre.brgm.fr`
  - Licence pages https://infoterre.brgm.fr/page/conditions-dutilisation-donnees, https://infoterre.brgm.fr/formulaire/telechargement-cartes-geologiques-departementales-150-000-bd-charm-50
  - Licence checked 2026-10-09
  - Facts pages https://infoterre.brgm.fr/formulaire/telechargement-cartes-geologiques-departementales-150-000-bd-charm-50
  - Coverage Metropolitan France: 95 departments available, one archive each.
  - Resolution Vector, harmonised departmental maps at 1:50 000, six information layers; the adapter reads the S_FGEOL layer in EPSG:2154.
  - Period One edition of a map, not a time series.
  - Update The BRGM download page was last updated on 2021-05-06.
  - Authentication None: the adapter fetches each department archive by plain HTTP.
  - Cache folder: data/geology, pattern: geology_brgm_50k_*.gpkg, format: GeoPackage, note: geology_brgm_50k_<bbox hash>.gpkg is the merged crop of one request. The departments it was built from stay in departments_50k/ (GEO050K_HARM_<code>.zip and one GeoPackage per department). Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence BRGM states on InfoTerre: 'Les Données disponibles sur le site InfoTerre sont soumises à la licence Ouverte / Open Licence Etalab Version 2.0', unless an exception is shown, with the source (BRGM) and the date of last update to cite and the data not to be altered. The BD Charm-50 download form points to those terms.

| `[data.impervious]` |
- `file`: built or read locally · licence not determined User-provided raster of the sealed share (GeoTIFF/ASC), 0 to 1 per pixel. Details
  - Why this licence A file the user supplied. Its licence is the user's to declare, in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
- `url`: built or read locally · licence not determined Remote raster of the sealed share, downloaded into the data cache by the `url` source. Details
  - Why this licence A remote file downloaded by URL. Its licence is declared by the user in the 'license' key of the section or sidecar.
- `ocsge`: downloads from `data.geopf.fr` · IGN · licence etalab-2.0 assumed OCS GE of the IGN, its built and unbuilt sealed covers rasterized at 10 m. Details
  - Attribution Source: IGN, OCS GE
  - Hosts contacted `data.geopf.fr`
  - Licence pages https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/ocs-ge
  - Licence checked 2026-11-21
  - Facts pages https://data.geopf.fr/telechargement/resource/OCSGE, https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/ocs-ge
  - Coverage France, one archive per department and edition; 98 departments listed by the download service on 2026-11-21, with 2.0 editions from 2017 onwards.
  - Resolution Vector land cover at large scale; the adapter burns on a 10 m grid in EPSG:2154 either the covers CS1.1.1.1 (built) and CS1.1.1.2 (unbuilt sealed) as the sealed share, or the infiltration ratio the section writes for each other cover.
  - Period One edition per department every three years or so, named by its year.
  - Update Departments are delivered edition by edition; the year is pinned in the config.
  - Authentication None: the adapter fetches each department archive by plain HTTP.
  - Cache folder: data/impervious, pattern: impervious_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: impervious_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m sealed share of one request. The department archives (about 200 MB each) stay once per machine in the ocsge folder of the HydroModPy user cache, shared by every family and project. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/infiltration_ratio, pattern: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m ratio of one request and one table of ratios; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/curve_number, pattern: curve_number_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: curve_number_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m GCN250 curve number of one request, soil group and class table; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence IGN publishes the dataset 'OCS GE' on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation with the licence 'lov2', the Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0. The metadata shipped in each archive set no use constraint ('Aucune contrainte, ouvert a tous').
- `worldcover`: downloads from `esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com` · ESA WorldCover consortium (VITO) · licence CC-BY-4.0 assumed ESA WorldCover, its built-up class read as sealed, 10 m over the world. Details
  - Attribution ESA WorldCover project / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data processed by ESA WorldCover consortium
  - Hosts contacted `esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com`
  - Licence pages https://raw.githubusercontent.com/awslabs/open-data-registry/main/datasets/esa-worldcover-vito.yaml, https://esa-worldcover.s3.amazonaws.com/readme.html
  - Licence checked 2026-11-21
  - Facts pages https://raw.githubusercontent.com/awslabs/open-data-registry/main/datasets/esa-worldcover-vito.yaml
  - Coverage The world, in tiles of 3 by 3 degrees.
  - Resolution Raster land cover at 10 m in EPSG:4326, eleven classes; the adapters read class 50, built-up, as sealed, or send every class to the ESA CCI legend for its GCN250 curve number.
  - Period Two maps, 2020 (algorithm v100) and 2021 (v200).
  - Update Yearly in the registry entry; two maps published so far.
  - Authentication None: the adapter reads the window of its box from the public bucket.
  - Cache folder: data/impervious, pattern: impervious_worldcover_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: impervious_worldcover_<year>_<hash>.tif. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/curve_number, pattern: curve_number_worldcover_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: curve_number_worldcover_<year>_<hash>.tif, the GCN250 curve number of one request, soil group and class table. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence The Registry of Open Data on AWS entry of ESA WorldCover, maintained by VITO, gives 'License: CC-BY 4.0'; the bucket readme gives the attribution text.

  - Cache folder: data/impervious, pattern: impervious_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: impervious_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m sealed share of one request. The department archives (about 200 MB each) stay once per machine in the ocsge folder of the HydroModPy user cache, shared by every family and project. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/infiltration_ratio, pattern: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: infiltration_ratio_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m ratio of one request and one table of ratios; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence., folder: data/curve_number, pattern: curve_number_ocsge_*.tif, format: GeoTIFF, note: curve_number_ocsge_<year>_<hash>.tif is the 10 m GCN250 curve number of one request, soil group and class table; the sealed covers are nodata. Each file has a sidecar named after it with a '.json' suffix, which holds its source, digest and licence.
  - Why this licence IGN publishes the dataset 'OCS GE' on data.gouv.fr under its own organisation with the licence 'lov2', the Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0. The metadata shipped in each archive set no use constraint ('Aucune contrainte, ouvert a tous').
 |

- Limits Download by stream is limited to 31 days per request; the adapter chunks by 31 days.
- Cache folder: data/oceanic, pattern: sealevel_shom_*.csv, format: CSV, note: sealevel_shom_<gauge id>_<start>_<end>_H.csv, one per gauge and period.
- Why this licence Shom publishes the two REFMAR datasets (the RONIM tide gauges and the partner tide gauges) on data.gouv.fr under the 'Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0'; the service lists gauges of exactly these two networks. The data.shom.fr support page calls the access to the observations free.
 |

### Supplied or generated by the user

| Source | Feeds | Licence | More |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `[data.crossings]``[data.curve_number]``[data.dem]``[data.geology]``[data.impervious]``[data.infiltration_ratio]``[data.lake_abacus]``[data.lake_bathymetry]``[data.lake_geometry]``[data.lake_inflow]``[data.lake_levels]``[data.lake_outflow]``[data.lake_withdrawal]``[data.layer_base]``[data.property_map]``[data.soil_capacity]``[data.substratum]` | licence not determined | Details
- Why this licence A file the user supplied. Its licence is the user's to declare, in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
 |
| `url` | `[data.crossings]``[data.curve_number]``[data.dem]``[data.geology]``[data.impervious]``[data.infiltration_ratio]``[data.lake_abacus]``[data.lake_bathymetry]``[data.lake_geometry]``[data.layer_base]``[data.soil_capacity]``[data.substratum]` | licence not determined | Details
- Why this licence A remote file downloaded by URL. Its licence is declared by the user in the 'license' key of the section or sidecar.
 |
| `land_cover` | `[data.curve_number]` | licence not determined | Details
- Why this licence A land cover raster the user supplied, turned into a curve number with the GCN250 table (Jaafar et al. 2019, CC BY 4.0). The licence of the raster is the user's to declare in the 'license' key of its sidecar.
 |
| `constant` | no section lists it | licence not determined | Details
- Why this licence A value generated from the configuration. Its terms are the author's to choose.
 |
| `synthetic` | no section lists it | licence not determined | Details
- Why this licence A series generated from the configuration. Its terms are the author's to choose.
 |

# Figure requests

Every table on this page is read from the code of the figure path when the site is built. To draw one, see Add a figure.

## Fields

A figure is a request, and a request holds panels.

### Fields of a figure

| Field | Type | Default | What it does | Accepted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `str or none` | `unset` | Name of a shipped preset or of one of your own presets. | `hydrograph`, `residuals`, `water_budget`, `watershed_id_card`, `network_expansion`, `calibration_landscape`, `calibration_progress`, `ensemble_band`, `flow_directions`, `lake_abacus_comparison`, `network_comparison`, `observed_network_heads`, `particle_tracks`, `recharge_estimates`, `recharge_regime`, `recharge_signals`, `parameter_space`, `recession`, `residence_time_distribution`, `root_search`, `sfr_longitudinal_profile`, `water_balance_loop` |
| `panels` | `list[PanelRequest] or none` | `unset` | The panels, in order. | |
| `draw` | `function or none` | `unset` | Python function that draws the figure, draw(subject, ax, theme). Never written in a file. | |
| `name` | `str or none` | `unset` | File name of the figure, no suffix. | |
| `title` | `str or none` | `unset` | Title written above the whole figure. Unset, none is written. | |
| `width` | `str or none` | `unset` | Printed width: 'single', 'medium' or 'double' column. Unset, single for one panel, double for more panels or a facet. | `single (85 mm)`, `medium (120 mm)`, `double (180 mm)` |
| `facet` | `'time' or 'run' or 'variable' or 'layer' or 'parameter' or none` | `unset` | Repeat the one panel over this key. | `time`, `run`, `variable`, `layer`, `parameter` |
| `when` | `str` | `"end"` | When the figure is drawn: 'end', 'session' or 'after:<step>'. | `end`, `session`, `after:<step>`, `with <step> one of prepare_solver, run_solver, extract, derive, export` |
| `engine` | `list[str]` | `["static"]` | Drawing engines to use for the figure, one file per engine. | `static`, `interactive` |
| `formats` | `list[str]` | `["png"]` | File formats written for the figure, such as png or svg. | `png`, `svg`, `pdf` |

### Fields of a panel

| Field | Type | Default | What it does | Accepted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `str or none` | `unset` | Frame of the panel. Unset, the natural frame of the variable. | `map`, `series`, `section`, `xy`, `distribution`, `groups`, `table`, `volume` |
| `variable` | `list[str] or none` | `unset` | Variable name or list. 'budget' is the budget terms the run kept. In a table panel, 'table.column' names. | `budget` |
| `time` | `str or int or list[str or int] or none` | `unset` | A date (YYYY-MM-DD), 'first', 'last', a period index, or a list of them. A date picks the period (start, end] that holds it. On a series, two values keep the periods whose start lies between them. | |
| `layer` | `int or str or none` | `unset` | Layer index from 0 at the top, or 'sum' over the layers. | `sum`, `top` |
| `station` | `str or list[str] or none` | `unset` | A station of the run (lake:1, a reach, a gauge), or zone:catchment, zone:domain. | `zone:catchment`, `zone:domain` |
| `overlays` | `list[str] or none` | `unset` | Context layers drawn over a map or a section, in place of the default ones. A map keeps its relief and its scale bar. | `relief`, `outline`, `network`, `generated_network`, `outlet`, `stations`, `lake`, `barrier`, `wells`, `seepage`, `pathlines`, `scale_bar`, `mesh` |
| `bbox` | `tuple[float, float, float, float] or none` | `unset` | Window drawn (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax). On a map, in m in the mesh CRS. On a section, distances along the line then elevations, in m. | |
| `line` | `list[tuple[float, float]] or none` | `unset` | Trace of a section, points (x, y) in m in the mesh CRS. | |
| `limits` | `tuple[float, float] or none` | `unset` | Colour limits of a map or a section (low, high), in the unit drawn. Unset, the range of the values. | |
| `contours` | `bool or none` | `unset` | Draw isolines. Unset, the quantity decides. | |
| `observed` | `bool` | `false` | Draw the observed record when it exists. | |
| `scores` | `bool` | `false` | Write the scores of the run on the panel. | |
| `scale` | `'linear' or 'log' or none` | `unset` | Value scale. Unset, the variable decides. | `linear`, `log` |
| `stack` | `bool` | `false` | Stack the variables one over the other, in the order given. | |
| `by` | `str or none` | `unset` | Category key of a groups panel. | `month`, `time`, `run` |
| `reference` | `list['one_to_one' or 'zero' or ReferenceValue] or none` | `unset` | Reference lines: 'one_to_one', 'zero', or {value, label}. | `one_to_one`, `zero` |
| `share` | `bool` | `false` | One colour norm for every small multiple. | |
| `reduce` | `'mean' or 'max' or 'frequency' or none` | `unset` | Reduce over time before drawing. Unset, the time asked for is drawn. | `mean`, `max`, `frequency` |
| `change` | `tuple[str or int, str or int] or none` | `unset` | Draw the change between two instants. | |
| `against` | `str or none` | `unset` | Draw the difference to 'observed' or to another run by name. | |
| `cumulative` | `bool` | `false` | Cumulate along the ordered axis of the frame. | |

### Field a panel of a preset adds

| Field | Type | Default | What it does | Accepted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `holes` | `list[str] or none` | `unset` | In a preset, the panel fields a user may give. The value written is the default. | `type`, `variable`, `time`, `layer`, `station`, `overlays`, `bbox`, `line`, `limits`, `contours`, `observed`, `scores`, `scale`, `stack`, `by`, `reference`, `share`, `reduce`, `change`, `against`, `cumulative` |

## Frames

A panel is drawn by one frame.

| Frame | What it draws | Shapes it takes | Overlays by default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `map` | Map frame: one value per mesh cell, drawn as filled polygons in the mesh CRS. | `time_layer_face`, `time_face`, `layer_face`, `face` | `relief`, `outline`, `network`, `outlet`, `scale_bar` |
| `series` | Series frame: values along an ordered axis, the time of a run. | `time` | - |
| `section` | Section frame: a vertical cut through the model along a line, distance against elevation. | `time_layer_face`, `layer_face`, `time_face`, `face` | `seepage` |
| `xy` | XY frame: one variable against another, one point per matched row. | `time`, `time_face`, `time_layer_face`, `layer_face`, `face` | - |
| `distribution` | Distribution frame: the values of one variable against how often they occur. | `time`, `time_face`, `time_layer_face`, `layer_face`, `face` | - |
| `groups` | Groups frame: named categories against a value, as bars or as boxes. | `time`, `time_face`, `time_layer_face`, `layer_face`, `face` | - |
| `table` | Table frame: rows of text, a label and a value for each column a panel names. | - | - |
| `volume` | Volume frame: the block of the model in 3D, coloured by one variable at one instant. | - | - |

## Closed values

These words are the only ones a request accepts for the fields they fill.

| Closed value | Accepted |
| --- | --- |
| engine | `static` png, svg, pdf `interactive` html |
| when | `end``session``after:<step>` prepare_solver, run_solver, extract, derive, export |
| width | `single` 85 mm `medium` 120 mm `double` 180 mm |
| formats | `png``svg``pdf` |
| zone | `zone:catchment``zone:domain` |
| group key | `month``time``run` |
| theme | `default``print``dark` |

## Presets

A preset is a request that lists the fields a user may fill.

| Preset | Width | Panels it expands to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hydrograph` | double |
1. `series` variable = `["recharge"]`, station = `"zone:catchment"` Holes `time`
1. `series` variable = `["discharge"]`, observed = `true`, scores = `true`, scale = `"linear"` Holes `variable`, `station`, `scale`, `time`
 |
| `residuals` | double |
1. `series` variable = `["discharge"]`, scores = `true`, reference = `["zero"]`, against = `"observed"` Holes `variable`, `station`
1. `distribution` variable = `["discharge"]`, against = `"observed"` Holes `variable`, `station`
 |
| `water_budget` | double |
1. `series` variable = `["budget"]`, station = `"zone:catchment"`, stack = `true` Holes `variable`, `station`, `time`
1. `groups` variable = `["budget"]`, station = `"zone:catchment"`, reduce = `"mean"` Holes `variable`, `station`, `time`
 |
| `watershed_id_card` | double |
1. `map` variable = `["topography"]`, overlays = `["relief", "outline", "outlet", "network", "stations", "scale_bar"]`
1. `table` variable = `["simulation.solver", "simulation.flow_regime", "simulation.period_start", "simulation.period_end", "simulation.n_timesteps", "simulation.n_cells", "simulation.n_layers"]`
 |
| `network_expansion` | double |
1. `series` variable = `["simulated_active_network"]`, station = `"zone:catchment"` Holes `time`
1. `series` variable = `["discharge"]`, observed = `true` Holes `station`, `time`
 |

## Special figures

A special figure is a preset drawn by a function, and it takes no panel.

| Special figure | Subject | Width | Takes | Reads | What it draws |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `calibration_landscape` | `session` | double | - | `trials`, `bounds` | Cost over the plane of each pair of searched parameters, one marker per trial. |
| `calibration_progress` | `session` | double | - | `trials` | Cost of each trial of a calibration, the best so far and the trial the session returned. |
| `ensemble_band` | `runset` | double | `station` | `discharge` | The 10 to 90 % band and the median of one series across the runs of a set, at one station. |
| `flow_directions` | `run` | double | - | `topography` | Where each cell sends its water on the descent, drawn as binned arrows over the relief. |
| `lake_abacus_comparison` | `run` | | `station` | - | Stage-volume and stage-area curves of a lake, as stored and as the simulation followed. |
| `network_comparison` | `run` | double | - | - | The mapped and the generated networks matched at the tolerance of the run. |
| `observed_network_heads` | `run` | double | - | - | The mapped network drawn from its heads, and how each head landed. |
| `particle_tracks` | `run` | double | `time`, `variable` | - | Pathlines of the particle table in plan, coloured along their way by the age of the water. |
| `recharge_estimates` | `run` | medium | - | `recharge_estimates` | Yearly recharge of each method of [recharge_estimates], beside the run's own. |
| `recharge_regime` | `run` | double | - | `recharge_estimates` | The mean year of each method: rain and ETP, recharge, runoff, month by month. |
| `recharge_signals` | `run` | double | - | `recharge_estimates` | Monthly rain and ETP, then the recharge and the runoff of each method, month by month. |
| `parameter_space` | `runset` | single | `station`, `time`, `variable` | - | Two parameters of a run set on log axes, each run coloured by one score. |
| `recession` | `run` | medium | `station` | `discharge`, `hydraulic_conductivity`, `specific_yield` | Recession rate against discharge on the Brutsaert-Nieber plane, at one station. |
| `residence_time_distribution` | `run` | | - | `head` | Survival function of the particle travel times against the exponential of the turnover time. |
| `root_search` | `session` | | - | `trials` | The distances of a root search against the parameter it searched, one point per evaluation. |
| `sfr_longitudinal_profile` | `run` | double | `time` | `head`, `sfr_reaches`, `timeseries` | Streambed, stream stage and aquifer head along the main stem of the SFR network. |
| `water_balance_loop` | `run` | medium | - | `recharge_estimates` | Monthly rain minus evapotranspiration against the gauged discharge, the storage loop. |

## Overlays

An overlay is a context layer on a map or a section.

| Overlay | Reads the field | On by default in | What it draws |

| `relief` | `topography` | `map` | Shade the map by the relief of `topography`, dark on the slopes away from the sun. |

| `network` | - | `map` | Draw the reference network, intermittent reaches dashed when `reference_permanent` exists. |
| `generated_network` | - | - | Draw the network generated from the DEM. |
| `outlet` | - | `map` | Mark the outlet of `read_mesh`. |
| `stations` | - | - | Mark the observation points the run declared, from its `observation_points` table. |
| `lake` | `lake` | - | Outline the cells that exchange with a lake at the instant of the panel. |
| `barrier` | - | - | Draw the cut-off walls of the `barrier` layer. |
| `wells` | `well` | - | Mark the cells where the `well` term is not zero at the instant of the panel. |
| `seepage` | `seepage_mask` | `section` | Fill in ink the cells where the water table reaches the land surface at the instant. |
| `pathlines` | - | - | Draw the paths of the tracked particles as thin lines, one in n beyond `MAX_PATHLINES`. |
| `scale_bar` | - | `map` | Draw the scale bar of `static.scale_bar`. |
| `mesh` | - | - | Draw the cell edges in thin grey. |

# Glossary

The terms used in this part of the site, with a short definition. Where a term has a setting in the configuration file, the second line of its entry says where. A term can be cited from another page with `{term}`unconfined aquifer``.

On the pages of this part, a term underlined with dots shows its definition when you point at it or move the keyboard focus to it. On a touch screen, tap it once for the definition and a second time to open this page.

**actual evapotranspiration**: The part of the potential evapotranspiration that is really taken, limited by the water available in the soil. Abbreviated AET. The soil reservoir computes it.
**aquifer**: Rock or sediment saturated with water, which lets the water move and stores it.
**aquifer thickness**: Depth of the modeled layer below the ground surface: 30 m in example 04. This is an assumption. The depth to water table cannot exceed it. In the file: `domain.depth_model.thickness`.
**attempt**: One try of a run. A run that failed is tried again in its own folder: the earlier attempt moves under `attempts/<n>/`, and the run keeps its name and its version.
**available water capacity**: Water that roots can take from the soil, in mm. Abbreviated AWC. It sets how much water the soil keeps before it lets water pass to the water table. In the file: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.ru`.
**baseflow**: The part of the river flow that comes from the aquifer. In the model: the water that leaves the aquifer through the drains, summed over the catchment.
**BD Topage**: The reference hydrographic network of France, published by Sandre. HydroModPy can download it as a mapped network. It is not the same product as the BD TOPO. In the file: `data.hydrography`.
**BD TOPO**: The topographic database of the French national mapping agency (IGN). Example 04 takes its mapped network from the permanent reaches of this database. In the file: `data.hydrography`.
**calibration**: Tuning of the model parameters (here K, then Sy) so that its results look like observations. A calibrated result is not, for that reason, validated (see validation). In the file: `calibration.protocol.name`.
**case**: One point of a plan: a site crossed with a recipe, named `<site>-<recipe>`. Its run is the folder `runs/<site>-<recipe>/`.
**catchment**: Surface that gathers water toward a single exit point, the outlet. In HydroModPy, it is drawn from the relief and the position of the outlet. In the file: `geographic.catchment.kind`.
**cell**: One square of the computation grid: 75 m wide in example 04. The model computes one value per cell, and the maps count cells. The set of cells that cuts the model area is the mesh.
**conductance**: How freely a drain passes water for a given rise of the water table. Unless you declare one, the model derives it from the hydraulic conductivity and from the thickness of the clogging layer of the drain bed. In the file: `solver.drain_bed_thickness_m`.
**criterion**: A number that a calibration drives toward a target, over many trials. It must behave well along that search. The same number, only read, is a diagnostic.
**depth to water table**: Distance between the ground and the top of the water table, in meters, never negative. Figure: `variable = "watertable_depth"`, in `display.figure`.
**diagnostic**: A number that you read to describe a result, put in a report or use to compare two runs. It is not driven to a target. See criterion.
**digital elevation model**: Map of the ground elevation, on a regular grid. Abbreviated DEM. In the file: `data.dem`.
**downslope distance**: Distance a cell travels along the slope before it reaches a network. Written \(D_{so}\) from the simulated network to the mapped one, and \(D_{os}\) in the opposite direction. It measures how far apart two networks are.
**drain**: Condition that lets water leave the aquifer when the water table reaches its elevation, never the reverse. In example 04, the drains are placed at the ground surface and their capacity (the conductance) is deduced from K. In the file: a `[flow.bc.drainage]` table.
**ensemble**: A set of runs of the same model with different parameters or inputs. The spread between the runs shows how much a result depends on those choices. See How sure is the model?.
**equifinality**: Several different sets of parameters reproduce the observations about equally well. The calibration then cannot say which set is right. See How sure is the model?.
**excess**: A cell where the model puts a stream and the map has none. See valid.
**forcing**: What drives the model through time: the recharge, or the rainfall and the potential evapotranspiration from which a soil reservoir computes it.
**gauge**: The station at the outlet of a site whose discharge the model is compared with. Every observed series and every score reads it, unless a section names another station. In the file: `site.gauge`.
**groundwater**: Water that fills the pores of the ground below the water table.
**Hub’Eau**: The public interface to French water data. HydroModPy can download the discharge measured at a gauging station from its hydrometry service. In the file: `data.hydrometry`.
**hydraulic conductivity**: How easily the subsurface lets water pass, written K, in m/s. It cannot be measured at the scale of a catchment: it is calibrated. In the file: `flow.param.K.field.value`.
**hydraulic head**: Elevation of the water table at a point. It is the unknown that the model computes in each cell; the depth to water table is deduced from it. In the file (initial state): `flow.ic.h.kind`.
**hydrograph**: Curve of the flow as a function of time.
**indicative**: A reliability label. No field measurement was compared with this result. See reliability label.
**initial condition**: State of the water table at the start of the computation. In example 04, a first month in steady state provides it. In the file: `flow.ic.h.kind`, `flow.first_period_steady`.
**interfluve**: The higher ground between two valleys. The water table is deep under it.
**intermittent flow**: A stream that flows for only part of the year. On the intermittence map: a cell that flows at some time steps of the year, not at all of them.
**lockfile**: The file `hydromodpy.lock` at the root of a project. It pins the fetched data and your own files by checksum, gives the licence of each, and records the version of the code. `hmp data lock` writes it. Each run also seals the inputs it read in its own `inputs.json`. See Can I check what was run?.
**mapped network**: Streams drawn on a map (here, the permanent reaches of the BD TOPO). It is a reference to compare and calibrate against, not an input to the flow computation. In the file: `data.hydrography`.
**mesh**: The set of cells that cuts the model area. The word grid means the same thing when the cells are squares.
**missing**: A cell where the map has a stream and the model puts none. See valid.
**MODFLOW 6**: The groundwater flow code of the United States Geological Survey (USGS). It is the solver of example 04. HydroModPy also runs MODFLOW-NWT, an older code of the same family, and a Boussinesq solver written for HydroModPy.
**NANCON station**: The gauge at the outlet of the Nançon catchment. Example 04 compares the discharge measured there with the simulated one. In the file: `site.gauge`.
**NSE**: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency: compares simulated and measured flow. 1 is a perfect match, 0 is the same as predicting the mean of the measurements, and a negative value is worse. The “log” variant computes it on the logarithms to give weight to low flows. A run scores it at the gauge over the declared window, and leaves it empty without a window. In the file: `metrics.window`, `calibration.protocol.transient_metric`.
**numerical check**: A reliability label. An internal check of the computation, independent of the calibration. See reliability label.
**objective**: What a calibration tries to reach: one or several criteria, each computed on an observation such as the stream network or the discharge. In the file: `calibration.objective_blocks.metric`.
**outlet**: Exit point of the catchment, where the flow is measured. In the file: `geographic.catchment.x_outlet`.
**percent bias**: Volume gap between the simulated flow and the measured flow, as a percentage of the measured volume. Abbreviated PBIAS. It has the sign of the mean error, simulated minus measured: positive when the model overestimates, that is when it is too wet, and negative when it underestimates.
**perennial flow**: A stream that flows all year. On the intermittence map: a cell that flows at every time step of the year.
**persistence**: Share of the time steps during which a cell flows, over the whole simulation.
**plan**: The list of the cases of a project of many sites, with the resolved configuration of each. A plan is written once under `plan/<hash>/` and never rewritten.
**potential evapotranspiration**: Amount of water that the atmosphere could take back from a soil that is well supplied with water. Abbreviated PET. In the file: `data.etp`.
**provenance**: The record of what produced a result: the version of the code, the solver, the input files and their checksums. See Can I check what was run?.
**reach**: A stretch of stream between two points.
**reanalysis**: A gridded estimate of past weather or hydrology, made by running a model over all the observations available. SIM2 is one.
**recharge**: Water that reaches the water table from the soil. It is supplied, or computed by a soil reservoir. In the file: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge`, `data.recharge`.
**recipe**: A variant run on every site of a project: a file, or a file with a few keys changed. In the file: `sites.recipes`.
**reliability label**: One of three words that tell how far a result can be trusted: numerical check, calibrated and indicative. They are used under every figure of Reading the results.
**resolution**: The size of one cell, 75 m in example 04. A feature smaller than the resolution is not drawn.
**run**: One execution of a configuration file, kept in its own folder `runs/<name>/`. Its `README.md` says its catchment, its period, its version, its checks and its run label.
**run label**: One of four words derived from the checks of a run when it is read: exploratory, calibrated, evaluated or failed. Calibrated means the run comes from a completed calibration and passed its checks; evaluated means it was then scored on a window the calibration did not use. The label is computed on read, so a run sealed by a version with a known defect is downgraded without being rewritten. It is not the reliability label of a figure.
**runoff**: Water that reaches the stream without passing through the water table. In example 04, it is given to the model as data and is added to the drainage to form the simulated flow. In the file: `data.runoff`.
**scoring window**: Period over which simulated and measured flow are compared. In example 04, 2001 and 2002; the year 2000 is used as spin-up. The window of a run’s scores is also the default window of a calibration, which may narrow it. Under the network protocol with no window written, the second stage scores from one year after the start of the run. A validation window is taken out of that default: the search never reads its dates, and each trial is scored on them beside its cost. In the file: `metrics.window`, `calibration.window`, `calibration.validation_window`, and for the network protocol `calibration.protocol.window`.
**seepage**: Cell where the water table reaches the ground surface and where water leaves the aquifer. Rebuilt on read from the head and the ground surface (or from the surface excess of a Boussinesq run); nothing to set.
**seepage threshold**: Fraction of the mean basin recharge, over its own area, that a cell must give back to count as seepage: 0.01 % by default. Another threshold changes the network maps. In the file: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.seepage_threshold`.
**session**: The record of one calibration, the folder `sessions/<name>/`: its configuration, every trial and the best one. The best trial becomes a run of the same name.
**sidecar**: The small file `<file>.json` that sits next to a file a provider delivered. It records the variable, the source, the area and period, the checksum, the licence and where the file came from. The sidecars are the data cache: there is no database. A file you provide yourself, under `inputs/`, is not part of the cache, even if it has a sidecar to state its licence.
**SIM2**: Météo-France reanalysis on an 8 km grid, which supplies rainfall and potential evapotranspiration to the soil reservoir. In the file: `data.etp`.
**simulated network**: Extension downstream, following the slope of the terrain, of the cells where the aquifer gives water back to the surface. It does not result from a hydraulic river computation.
**site**: The catchment a file models: a name, and optionally a label, a gauge and a code that identifies it across workspaces. In the file: `site.name`.
**soil reservoir**: Simple daily balance: the soil fills with rain, empties by evapotranspiration and lets the surplus pass to the water table. In the file: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil`.
**specific yield**: Share of the rock volume that drains when the water table falls, written Sy, without dimension. It sets the speed at which the water table empties and refills. In the file: `flow.param.Sy.field.value`.
**spin-up**: Start of the simulation that is not scored, while the initial state of the model fades out. In example 04, the year 2000. The second stage of the network protocol leaves the first year out when no window is written. In the file: a scoring window that starts after it.
**spring**: A place where groundwater comes out of the ground. A seepage cell is a spring of the model.
**steady state**: Computation where nothing changes with time: the recharge is a constant mean. In the file: `flow.flow_regime`.
**stream head**: The upstream end of a stream, where it starts to flow. The heads dry up first in summer.
**stress period**: Interval over which the forcing is held constant. It is one month in example 04. The solver may cut it into smaller time steps. In the file: `simulation.time.step_value`, `simulation.time.substeps_per_period`.
**summary**: The tables, map, figures and report over all the cases of a project, written under `summary/` by `hmp campaign collect`. It is rebuilt from the runs each time.
**time step**: On the maps and curves of this part of the site, the unit of time of the results: one month in example 04. Strictly, the month is a stress period and the solver may cut it into smaller steps.
**TOML**: The plain-text format of the configuration file. One TOML file describes a whole run. The file of example 04 is walked through in Example 04.
**transient**: Computation where the recharge and the water table vary from one time step to the next. In the file: `flow.flow_regime`.
**trial**: One run of the model with one set of parameter values, tried by a calibration. A calibration runs many trials and keeps the best. The trials of a session are numbered once, across its phases and restarts.
**uncertainty**: How far a result could be from the truth. See How sure is the model?.
**unconfined aquifer**: Aquifer whose top is not trapped under an impermeable layer: it rises and falls freely with the recharge. HydroModPy targets this type of aquifer.
**valid**: A cell where the simulated network and the mapped network both pass. With excess and missing, it gives the three classes of the confusion map.
**validation**: A comparison of a model with measurements that the calibration has not seen. See What “validated” means here.
**visible flow**: Minimum flow that a cell must carry to count as “flowing” on the persistence maps: 1 L/s by default. It is a convention. In the file: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent.visible_flow`.
**water budget**: What enters the aquifer (recharge), what leaves it (drainage) and the change in storage. Its closure is a numerical check of the solver.
**water table**: The top of the groundwater: the level below which the ground is saturated. The model computes its elevation in every cell, as the hydraulic head.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/outputs.html -->
# Outputs of a run

A run stores its field arrays in `fields.zarr` and its station series in `tables.parquet/timeseries.parquet`. Both lists below are read from the field registry of the code. A name added to the registry shows up here at the next build.

## Field arrays

Each group is the first folder of the path in the store. The fields under `budget/` follow one sign rule, set in the registry.

### Top level

| Name | Path in the store | Unit | Dimensions | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `head` | `head` | `m` | time, layer, face | Groundwater head (per layer and UGRID face) |

# `[calibration.aggregate]`

How several scored targets become one cost.

- `calibration.aggregate`[table] · optional · 1 user key
[calibration.aggregate]

`# min_samples = 1` : Fewest paired samples a member may be scored on. - >= 1 experimental
**Path**: `calibration.aggregate.min_samples`
**More**: An alignment that collapses to three days still returns a number, and a weight of 65 per cent resting on three days is not what the file says it is.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/objective_blocks.html -->
# `[[calibration.objective_blocks]]`

Weighted metric block used by a composite objective.

- `calibration.objective_blocks`[[array of tables]] · optional · 6 user keys

Repeat the table: one `[[calibration.objective_blocks]]` block per item.

[[calibration.objective_blocks]]

`name = ‹string›` : Unique block identifier used in logs and persistence. required experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.name`
**Accepted**: string

`metric = ‹"rmse" | "nse" | "kge" | "mae" | "nse_log" | "nse_delta" | "nse_seasonal" | "reservoir" | "distance_gap" | "distance_mean" | "bfi_error"›` : Metric that scores this block against its observations. required experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.metric`
**Values**:
- `"rmse"` : Root-mean-square error, in the observed unit; penalizes large misfits most.
- `"nse"` : Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency against the observed mean; the standard choice for a level or discharge series.
- `"kge"` : Kling-Gupta efficiency, 2009 form (bias as the ratio of sums, variability as the ratio of standard deviations); separates correlation, variability and bias when NSE alone is ambiguous.
- `"mae"` : Mean absolute error, in the observed unit; less sensitive to outliers than RMSE.
- `"nse_log"` : NSE on log-transformed series; weights low flows as heavily as peaks, good for recessions.
- `"nse_delta"` : NSE on the increments of the series rather than its level; a level is an integral and can hide flux errors that compensate, which only its increments show.
- `"nse_seasonal"` : NSE against the seasonal cycle rather than the overall mean; asks whether the model beats climatology.
- `"reservoir"` : Half nse_seasonal plus half nse_delta, built for an impounded level: a plain NSE there is beaten by the seasonal cycle, and the increments are what carry the flux errors.
- `"distance_gap"` : Balances the simulated stream network against the mapped one; zero marks the crossing.
- `"distance_mean"` : Mean spatial offset between simulated and mapped streams; a diagnostic, not a substitute for distance_gap.
- `"bfi_error"` : Distance between the simulated and observed baseflow indices (Wallingford, daily discharge only); asks whether the stream is fed by its aquifer in the right share. Blind to volume and timing, so it goes beside a fit, never alone.
**Accepted**: "rmse" | "nse" | "kge" | "mae" | "nse_log" | "nse_delta" | "nse_seasonal" | "reservoir" | "distance_gap" | "distance_mean" | "bfi_error"

`uses_outputs = ‹list of string›` : Outputs (by name) consumed by this block. required at least 1 item experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.uses_outputs`
**More**: An error metric (rmse, mae) or a network distance may read several, pooled into one cost. A metric that rises with the fit (nse, kge and the other efficiencies) reads exactly one: write one block per output, each with its weight, so the costs average per station.
**Accepted**: list of string
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)

`# weight = 1.0` : Weight of this block in the sum of the block costs. - > 0 experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.weight`
**More**: Only the ratios between weights matter.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# normalize_cost = false` : When True, divide the block cost by a reference scale, so it adds to other blocks as a pure number and a share means a share. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.normalize_cost`
**More**: On a residual metric (rmse, mae) the scale is the standard deviation of the observations, their mean absolute value if that is zero. On a network distance (distance_gap, distance_mean) it is the output's validity_length, 2 h_obs under 'auto': a gap of one validity length costs 1, as much as an NSE of 0 on nse_log. Refused on an efficiency score, already a pure number.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# cost_transform = "identity"` : Transform applied to the cost of this block before weighting. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.objective_blocks.cost_transform`
**More**: Note that cost_transform='log' takes the logarithm of the cost, which is not the same thing as metric='nse_log', an NSE computed on log-transformed series.
**Values**:
- `"identity"` : Uses the block cost as computed, with no transform.
- `"log"` : Takes log10 of the cost plus a small epsilon, compressing large costs before weighting.
- `"inverse"` : Takes -1 / (cost + epsilon), sharpening the gradient near a cost of zero.
**Accepted**: "identity" | "log" | "inverse"
**Was**: `calibration.objective_blocks.transform`


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/outputs.html -->
# `[calibration.outputs]`

Named observables extracted from each candidate run.

- `calibration.outputs`{ name = table } · optional · 34 user keys, 3 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[calibration.outputs.<name>]`. The name is free text.

`support` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“point”
[calibration.outputs.<name>]

`support = "point"` : Observable extracted at a planar `(x, y)` point. chosen shape
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.support`
**More**: 'point' reads the variable at (x, y).
**Values**:
- `"point"` : Observable extracted at a planar `(x, y)` point.
- `"boundary"` : Observable extracted from a boundary package.
- `"cell"` : Observable extracted at one structured cell.
- `"lake"` : Observable extracted from a MODFLOW 6 LAK lake state.
- `"network"` : The mapped stream network as a calibration target.
**Accepted**: "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake" | "network"

`variable = "head"` : Simulated variable to extract (e.g. 'head', 'outlet_discharge'). required experimental example value
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.variable`
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"head"`

`# observes = ‹string›` : Station whose loaded record this output is scored against. varies by site experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observes`
**More**: The record is aligned on the simulated timestamps, so a weighted block scores dated observations rather than a vector typed into the file. The data family follows 'variable': discharge from hydrometry, head from piezometry, stage from lake_levels. Mutually exclusive with 'observed_values'. The station is located by its own record and not by coordinates written beside it, so this output and the single-metric route read the same cell and their costs are comparable; a station the project cannot locate is refused by name rather than scored on another quantity.
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"
**Varies by site**: yes: in a project of many sites, bind it to a column with `sites.bind` or set it in a per-site overlay; a literal value is refused

`# geometry = ‹table { key = any value }›` : GeoJSON point geometry. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.geometry`
**More**: Coordinates are in meters.
**Accepted**: table { key = any value }
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# x = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : X coordinate. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.x`
**More**: Accepts a bare number (meters) or a pint string like '100 m'. Beside 'observes' it is not read, and loading warns so, unless snap_radius is set and the station's record carries no coordinate.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# y = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Y coordinate. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.y`
**More**: Accepts a bare number (meters) or a pint string like '100 m'. Beside 'observes' it is not read, as for 'x'.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point"

`# time = "all"` : 'all' keeps every time step; 'last' / 'first' selects one. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.time`
**Values**:
- `"all"`
- `"last"`
- `"first"`
**Accepted**: "all" | "last" | "first"

`# reducer = "none"` : How the values kept by time are reduced before they are scored against 'observed_values'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.reducer`
**More**: Refused beside 'observes': its record is paired with the series step by step.
**Values**:
- `"mean"` : Scores one value: the mean of the kept values.
- `"sum"` : Scores one value: the sum of the kept values.
- `"last"` : Scores one value: the last kept value.
- `"none"` : Scores every kept value against its observation.
**Accepted**: "mean" | "sum" | "last" | "none"
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"

`# observed_values = ‹list of number›` : Hard-coded observed values, positional and dateless. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.observed_values`
**More**: Name a station in 'observes' to score a record the project loaded instead.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Only if**: support = "point" | "boundary" | "cell" | "lake"

`# snap_radius = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Opt-in. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.snap_radius`
**More**: Move this gauge onto the cell that drains the most within this radius, before it is scored. Accepts a bare number (metres) or a pint string like '150 m'; it is a maximum displacement, measured from the gauge coordinate to the cell centres. The drained area is the one the solver routes on the mesh, along the descent D of the build. Only for 'variable' = 'discharge'. With 'observes', a discharge station is then located by the coordinate of its record, which it otherwise is not, and snapped from there. Off by default: a gauge otherwise stays in the cell it resolves to, which may drain a small share of the catchment, and the run logs that share.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Only if**: support = "point" | "cell"

## `[calibration.outputs.<name>.map]`

What is observed: the mapped network, its role in the cost and how it is drawn.

Only with `support = "network"`.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.map]

`# complete = ‹"data.hydrography" or path›` : The complete map, every mapped reach: a vector file, read only from here, or 'data.hydrography', the network the hydrography data family loaded (a local file or an osm / bdtopage / euhydro download), clipped to the delineated catchment. varies by site experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.complete`
**Values**:
- `"data.hydrography"`
**Accepted**: "data.hydrography" or path
**Varies by site**: yes: in a project of many sites, bind it to a column with `sites.bind` or set it in a per-site overlay; a literal value is refused
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.stream_geometry_path`, `calibration.outputs.observed_network`

`# permanent = ‹"data.hydrography" or path›` : The permanent map, the reaches that flow all year, which the complete map contains: a vector file, read as it is and never filtered by attribute, or 'data.hydrography', the permanent reaches the hydrography data family wrote beside its network. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.permanent`
**More**: A source that does not say which reaches flow all year gives none. The complete map scored is the union of the two, and the share of this map outside the complete one is published.
**Values**:
- `"data.hydrography"`
**Accepted**: "data.hydrography" or path
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.minimal_stream_geometry_path`, `calibration.outputs.minimal_observed_network`

`# drawn_by = "crossing"` : How the map is drawn on the mesh cells. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.drawn_by`
**More**: 'crossing', the default, draws the map as the data gives it: it keeps the cell holding each point where a line crosses the segment joining two edge-sharing cell centres. On a structured grid it reproduces WhiteboxTools VectorLinesToRaster, the paper's tool, and draws the map one cell wide like the simulated network, so a model that matches the map scores J = 0. 'touch' keeps every cell the line touches, corners included, and replays a session made before 2026-09; it thickens every diagonal step of the map and departs from the paper. 'heads' keeps only the free ends of the map whose largest drained area within 'heads.radius' does not exceed that of the other end of their reach, lands each on a nearby cell and draws the rest down the criterion's own descent: the field ditches and rectified reaches below a head stop counting as model error, and the drawn map reaches the outlet. 'heads' does not suit a map that is not a tree: canals, braids, polders, karst.
**Values**:
- `"heads"`
- `"crossing"`
- `"touch"`
**Accepted**: "heads" | "crossing" | "touch"
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.observed_rasterization`

`# clip_to_catchment = true` : Cut the map to the delineated catchment before drawing it, with the shape the hydrography data family clips what it loads to, so a file and 'data.hydrography' draw the same map from the same data. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.clip_to_catchment`
**More**: Under 'heads' an end the cut made is no stream head. false reads a file whole and takes every free end as a candidate head.
**Accepted**: true | false
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.clip_map_to_catchment`

`# position_accuracy = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Positional accuracy of the map. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.position_accuracy`
**More**: It enters the automatic validity length only, so it is refused beside a 'verdict.validity_length' written as a length: the cell size h there is max(h_obs, this), because a map is not placed better when the mesh is refined. r_optim stays D_optim / h_obs, the paper's Eq. 3. Unset is the literal reading of the paper.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.observed_position_accuracy`

### `[calibration.outputs.<name>.map.calibrate_on]`

How the two maps of a network output share one calibrated value.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.map.calibrate_on]

`# permanent = 0.5` : Weight of the permanent map, scored against the minimal mask. - [0, 1] experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.calibrate_on.permanent`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# complete = 0.5` : Weight of the complete map, scored against the maximal mask. - [0, 1] experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.calibrate_on.complete`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

### `[calibration.outputs.<name>.map.heads]`

Where a mapped stream head may land, read only under `drawn_by = 'heads'`.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.map.heads]

`# radius = 100.0` : The largest distance, a length (a bare number is in metres), between a mapped stream head and the centre of the cell it lands on. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.heads.radius`
**More**: A head with no landing cell that close is lost, draws nothing and is counted in n_heads_lost.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.heads_snap_radius`

`# min_drained_area = 0.02` : The drained area a cell needs before a head may land on it, so a head next to its valley lands in the valley and not on the ridge cell beside it. km2 >= 0 experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.map.heads.min_drained_area`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: km2
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.heads_min_drained_area_km2`

## `[calibration.outputs.<name>.model]`

How the model draws its own stream network.

Only with `support = "network"`.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.model]

`# seepage_threshold = 0.0001` : A cell releasing less than this fraction of the mean basin recharge, taken over its own area, is not a seepage face. - >= 0 experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.seepage_threshold`
**More**: Zero reproduces the purely geometric criterion of the paper. Frozen over the whole search: a threshold moving with the trial would cost the criterion its monotonicity.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.tau_specific_ratio`

`# neighbours = "D8"` : The graph the descent walks. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.neighbours`
**More**: 'D8' descends over shared nodes, the eight neighbours of a quad mesh, and is the paper: its distances are traced by WhiteboxTools on a D8 pointer, and the delineation that produced the catchment uses one too. 'D4' descends over shared edges only and departs from the paper. It is not a second-decimal choice: on a synthetic valley whose talweg runs along the grid diagonal, the most accumulated cell collects 100 per cent of the domain over shared nodes and 6.6 per cent over shared edges. On a mesh whose faces are not all quadrilaterals no cell has a diagonal and the descent walks shared edges either way; on a Voronoi mesh the two graphs are the same one.
**Values**:
- `"D8"`
- `"D4"`
**Accepted**: "D8" | "D4"
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.diagonal_neighbors`

`# weighting = "cell"` : Average one cell one vote (the paper) or weighted by cell area. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.weighting`
**More**: Both values are always reported; use 'area' on a mesh refined along the streams, where cell density is highest exactly where distances are smallest.
**Values**:
- `"cell"` : Every cell counts once in the average, as in the paper.
- `"area"` : Every cell counts in proportion to its area.
**Accepted**: "cell" | "area"
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.weighting`

### `[calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent]`

The transient two-bound mode of a network output.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent]

`# flowing_at_least = ‹string›` : How long a cell has to flow in a year to enter the maximal mask, with its unit: '30 d', '1 month'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent.flowing_at_least`
**More**: Converted by the run's timestep, rounded up to whole timesteps and never below one. Left out, one timestep, whatever the step. At most the shortest complete year, checked on the run.
**Accepted**: string
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.extent.maximal_flowing_steps`, `calibration.outputs.extent.maximal_flowing_duration`

`# dry_at_most = ‹string›` : How long a cell may be dry in a year and stay in the minimal mask, with its unit: '1 d', '1 month'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent.dry_at_most`
**More**: Converted by the run's timestep and rounded down to whole timesteps, possibly none: '1 d' is one dry timestep on a daily run, none on a monthly one. Left out, one timestep, whatever the step. The year's timesteps minus these have to stay at least the flowing timesteps of the maximal rule, checked on the run, so the minimal mask sits inside the maximal one.
**Accepted**: string
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.extent.minimal_dry_steps`, `calibration.outputs.extent.minimal_dry_duration`

`# year_quorum = 0.5` : Share of the scored years in which a cell has to meet a bound's rule to enter it: ceil(year_quorum * n_years) years. - ]0, 1] experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent.year_quorum`
**More**: Warned under three scored years, where one half is a union of two.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# visible_flow = "1 L/s"` : Routed discharge a cell of the downstream closure has to carry to flow: a discharge with its unit ('1 L/s') or a share of the outlet discharge at the same timestep ('1%'). experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.model.extent.visible_flow`
**More**: '0 L/s' is the geometric definition. Never scaled with the cell size. It exists in this transient mode only: an output read in one state scores the closure alone. No value is agreed: Zanetti et al. (2024) threshold a simulated discharge at 10 L/s, field zero-flow thresholds of 1 to 3 L/s are in use.
**Accepted**: string

## `[calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict]`

When the result of a network output is qualified or refused.

Only with `support = "network"`.

[calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict]

`# max_catchment_mismatch = 0.05` : Largest gap allowed between the scored catchment and the delineated one, as a share of the delineated area: 'catchment_mismatch', the area of their symmetric difference over the area of the outline the mesh followed. >= 0 experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.max_catchment_mismatch`
**More**: It depends on the geometry alone, so it is read once, before the first solve, and a gap above it refuses the search. A large gap means an outlet on another branch, or a mesh too coarse for the catchment. false never refuses, and the gap is still published on every trial. A synthetic domain has no delineated catchment and is never refused.
**Values**:
- `false`no explanation
**Accepted**: number or false
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)

`# validity_length = "auto"` : Validity bound of Eq. 4, a length: the calibration is valid when D_optim <= this. m experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.validity_length`
**More**: 'auto' is 2 h, the paper's two cells, where h is h_obs, the cell size on the mapped network, raised to 'map.position_accuracy' if that is declared. A length such as '150 m' is used as it is. The bound qualifies the result and never penalises the cost.
**Values**:
- `"auto"`
**Accepted**: "auto" or number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.validity_length`

`# on_invalid = "warn"` : What a violation of Eq. 4 does: D_optim above 'validity_length'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.on_invalid`
**More**: The bound is read once, on the trial the search returns, as the paper reads it at the optimum, and on each bound in the cost of the two-bound mode; every trial still records 'r_optim', 'r_optim_valid' and 'validity_length_m'. 'warn' logs it and returns the value, because a calibration is asked for a number. 'error' raises after the session is saved, so a staged calibration freezes nothing and runs no phase that depends on this one.
**Values**:
- `"warn"`
- `"error"`
**Accepted**: "warn" | "error"
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.on_roptim_violation`

`# alpha_warning_threshold = 0.9` : Below this value of 'alpha_obs_closure_catchment' the run warns that its distances carry a top-versus-map disagreement on top of the hydrogeology. alpha is the share of the downstream closure of the mapped network the network itself covers, measured on the MODEL TOP and on the catchment. ]0, 1] expert experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.alpha_warning_threshold`
**More**: It changes nothing that is computed: the criterion is scored the same way above and below it.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.alpha_warning_threshold`

`# clipping_warning_share = 0.1` : Share of the mapped stream cells lying outside the delineated catchment above which the whole-mesh alpha is reported as unreadable. - [0, 1] expert experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.clipping_warning_share`
**More**: Those reaches trace through the buffer, where no cell is required to descend into the network, so they inflate the closure without adding to the numerator. Reported together with clipping_warning_gap, never alone.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.clipping_warning_share`

`# clipping_warning_gap = 0.05` : Minimum absolute gap between the whole-mesh and the catchment alpha for the clipping report to fire. [0, 1] expert experimental
**Path**: `calibration.outputs.<name>.verdict.clipping_warning_gap`
**More**: A linework spilling out of the catchment over ground that routes the same way leaves the two ratios equal, and reporting it there would be noise on every ordinary project.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Was**: `calibration.outputs.clipping_warning_gap`

# `[calibration.parameters]`

User declaration for one calibrated parameter.

- `calibration.parameters`{ name = table } · optional · 7 user keys

One table per name you choose: `[calibration.parameters.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[calibration.parameters.<name>]

`# bounds = ‹list of number›` : [low, high] physical bounds, in 'units' when the file writes it, else in the unit the target declares. exactly 2 items experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`
**More**: Falls back to what the field annotates when the file omits it, which most fields deliberately leave unset because a range belongs to the site.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: exactly 2 items (refused outside)

`# search_space = "identity"` : Space the search walks the parameter in. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.search_space`
**More**: 'log' for strictly-positive quantities spanning orders of magnitude. Unset, the target's own field decides: a hydraulic conductivity declares 'log' where it is defined, so a file states this only to depart from it.
**Values**:
- `"identity"` : Searches the value as written.
- `"log"` : Searches the logarithm of the value: for a positive quantity that spans orders of magnitude.
- `"logit"` : Searches log(x / (1 - x)): for a share strictly between 0 and 1. Both bounds must lie inside (0, 1).
**Accepted**: "identity" | "log" | "logit"
**Was**: `calibration.parameters.transform`

`# sampling = "uniform"` : Distribution, between the bounds, that starting points, random draws and Bayesian samplers take values from. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.sampling`
**Values**:
- `"uniform"` : Every value between the bounds is equally likely.
- `"log_uniform"` : Every decade between the bounds is equally likely.
- `"normal"` : A normal law centred between the bounds, with a standard deviation of a sixth of their span, cut at the bounds.
**Accepted**: "uniform" | "log_uniform" | "normal"
**Was**: `calibration.parameters.prior`

`# path = ‹string›` : Dotted TOML path of the value to move, such as 'flow.param.K.field.value'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.path`
**More**: Optional, and the way out rather than the way in: when omitted, the section name is resolved against the project catalogue ('hmp config targets' lists it). Write one to reach a value the catalogue does not carry, or to settle a name two targets answer to. A path written here wins without a lookup. When the catalogue carries it, the parameter inherits the field's space and draw like a named one; when it does not, nothing is inherited and the sample is written as it is drawn.
**Accepted**: string

`# target = ‹string›` : Readable alias for 'path'. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.target`
**More**: Setting both is refused.
**Accepted**: string

`# mode = "replace"` : 'replace' writes the sampled value as-is; 'scale' multiplies the base TOML value at the target path by the sample. experimental
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.mode`
**Values**:
- `"replace"`
- `"scale"`
**Accepted**: "replace" | "scale"

`# units = "m/s"` : Unit the bounds are written in, such as 'm/s'. experimental example value
**Path**: `calibration.parameters.<name>.units`
**More**: For a parameter the catalogue resolves, bounds in another unit of the same quantity are converted when the file loads into the unit the target is read in, and the search draws, writes and reports its samples in that unit ('hmp config targets' lists it). A unit of another quantity is refused. Unset, the unit of the target applies. With mode = 'scale' the bounds are factors without a unit, and writing one is refused. For a path outside the catalogue it is the unit the bounds are checked against the physical range in.
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"m/s"`
