# `[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers]`

Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).

- `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers`{ name = table } · optional · 13 user keys

One table per name you choose: `[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>]

`# enabled = true` : Whether this barrier is built. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.enabled`
**More**: Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# auto = false` : Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.auto`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# line = ‹list of list of number›` : Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.line`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
**Accepted**: list of list of number

`# line_path = ‹path›` : Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.line_path`
**More**: A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
**Accepted**: path

`# depths = ‹list of number›` : Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). m at least 1 item experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.depths`
**More**: One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# crest_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). m experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.crest_elevation`
**More**: Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# base_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. m experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.base_elevation`
**More**: When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# hydchr = ‹number›` : HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. >= 0 calibrable · log experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.hydchr`
**More**: A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Zero is accepted only without XT3D: MODFLOW 6 ignores a zero hydchr under XT3D, so the build refuses it with XT3D active (XT3D turns itself on for triangle and strongly non-orthogonal meshes). Each face of the barrier receives hydchr times trace length over the summed face length, so a zigzag chain of faces keeps the declared conductance. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: 1/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# hydchr_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.hydchr_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# k = ‹number›` : Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]. > 0 calibrable · log experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.k`
**More**: Give it with thickness in place of hydchr.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# k_unit = "m/s"` : Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.k_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# thickness = ‹number›` : Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). m > 0 experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.thickness`
**More**: With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness, in place of hydchr.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# thickness_unit = "m"` : Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers.<name>.thickness_unit`
**More**: Converted to m.
**Accepted**: string


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/lakes.html -->
# `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes]`

Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 LAK lake.

- `flow.sinks_sources.lakes`{ name = table } · optional · 134 user keys, 39 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>]

`bedleak = 1e-06` : Lake-bed leakance [1/T] = K_bed / thickness_bed. required >= 0 calibrable · log example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bedleak`
**More**: Resistance of the lake-aquifer interface over the whole lake bed, the handle of the lake-aquifer exchange. The flow through or under the dam is set by the cutoff_wall and the aquifer, not by this value. 0 means a perfectly sealed lakebed (no leakage).
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: 1/s
**Example**: `1e-06`
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`initial_stage = 45.0` : Lake stage at the start of the run: the elevation of the water surface, in metres. required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.initial_stage`
**More**: When the first period is steady, the steady solve sets the stage and this value is only its first guess, unless steady_stage_hold holds it.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `45.0`
**Was**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.stageinit`

`# enabled = true` : Whether this lake is built.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.enabled`
**More**: Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# bedleak_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of bedleak (leakance, 1/T): one of 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min (aliases like 1/d accepted).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bedleak_unit`
**More**: HydroModPy converts it to 1/s for MF6, so a 1/day leakance is not silently taken as 1/s.
**Accepted**: string

`# steady_stage_hold = false` : Hold the lake stage at initial_stage during the steady warm-up period(s) (LAK status CONSTANT) and re-activate it on the first transient period.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.steady_stage_hold`
**More**: Use for a managed reservoir whose observed initial level is far from the natural steady equilibrium: the aquifer equilibrates around the observed stage instead of overriding it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# occupied_layers = 1` : Number of top grid layers the lake occupies in each of its columns. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.occupied_layers`
**More**: 1 is a surface lake; a deeper reservoir embedded over several layers uses a higher count. Must leave at least one active layer below the lake for the VERTICAL leakage connection. A count of layers.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# fill_enclosed_cells = false` : Fill cells enclosed by the lake footprint (the polygon's interior rings / islands) so the lake is contiguous.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.fill_enclosed_cells`
**More**: Off by default: interior rings stay active aquifer (real islands). Enable to drop sub-grid islands and classification pockets that would otherwise be isolated non-lake cells inside the lake.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# surfdep = ‹number›` : LAK surface depression depth [L] that smooths the dry/wet (marnage) transition for Newton. m >= 0 expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.surfdep`
**More**: Default (None) uses 0.1 m. Raise it (e.g. 0.5 to 1.0 m) to stabilise and speed up the active-littoral steady solve when many lakebed cells toggle at once; it slightly fuzzes the shoreline.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

## `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction]`

Opt-in carving of the real lake bed from bathymetry into the grid.

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction]

`# reconcile_to_abacus = true` : Re-map the regridded bed so the cell area-vs-elevation distribution matches the abacus (the abacus is the storage source of truth).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.reconcile_to_abacus`
**More**: When False, the raw regridded bathymetry is carved as-is.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# dynamic_area = false` : Active-littoral (marnage) representation.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.dynamic_area`
**More**: When True the lake-bed cells stay ACTIVE with the carved bathymetric bed as their cell top and one VERTICAL LAK connection each; MODFLOW 6 then toggles recharge/ET per cell (IWETLAKE) so a cell exchanges with the lake when submerged and recharges as land when the shoreline recedes below its bed. When False the footprint is deactivated (fixed-area reservoir, the classic inactive-footprint carve).
**Accepted**: true | false

`# bank_seepage = true` : Also emit HORIZONTAL (bank) LAK connections on the active-littoral footprint, in addition to the VERTICAL (bed) ones, so the lake exchanges with the aquifer through both the bed AND the banks (the physical case). only if dynamic_area = true
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.bank_seepage`
**More**: Sealed at the cutoff wall (dam) when one is declared. Only applies with dynamic_area = true; a fixed-area lake always emits both. Set False to keep the bed-only marnage representation (the bedleak then absorbs the bank contribution).
**Accepted**: true | false
**Only if**: dynamic_area = true

`# min_thickness = 0.5` : Minimum layer thickness, in metres, held by EVERY layer when re-grading a lake column around the carved bed, so no degenerate (near-zero) cell breaks the solver. m > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.min_thickness`
**More**: The bed is clamped into the band the column can hold at that floor, i.e. [base + n_active * min_thickness, top - n_occupied * min_thickness]; a column too thin for it raises at build time. Raising this value moves the carved bed away from the bathymetry (the build logs the shift).
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# min_pixels = 1` : Minimum bathymetry pixels whose centre must fall inside a cell for the zonal mean to be used; below it a bilinear sample at the cell centroid is taken instead. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.min_pixels`
**More**: A count of pixels.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# exposed_band_runoff = false` : Shed the overland runoff of the exposed lakebed band directly to the lake, sized per timestep from the simulated stage via the MODFLOW 6 BMI API (runoff_rate * exposed_area). expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.bed_reconstruction.exposed_band_runoff`
**More**: Requires dynamic_area and forces the in-process API runner (serial only). When False the catchment runoff already covers the footprint area in a lumped, stage-static way.
**Accepted**: true | false

## `[[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets]]`

Surverse / spillway / controlled-release outlets for this lake.

Repeat the table: one `[[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets]]` block per item.

`kind` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“WEIR”
[[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets]]

`kind = "WEIR"` : A sharp-crest weir outlet: `Q = (2/3)*Cd*width*sqrt(2g)*d^(3/2)`. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.kind`
**Values**:
- `"WEIR"` : A sharp-crest weir outlet: `Q = (2/3)*Cd*width*sqrt(2g)*d^(3/2)`.
- `"MANNING"` : A Manning channel outlet: `Q ~ (1/rough)*width*d^(5/3)*sqrt(slope)`.
- `"SPECIFIED"` : A specified-flow outlet (controlled release / gate): `Q = rate`.
**Accepted**: "WEIR" | "MANNING" | "SPECIFIED"
**Was**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.outlets.couttype`

`invert = 45.0` : Elevation of the weir crest, in metres. required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.invert`
**More**: No water leaves while the stage is at or below it.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `45.0`
**Only if**: kind = "WEIR" | "MANNING"

`width = 10.0` : Effective length of the weir crest, in metres. required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.width`
**More**: The discharge grows in proportion to it.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `10.0`
**Only if**: kind = "WEIR" | "MANNING"

`# lakeout = 0` : Number of the lake that receives the discharge, counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared. - >= 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.lakeout`
**More**: 0 sends the discharge out of the model. A sill between two lakes is one outlet, on the upper lake; two WEIR outlets that spill into each other over the same crest are refused.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

“MANNING”
[[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets]]

`kind = "MANNING"` : A Manning channel outlet: `Q ~ (1/rough)*width*d^(5/3)*sqrt(slope)`. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.kind`
**Values**:
- `"WEIR"` : A sharp-crest weir outlet: `Q = (2/3)*Cd*width*sqrt(2g)*d^(3/2)`.
- `"MANNING"` : A Manning channel outlet: `Q ~ (1/rough)*width*d^(5/3)*sqrt(slope)`.
- `"SPECIFIED"` : A specified-flow outlet (controlled release / gate): `Q = rate`.
**Accepted**: "WEIR" | "MANNING" | "SPECIFIED"
**Was**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.outlets.couttype`

`invert = 45.0` : Elevation of the weir crest, in metres. required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.invert`
**More**: No water leaves while the stage is at or below it.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `45.0`
**Only if**: kind = "WEIR" | "MANNING"

`width = 10.0` : Effective length of the weir crest, in metres. required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.width`
**More**: The discharge grows in proportion to it.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `10.0`
**Only if**: kind = "WEIR" | "MANNING"

`rough = 0.035` : Manning roughness coefficient n of the outlet channel. required s/m^(1/3) > 0 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.rough`
**More**: A higher value slows the discharge.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: s/m^(1/3)
**Example**: `0.035`
**Only if**: kind = "MANNING"

`slope = 0.001` : Slope of the outlet channel bed, in meters of drop per meter of length. required - > 0 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.slope`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `0.001`
**Only if**: kind = "MANNING"

`# lakeout = 0` : Number of the lake that receives the discharge, counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared. - >= 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.lakeout`
**More**: 0 sends the discharge out of the model. A sill between two lakes is one outlet, on the upper lake; two WEIR outlets that spill into each other over the same crest are refused.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

“SPECIFIED”

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.kind`

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.outlets.mover.discharge_xy`
**More**: With to_downstream_reach, the dam foot is located nearest this point instead of inferred from the domain outlet. Use it when the spillway is not on the outlet-facing shore, or for a lake away from the catchment outlet.
**Accepted**: list of number

## `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall]`

The flow barrier of a lake dam, laid on the lake shore.

[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall]

`# enabled = true` : Whether this barrier is built. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.enabled`
**More**: Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# auto = false` : Auto-place the dam cutoff wall (lakes only): the trace is derived at bind time as the chord across the reservoir at its downstream neck (the footprint point nearest the catchment outlet), perpendicular to the outlet-flow direction. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.auto`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line / line_path; the mesh dam refinement then follows this auto axis too.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# line = ‹list of list of number›` : Inline barrier-trace vertices [(x, y), ...] in the project CRS. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.line`
**More**: Mutually exclusive with line_path and auto.
**Accepted**: list of list of number

`# line_path = ‹path›` : Barrier-trace file: a vector polyline (gpkg / shp / GeoJSON) or a CSV of ordered x,y (or lon,lat) vertices. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.line_path`
**More**: A bare filename resolves against <workspace>/data/cutoff_wall/. Alternative to line and auto.
**Accepted**: path

`# depths = ‹list of number›` : Barrier depth [m] below the top (or below crest_elevation). m at least 1 item experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.depths`
**More**: One value is uniform; several are interpolated per vertex along the trace. The HFB blocks every layer down to this depth. Mutually exclusive with base_elevation.
**Accepted**: list of number
**Valid range**: at least 1 item (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# crest_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute TOP elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]; defaults to the cell top (the DEM). m experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.crest_elevation`
**More**: Set it when the barrier crest sits below the DEM top. Not calibratable: raising the crest and lowering hydchr both shrink the flow section the wall lets through, so a search cannot tell the two apart. It is a built structure, not a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# base_elevation = ‹number›` : Absolute BOTTOM elevation of the barrier [m, model datum]. m experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.base_elevation`
**More**: When set, the HFB spans [base_elevation, crest_elevation or top] and blocks EVERY layer in that band. Use it to make a full-height dam impervious: the concrete body plus the grout curtain block all flow from the crest down to the curtain foot (e.g. base_elevation = 41 m), so nothing seeps across the dam above that. Mutually exclusive with depths. Not calibratable: a deeper foot and a lower hydchr produce the same reduction of under-dam flow, so putting both in a search is equifinality by construction, the same mechanism that makes the second stage of the stream-network protocol pin the specific yield on its bound. When the foot is genuinely unknown, run mode = "comparison", one elevation per run, which also yields a defensible sensitivity instead of a fitted number; path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for an override.
**Accepted**: number
**Unit**: m

`# hydchr = ‹number›` : HFB hydraulic characteristic [1/T] = K_barrier / thickness_barrier. >= 0 calibrable · log experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.hydchr`
**More**: A near-zero value (e.g. 1e-9 1/s) is a quasi-impermeable wall. Zero is accepted only without XT3D: MODFLOW 6 ignores a zero hydchr under XT3D, so the build refuses it with XT3D active (XT3D turns itself on for triangle and strongly non-orthogonal meshes). Each face of the barrier receives hydchr times trace length over the summed face length, so a zigzag chain of faces keeps the declared conductance. Mutually exclusive with k + thickness.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: 1/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# hydchr_unit = "1/s"` : Unit of hydchr (1/T): 1/s, 1/day, 1/h, 1/min. Converted to 1/s for MF6. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.hydchr_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# k = ‹number›` : Barrier hydraulic conductivity [L/T]. > 0 calibrable · log experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.k`
**More**: Give it with thickness in place of hydchr.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# k_unit = "m/s"` : Unit of k (L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h, m/min. Converted to m/s. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.k_unit`
**Accepted**: string

`# thickness = ‹number›` : Thickness of the barrier, in the unit thickness_unit names (metres by default). m > 0 experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.thickness`
**More**: With k it gives hydchr = k / thickness, in place of hydchr.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# thickness_unit = "m"` : Unit of thickness (L): m, cm, mm, km. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.thickness_unit`
**More**: Converted to m.
**Accepted**: string

`# snap_tolerance = 50.0` : Largest gap [m] between the declared trace and the lake shore. m >= 0 experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.cutoff_wall.snap_tolerance`
**More**: The part of the trace facing the lake moves onto the shore it faces, so no cell sits between the reservoir and the wall; the trace beyond the banks stays as declared. A trace farther than this from the lake is refused. A trace that crosses the lake cuts its footprint, and the part downstream is dropped.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.kind`
**Values**:
- `"constant"` : One value applied to every stress period.
- `"csv"` : A dated record read from a CSV file and aligned on the stress periods.
- `"piecewise"` : Ordered dated segments, each a constant or a csv.
- `"seasonal"` : Calendar month or season to value, repeated across the years.
**Accepted**: "constant" | "csv" | "piecewise" | "seasonal"

`path_file = "forcing.csv"` : CSV file of the dated values. required example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.path_file`
**More**: Each stress period takes the aggregate of the samples that fall inside it.
**Accepted**: path
**Example**: `"forcing.csv"`
**Only if**: kind = "csv"
**Workspace file**: `workspace:<name>` reads `data/forcing/<name>` of the workspace, and `workspace:.` the folder itself

`# units = ‹string›` : Unit of the values: a volume per time such as 'm3/day' for a flow, a length per time such as 'mm/day' for a rate on a surface, a length for a head.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.units`
**More**: Values are converted to SI when the run starts. Unset, a well forcing takes the well's units, a boundary head the boundary's, and the others read SI.
**Accepted**: string

`# date_column = "date"` : Name of the CSV column that holds the dates.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.date_column`
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: kind = "csv"

`# value_column = "value"` : Name of the CSV column that holds the values.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.value_column`
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: kind = "csv"

`# sep = ","` : CSV delimiter. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.sep`
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: kind = "csv"

`# date_format = ‹string›` : Optional datetime format passed to pandas.to_datetime. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.date_format`
**Accepted**: string
**Only if**: kind = "csv"

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff.aggregate`
**Values**:
- `"mean"`no explanation

**Accepted**: "mean" | "last"
**Only if**: kind = "csv"

# `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]`

Typed payload for diffuse recharge over the model domain.

- `flow.sinks_sources.recharge`[table] · optional · 23 user keys, 5 dev or expert

Connections found in the code (3)
- Same name `[data.recharge]` Recharge data: a synthetic series, custom files or SIM2 grids, in mm/day. Read when `data.types` lists `"recharge"`.
- The code says `calibration.parameters`: [calibration.parameters....] moves flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values, which ...
- The code says `data.types`: flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values = ... would be replaced by the series [data.recharge] loads, so the model would not read it: remove values (write values__delete = true if a base file declares it), or remove "recharge" from data.types to impose this rate.

[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]

`# enabled = true` : Whether the model receives this recharge.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.enabled`
**More**: Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# values = 0.0` : Recharge rate: one number, one number per stress period, or a table {period: value} that states every period, in the unit that 'units' names (mm/day by default). mm/day calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values`
**More**: It is positive when water enters the aquifer; a negative rate leaves it, through the EVT package when negative_to_evt holds. A calibration reads its bounds in that unit too. Do not write it beside [data.recharge] or the soil section, which replace it.
**Accepted**: any value
**Unit**: mm/day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# factor = 1.0` : Number that multiplies the recharge in force, from 'values' or from [data.recharge], a deficit and a numeric first_clim included. > 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.factor`
**More**: 1 changes nothing. Do not write it beside the soil section, whose recharge is an output.
**See**: data.recharge
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, default bounds [0.5, 2.0]

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.units`
**More**: Data-manager outputs use mm/day by convention; set it when you write 'values' in another unit. The run converts the rate to m/s.
**Accepted**: string

`# heterogeneous_source = ‹any value›` : Optional raw data source for heterogeneous (2D per-cell) recharge. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.heterogeneous_source`
**More**: When set, the solver adapter discretizes FieldRecords onto the MODFLOW grid instead of using the scalar 'values' field. Expected: LoadResult with FieldRecords.
**Accepted**: any value

`# first_clim = "mean"` : Recharge rate of every steady stress period: every period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when flow.first_period_steady is true. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim`
**More**: 'mean' is the mean of the per-period rates, each weighted by its length; 'first' is the rate of period 0; a number is that rate, in the units of values. A transient period keeps its own rate. The same rule holds for one value per period and for one grid per period, under every solver. With negative_to_evt, the steady period takes the rule on the recharge part and on the deficit part, so its net rate is the one stated here. Boussinesq has no EVT and refuses a negative number.
**See**: flow.first_period_steady
**Accepted**: string or number
**Example**: `"mean"`, `"first"`, `2.0`

**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.negative_to_evt`
**More**: Boussinesq has no EVT and refuses a negative rate whatever this says.
**Accepted**: true | false

## `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]`

Daily soil reservoir that turns precipitation and ETP into recharge.

Connections found in the code (5)
- Same name `[recharge_estimates.soil]` The soil the laws of soil_methods run with, when the run has no [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] of its own, such as a run forced by SIM2.
- The code says `data.types`: [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] computes the recharge from the precipitation and the ETP, and data.types also loads one from [data.recharge]: the model would receive one and ignore the other. Remove "recharge" from data.types to keep the soil reservoir (and write recharge__delete = true under [data] if a base file declares it), or remove [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] to use the loaded rech
- The code says `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.scenario`: [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.scenario] rebuilds the loaded recharge, and [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] computes it from the weather: remove one of them.
- The code says `flow.sinks_sources.sfr`: [flow.sinks_sources.sfr....] sets route_drainage = false with a lake and [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]: the water of the drains would leave the model and the lake would receive only its own rain. Remove route_drainage = false (it is on by default).
- The code says `data.recharge`: [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] computes the recharge from the precipitation and the ETP, and data.types also loads one from [data.recharge]: the model would receive one and ignore the other. Remove "recharge" from data.types to keep the soil reservoir (and write recharge__delete = true under [data] if a base file declares it), or remove [flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] to use the loaded rech

[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil]

`ru = "150 mm"` : Available water capacity of the soil, in mm of water: what the roots can draw between field capacity and wilting point. required mm [0, 1000] calibrable example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.ru`
**More**: A bare number is in mm; "120 mm" and "12 cm" also read. Between 0 and 1000 mm. Required, since it belongs to the site. Start from a soil map, then compare the recharge the soil alone prints for 50 to 250 mm with the gauged discharge (hmp run <file> --until load_data). With [data.soil_capacity], it is the mean capacity over the catchment, and the raster spreads it over classes inside each cell. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.ru].
**Accepted**: number or "<n> mm" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 1000] (refused outside)
**Unit**: mm
**Example**: `"150 mm"`
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# method = "fao56"` : Storage law of the soil, the one thing that differs between methods. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.method`
**More**: "fao56" lowers ETR linearly below alpha x ru (Allen et al. 1998). "thornthwaite" meets the full demand while water is left (Thornthwaite 1948). "dingman" empties the soil as an exponential of the deficit on dry days (Dingman 2008). "edijatno_michel" is the production store of GR4J without its percolation (Edijatno and Michel 1989). The sealed share, the curve number, the bypass, the transit and the snow work the same around every law.
**Accepted**: string
**Example**: `"fao56"`, `"thornthwaite"`

`# alpha = 0.45` : Share of ru above which the soil evaporates at the full rate kc x ETP. ]0, 1] calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.alpha`
**More**: Below alpha x ru, ETR falls linearly with the stored water. It is 1 - p of FAO-56 and LP of HBV. The default 0.45 is a choice: it means p = 0.55, the value of FAO-56 table 22 for cereals and maize (pasture 0.60). Above 0, at most 1. Kept fixed by default: on the discharge alone it trades off with ru, since both move the annual volume.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: ]0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, default bounds [0.3, 1.0]

`# impervious_fraction = 0.0` : Share of the area that is sealed (roofs, roads). [0, 1[ calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.impervious_fraction`
**More**: The rain that falls on it runs off at once, with no infiltration and no evaporation, and reaches the streams, the lakes and the gauged discharge. The soil reservoir covers the rest of the area. From 0 up to, not including, 1. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.impervious_fraction]; the range belongs to the site, so a file has to state it. [data.impervious] gives it cell by cell instead, and then it is not written here.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1[ (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# bypass_fraction = 0.0` : Share of the rain on the unsealed area that skips the soil through macropores and joins the recharge the same day, even when the soil is dry. [0, 1[ calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.bypass_fraction`
**More**: From 0 up to, not including, 1. Keep it at 0 while K and Sy are calibrated: a bypass can rebuild the summer recharge the soil reservoir removes.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1[ (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, default bounds [0.0, 0.3]

`# transit_time = 0.0` : Mean time the water leaving the soil takes to cross the unsaturated zone down to the water table, in days. day [0, 30] calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.transit_time`
**More**: A linear reservoir with this time constant delays and smooths the recharge; 0 sends it the same day. A bare number is in days; "5 days" also reads. At most 30 days: a longer delay would rebuild the slow groundwater memory MODFLOW computes itself.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 30] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, default bounds [0.0, 30.0]

`# curve_number = ‹number›` : SCS curve number (AMC II), dimensionless, of a HELP-style surface runoff (Schroeder et al. 1994): the unsealed share of the rain above a daily retention loses some to a fast runoff, more as the soil is wetter. [30, 98] calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.curve_number`
**More**: None turns the term off, bit for bit as before. Between 30 and 98. It reads the soil and never the water table, so it renders saturation runoff badly: leave it off where the drains already give that runoff. To calibrate it, state a range under [calibration.parameters.curve_number]: it belongs to the soil group and the land use of the site. [data.curve_number] gives it cell by cell instead, and then it is not written here.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [30, 98] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# infiltration_ratio = 1.0` : Share of the water leaving the soil that goes on to the aquifer, the RIPE of ESPERE (BRGM): the rest runs off on the same day, beside the sealed share and the curve number, and reaches the streams through the runoff of the run. - [0, 1] experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.infiltration_ratio`
**More**: 1, the default, sends it all to the aquifer, bit for bit as before, and the drains give back what saturates. Between 0 and 1. ESPERE proposes the lowest yearly baseflow index of the gauge, which the soil budget of `hmp run --until load_data` prints when a gauge is loaded: copy it here, the gauge never sets it on its own. [data.infiltration_ratio] gives it cell by cell instead, and then it is not written here.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: [0, 1] (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# runoff_time = 1.0` : Time constant of the linear reservoir that routes the curve-number runoff to the outlet, in days. day [0, 10] calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.runoff_time`
**More**: No effect without a curve number, here or in [data.curve_number]. 0 sends it the same day; "2 days" also reads. Between 0 and 10 days: a longer delay would smooth away the fast surface peak the term exists for.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 10] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, default bounds [0.0, 10.0]

`# runoff_lag = 0.0` : Pure delay applied to the routed curve-number runoff, after runoff_time, before it reaches the gauged discharge: the travel time to the outlet plus any lag between the forcing's daily step and the gauge's. day [0, 5] calibrable experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.runoff_lag`
**More**: No effect without a curve number, here or in [data.curve_number]. 0 adds no delay, bit for bit as before; "0.75 days" also reads, interpolated linearly between the neighbouring whole-day shifts. Between 0 and 5 days: a longer shift belongs to runoff_time's reservoir, not to a fixed travel time. Calibrate it with [calibration.parameters.runoff_lag].
**Accepted**: number or "<n> day" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: [0, 5] (refused outside)
**Unit**: day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, default bounds [0.0, 5.0]

`# spinup = "first_year"` : State of the soil on the first day. experimental
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil.spinup`
**More**: "first_year" repeats the first 365 days of the run until the storage at the end of that year moves by less than 0.1 mm, 20 times at most; the run must last 364 days (52 weeks) at least, and a 364-day run repeats those 364 days. "none" starts from a full soil, the state of a soil in a wet winter. Beside a cyclic spin-up of the aquifer (flow.ic.kind = "spinup_cyclic"), the two starts are computed over two windows: the soil settles on the first year, the heads on the whole run. That pair is allowed without a warning, because it is sometimes what the study wants.
**Values**:
- `"first_year"` : Repeat the first year until the soil storage settles.
- `"none"` : Start from a full soil and an empty transit store.
**Accepted**: "first_year" | "none"

**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: [0, 50] (refused outside)
**Unit**: year

`# start = 1990` : Calendar year of the first dry year of the scenario. year experimental example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.scenario.start`
**Accepted**: integer
**Unit**: year
**Example**: `1990`

# `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr]`

Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 SFR stream network.

- `flow.sinks_sources.sfr`{ name = table } · optional · 116 user keys, 36 dev or expert

One table per name you choose: `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>]`. The name is free text.

[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>]

`# enabled = true` : Whether this stream network is built.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.enabled`
**More**: Declaring it is what activates it. false keeps the table and builds nothing from it.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# min_reach_length = "0 m"` : Prune reaches shorter than this [L] (0 keeps all reaches). m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.min_reach_length`
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# manning = 0.035` : Manning roughness coefficient n [T/L^(1/3)] (> 0). > 0 calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.manning`
**More**: Default 0.035.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: s/m^(1/3)
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# streambed_k = 1e-06` : Streambed hydraulic conductivity rhk [L/T]. >= 0 calibrable · log
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.streambed_k`
**More**: 0 = no reach-aquifer leakage (pure routing).
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space log, sampling log_uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# streambed_k_unit = "m/s"` : Unit of streambed_k (velocity, L/T): m/s, m/day, m/h...
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.streambed_k_unit`
**More**: HydroModPy converts it to m/s for MF6, so a m/day value is not taken as m/s.
**Accepted**: string

`# streambed_thickness = "1 m"` : Streambed thickness rbth [L] (> 0). m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.streambed_thickness`
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# min_slope = 0.0001` : Smallest slope a reach bed may take, in metres of drop per metre (floor of rgrd). - > 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.min_slope`
**More**: It also sets the drop the bed profile solve keeps between neighbouring reaches.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# bed_incision = ‹number or "<n> m"›` : Depth [L] of the streambed top rtp below the top of the reach's OWN aquifer cell. m
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.bed_incision`
**More**: A bed never sits above the ground of its own cell, whether this is set or not. None (default) only lifts the lower bound: the bed may then sink to the cell bottom instead of stopping at max_bed_sag. When set, each reach is solved inside [cell_top - bed_incision - max_bed_sag, cell_top - bed_incision], monotone downstream, and the build refuses when that band is empty. rtp is delineated on the model top, so this anchors a bed that a coarse DEM cannot resolve; it is not a correction for the descent D, which never reaches the bed. Pick it against the water table, not against the channel: MODFLOW 6 switches a reach between connected and disconnected at rtp minus streambed_thickness (gwf-sfr.f90:3973-3985), so a bed sitting near the seasonal water-table depth toggles at every outer iteration.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# connected_to_aquifer = true` : If False every reach uses cellid 'none' (routing only, no streambed leakage).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.connected_to_aquifer`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# route_drainage = true` : Route the hillslope drainage (DRN) discharge into the stream network: every remaining DRN cell of the basin hands its outflow, through an MVR record (FACTOR 1.0), to the first reach or lake cell met on its descent D, a filled copy of the model top.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.route_drainage`
**More**: A cell whose descent leaves the model first keeps a plain DRN. This is the surface re-infiltration / runon convergence of drained water towards the river; without it only the reach cells' streambed captures baseflow and the rest of the catchment discharge is lost (a few per cent of the water of a catchment). On by default; set False only to study the network alone.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# storage = false` : Enable the channel-storage term (transient first period / SIMPLE only).
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.storage`
**Accepted**: true | false

`# outflow_to_lake = ‹integer›` : Number of the lake the last reach feeds through a mover (SFR -> LAK), counted from 1 in the order the lakes are declared. - >= 1
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_to_lake`
**More**: Unset, the network outflow leaves the model.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

`# outflow_mvrtype = "FACTOR"` : How much of the network outflow the mover passes to the lake, given outflow_value.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_mvrtype`
**Values**:
- `"FACTOR"` : Moves the share outflow_value (from 0 to 1) of the outflow.
- `"UPTO"` : Moves the outflow, capped at outflow_value.
- `"EXCESS"` : Moves only the part of the outflow above outflow_value.
- `"THRESHOLD"` : Moves outflow_value once the outflow exceeds it, and nothing below it.
**Accepted**: "FACTOR" | "UPTO" | "EXCESS" | "THRESHOLD"

`# outflow_value = 1.0` : Amount of the transfer rule: a share from 0 to 1 for FACTOR, a flow rate in m3/s for UPTO, EXCESS and THRESHOLD. - or m3/s >= 0
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outflow_value`
**More**: Not calibratable: it is a coupling rule, not a hydraulic property of the reach or the lake, so letting a search move it would buy fit by reshaping how water is split between them rather than resolve streambed_k or the lake bathymetry, the actual unknowns. path = in [calibration.parameters] still reaches it for whoever wants to override this deliberately.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: >= 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: - or m3/s

`# max_bed_sag = "5 m"` : Only read when bed_incision is set. m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.max_bed_sag`
**More**: How far [L] below cell_top - bed_incision the monotone-downstream solve may sink a reach. It bounds the cumulative descent that a traced channel climbing over a rise forces on everything downstream of it. Widening it never refuses the build on its own: a reach that cannot hold the descent is warned about and pinned to the floor.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# lake_feeder_snap = "300 m"` : Max distance from a lake shoreline within which a dead-end reach is snapped to that lake via MVR (a real feeder the DEM fell short of). m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.lake_feeder_snap`
**More**: Scale it to the catchment: too large teleports an unrelated reach into the lake.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# outlet_keepout = "1000 m"` : Min distance from the model outlet a terminal reach must keep to count as a lake feeder. m expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.outlet_keepout`
**More**: A terminal closer than this is the below-dam discharge reach (the lake feeds it and it leaves the model), so it is not routed into the lake.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m

`# rectify_on_mesh = false` : Re-derive the delineated reach cells as a clean single-flow-direction (SFD) channel on the DISV mesh. expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_on_mesh`
**More**: From every delineated cell the descent D, a filled copy of the model top, is traced one neighbour at a time until it reaches a lake, the outlet of D, or an already-traced cell. The union of those paths is the channel: one cell wide (a single downstream per cell, so no braiding), continuous on the descent graph (shared faces, or shared nodes on a quad mesh), following the thalweg of D (so the surface flow follows the reach), and always reaching a real sink (no inland dead-end that leaks its flow out). The streambed top is read on the model top, never on D. D is a copy and never returns to the solver.
**Accepted**: true | false

`# rectify_stub_max_upstream = 2` : When rectify_on_mesh is set, demote a low-order parallel stub to hillslope drainage (DRN -> SFR) to thin braided bands: a reach cell with at most this many reach cells upstream of it that runs beside a reach carrying strictly more (the true channel) is dropped from SFR, keeping a one-thread channel; its water still reaches the network as routed drainage. - expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_stub_max_upstream`
**More**: 0 demotes only headwater leaves, a negative value keeps every traced cell. Default 2 removes stubs up to ~3 cells.
**Accepted**: integer
**Unit**: -

`# rectify_min_component_cells = 2` : When rectify_on_mesh is set, drop a whole reach component smaller than this many cells (a lone one-cell stream that just touches a lake or the outlet is hillslope drainage, not a channel, and reads as a spurious SFR -> lake entry). - expert
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.rectify_min_component_cells`
**More**: Its water still reaches the network as routed DRN. Default 2 drops single-cell components; 1 keeps every component.
**Accepted**: integer
**Unit**: -

## `[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.runoff]`

Overland runoff that enters the network, as a volume per time (m3/s in SI), shared over the reaches by length.

Connections found in the code (2)
- Same name `[data.runoff]` Runoff configuration (surface runoff time series). Read when `data.types` lists `"runoff"`.
- Same name `[flow.sinks_sources.lakes.<name>.runoff]` Runoff that enters the lake over time, as a volume per time (m3/s in SI). `kind` = `"constant"` | `"csv"` | `"piecewise"` | `"seasonal"`

`kind` selects the shape of this table. One tab per shape, the default first.

“constant”
[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.runoff]

`kind = "constant"` : One value applied to every stress period. chosen shape
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.runoff.kind`
**Values**:
- `"constant"` : One value applied to every stress period.
- `"csv"` : A dated record read from a CSV file and aligned on the stress periods.
- `"piecewise"` : Ordered dated segments, each a constant or a csv.
- `"seasonal"` : Calendar month or season to value, repeated across the years.
**Accepted**: "constant" | "csv" | "piecewise" | "seasonal"

`value = "2 mm/day"` : Value applied to every stress period. required in units, or m3/s, m/s, m by mount example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.runoff.value`
**More**: A text carries its unit, such as '2 mm/day' or '100 m**3/day'. A bare number is in the unit that units names, else in the unit its table reads: m3/s for a flow, m/s for a rate on a surface, m for a head. The sign follows the table: a well rate is negative when it pumps, and a rate whose name says its direction, such as a withdrawal or an evaporation, is zero or more.
**Accepted**: number or string
**Unit**: in units, or m3/s, m/s, m by mount
**Example**: `"2 mm/day"`, `-0.001`
**Only if**: kind = "constant"

`# units = ‹string›` : Unit of the values: a volume per time such as 'm3/day' for a flow, a length per time such as 'mm/day' for a rate on a surface, a length for a head.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.runoff.units`
**More**: Values are converted to SI when the run starts. Unset, a well forcing takes the well's units, a boundary head the boundary's, and the others read SI.
**Accepted**: string

## `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]`

An SFR-to-SFR diversion: a controlled split from one reach to another.

Repeat the table: one `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]` block per item.

[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions]]

`reach = 12` : Number of the reach the diversion leaves from, counted from 1. required - >= 1 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.reach`
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `12`

`to_reach = 13` : Number of the reach that receives the diversion, counted from 1. required - >= 1 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.to_reach`
**More**: It must be a downstream connection of reach.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `13`

`# cprior = "FRACTION"` : How much of the flow leaving reach the diversion takes, given divflow.
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.diversions.cprior`
**Values**:
- `"FRACTION"` : Takes the share divflow (from 0 to 1) of the flow.
- `"EXCESS"` : Takes only the part of the flow above divflow.
- `"THRESHOLD"` : Takes divflow once the flow reaches it, and nothing below it.
- `"UPTO"` : Takes the flow, capped at divflow.
**Accepted**: "FRACTION" | "EXCESS" | "THRESHOLD" | "UPTO"

## `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches]]`

One explicit reach row, used to bypass automatic network delineation.

Repeat the table: one `[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches]]` block per item.

[[flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches]]

`length = "250 m"` : Length of the reach along the channel, in meters (rlen of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.length`
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"250 m"`

`width = "3 m"` : Width of the channel of the reach, in meters (rwid of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.width`
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"3 m"`

`slope = 0.002` : Slope of the reach bed, in metres of drop per metre of length (rgrd of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required - > 0 example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.slope`
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -
**Example**: `0.002`

`top = "42 m"` : Elevation of the streambed top of the reach, in meters (rtp of MODFLOW 6 SFR). required m example value
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.sfr.<name>.reaches.top`
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"42 m"`

`# upstream = []` : 1-based ids of reaches whose downstream end feeds this reach.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/geographic.html -->
# `[geographic]`

Geographic configuration for watershed delineation.

- `geographic`[table] · required in every file · 43 user keys, 10 dev or expert
- Start a file: `hmp config template --modules geographic` (download it), then `hmp check file.toml`. Minimal file
[geographic]

`# source_mode = "standard"` : Where the model domain comes from.
**Path**: `geographic.source_mode`
**More**: 'standard' delineates it from a DEM, an outlet or a polygon ([geographic.catchment]). 'synthetic' builds one analytical support from [geographic.synthetic].
**Values**:
- `"standard"`
- `"synthetic"`
**Accepted**: "standard" | "synthetic"

`# crs_project = ‹string›` : Target projected CRS for all outputs (e.g. 'EPSG:2154').
**Path**: `geographic.crs_project`
**More**: If not set, derived from the input DEM.
**Accepted**: string

`# dem_correc_type = "fill"` : How the DEM is conditioned before the catchment is delineated.
**Path**: `geographic.dem_correc_type`
**More**: 'fill' (default) only raises cells: each closed depression is raised to its spill level, then a small gradient on the flats lets every cell drain. 'breach' mostly lowers cells: it carves a path through the barrier that closes a depression, after raising single-cell pits to their lowest neighbour, with no limit on length or depth and no fill afterwards (least-cost breaching, Lindsay 2016); it changes far fewer cells than 'fill' and can dig deep. 'capped_breach' lowers and raises: it breaches only within the limits of [geographic.capped_breach] (a maximum cumulative lowering and a maximum length, in metres), then fills every depression the limits refused (the hybrid of Lindsay 2016). The depth limit is a sum over the cells of a path, so it does not give the same landscape at every grid resolution. 'fill' is the default because it is the tool of the paper behind the network criterion (FillDepressions, Abherve et al. 2023), and the criterion itself fills the model top on the mesh by a priority flood: one conditioning rule from the DEM to the score. A DEM declared state = "conditioned" on its [[data.dem.sources]] entry is already conditioned, so this key is ignored and the run records 'provided'.
**Values**:
- `"breach"`
- `"fill"`
- `"capped_breach"`
**Accepted**: "breach" | "fill" | "capped_breach"

`# terrain_engine = ‹string›` : Flow-routing engine that conditions the DEM and delineates the catchment.
**Path**: `geographic.terrain_engine`
**More**: Unset uses the engine this build defaults to. A string and not an enumeration: the values that resolve depend on what is installed beside HydroModPy, which is how a third-party engine is named without a patch.
**Accepted**: string

`# domain_extent = "box"` : Selects the DEM surface used for the domain. experimental
**Path**: `geographic.domain_extent`
**More**: 'box' (default) keeps the full buffered rectangular support. 'watershed' / 'watershed_buff' select the catchment (optionally with a buffer ring) surface. Note: the MODFLOW 6 mesh still covers the buffered box (the buffer stays active for inter-basin exchange); out-of-watershed drainage is kept out of the catchment discharge by the DRN watershed-routing, not by an idomain mask.
**Values**:
- `"box"`
- `"watershed_buff"`
- `"watershed"`
**Accepted**: "box" | "watershed_buff" | "watershed"

`# write_intermediates = false` : Keep intermediate rasters and shapefiles on disk after geographic preprocessing. dev
**Path**: `geographic.write_intermediates`
**More**: When false (default), .hmp/scratch/<run>/_preprocessing/ is removed after ingestion into the run field store.

## `[geographic.catchment]`

How the model domain is defined.

Connections found in the code (2)

- The code says `geographic.crossings.path`: A crossings API source can only feed the notch when geographic.catchment.x_outlet / y_outlet are declared, since the watershed that would otherwise give the download box is not delineated yet. Declare geographic.crossings.path explicitly instead.

[geographic.catchment]

**Path**: `geographic.catchment.kind`
**Values**:

- `"txt"` : Model domain defined from an XYZ text grid plus a cell size.

**More**: The routing surface, the catchment, the mesh and the model top all take it. Unset keeps the pixel of the DEM file, which is what the mesh follows otherwise: 25 m for a BD ALTI download. Second of three sizes, each read from the one before: data.dem.sources.resolution_m says what a provider serves, this key what the run works on, and mesh.cell_size what the model solves on. Aggregation only: each coarse cell is the mean of the fine pixels it covers, nodata left out, on a grid aligned on the upper-left corner of the DEM; a value finer than the DEM's own pixel is refused when the run starts. The DEM file is not changed, the aggregated copy lives in the geographic products of the run.
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"75 m"`

`buff_area = "10%"` : Margin around the watershed polygon. required example value
**Path**: `geographic.catchment.buff_area`
**More**: A percentage ('10%') enlarges the catchment AREA by that share, the rule of Abherve et al. (2023): the distance is solved on the real polygon, then snapped to the DEM grid. A length ('500 m', '2 km') is an explicit distance, snapped to the DEM grid like the percentage. '10% of sqrt(area)' is the rule of version 1 written out, 10 per cent of the square root of the catchment area, about 50 per cent more area on a real catchment. A bare number (5) still reads as that rule, so a sealed run replays its domain; the explicit form with the same distance says the same thing.
**Accepted**: number or string
**Example**: `"10%"`
**Only if**: kind = "from_outlet_coord" | "from_polyg_shp"

`# dem_resolution = "75 m"` : Cell size the DEM is aggregated to before anything is delineated, a length ('75 m', a bare number in metres). m example value

**Unit**: m
**Example**: `"75 m"`

`# snap_method = "window"` : Where the outlet lands inside the window of snap_dist.
**Path**: `geographic.catchment.snap_method`
**More**: 'window' (default) takes the cell with the largest flow accumulation, so it can land on a larger stream that lies in the window beside the one the outlet was declared on. 'jenson' takes the nearest cell of the stream network drawn from the DEM (Jenson and Domingue 1988, as used by Lindsay, Rothwell and Davies 2008), so it stays on the nearest stream, and it refuses an outlet with no stream cell in its window. The network is the cells that drain more than the threshold of [geographic.river_network] (threshold_area_km2 in km^2, or threshold_cells), which 'jenson' needs even when that section is not enabled. It is computed from the DEM: no observed network is read.
**Values**:
- `"window"`
- `"jenson"`
**Accepted**: "window" | "jenson"
**Only if**: kind = "from_outlet_coord"

## `[geographic.capped_breach]`

Limits of the `capped_breach` DEM conditioning, in meters.

[geographic.capped_breach]

`# max_depth = 0.5` : Largest cumulative lowering, in metres, of one breach path (the 'max_cost' of Whitebox): the lowering summed over the cells of the path, not the depth of one cell. m > 0
**Path**: `geographic.capped_breach.max_depth`
**More**: With short paths the realised maximum lowering of a cell stays close to it. On a finer grid a thick embankment spreads the cost over more cells, so it is filled instead of dug: the same value does not give the same landscape at every resolution. A depression whose cheapest breach costs more is filled. Paths overlap, so the lowering of a cell can exceed it (0.56 m for a value of 0.5 m, on a 75 m grid). The realised depth is measured after the call, logged, and warned about when it exceeds this value. Accepts inline units (e.g. 0.5, '0.5 m').
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# max_distance = 200.0` : Longest breach path, in metres. m > 0
**Path**: `geographic.capped_breach.max_distance`
**More**: Translated to the DEM grid as ceil(max_distance / cell size) cells, at least one, and counted in cells along the path: a diagonal step counts one cell, so a diagonal breach can be up to 1.41 times longer than max_distance. A depression with no way out within this length is filled. Accepts inline units (e.g. 200, '0.2 km').
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m

`# notch_width = 10.0` : Width of the notch across the embankment, in metres. m > 0
**Path**: `geographic.crossings.notch_width`
**More**: The channel pixel itself is always lowered, so a width below the cell size cuts one pixel. The width is applied along the embankment only, the run of channel pixels that stand above the bed line, never to the two pixels where the bed is read. Accepts inline units (e.g. 10, '10 m').
**Accepted**: number or "<n> m" (a bare number is read in the canonical unit)
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
