**Return type:**: DataFrame
** Run.has_table(table)[source]**: Return True when the run holds at least one row of `table`. Used by the display layer to decide whether a figure can render before calling it, so a run that never produced (for example) calibration iterations reports the figure as unavailable instead of raising mid-render.
** property Run.mass_balance: DataFrame[source]**: Mass-balance diagnostics ordered by timestep.
** property Run.metrics: DataFrame[source]**: Every score the seal of this run records, read from `manifest.json`. The runtime numbers of the solve (variable `runtime`) are not scores.
**Returns:**: pandas.DataFrame – Long-form table: `station`, `variable`, `metric`, `value` and the window each score was computed on (`window_start`, `window_end`, `n_samples`, `metric_rule_version`), then `n_clipped`, the negative values a log-scale score clipped to zero (0 on `nse_log` when none, empty on a metric that never clips), and `n_sim_nan`, the periods of the window a NaN simulated value (a dry cell) took out of the pairs. A run scored without a window carries no row, and a run that never completed has no seal and no row.
** Run.observed(variable, *, station=None, period=None)[source]**: Return observed timeseries ingested for this simulation. Observation series are persisted in the `timeseries` table of the run with `source = observed` (see `hydromodpy.data.ingest.observations.ingest_observations()`).
**Parameters:**:
- variable (str) – Canonical variable name (`discharge`, `head`, …).
- station (str, optional) – Station id to filter on. When `None`, every observed station for `variable` is returned.
- period (tuple, optional) – Window `(start, end)`, read as `timeseries()` reads it for an observation: what falls in the periods of the window, `[lo, hi)`.
**Returns:**: pd.DataFrame – Long-form frame with columns `station_id`, `datetime`, `value`. Datetimes are tz-naive UTC.
**Raises:**: ValueError – When no observation rows match the filter.
**Return type:**: DataFrame
** property Run.parameters: DataFrame[source]**: Calibratable parameters persisted for this run. Returns a `DataFrame` indexed by `param_name` (or by the `(param_name, zone_id)` MultiIndex when a parameter is zonal) with columns `value`, `unit`, `parameterization`. Homogeneous scalars are trivially looked up via `run.parameters.loc["thickness", "value"]`.
** Run.recharge_forcing()[source]**: Input recharge rate of the model domain per stress period, in m/s.
** Run.score(windows=None, metrics=None, months=None, station=None)[source]**: Score the stored series of this run again, on any window, after the fact. No model is run: the series come from `timeseries.parquet` and are paired as the seal pairs them, a simulated stamp closing its period.
**Parameters:**:
- windows (Mapping[str, tuple[Any, Any]] | Sequence[DateWindow] | None) – `{name: (start, end)}` with ISO dates, either bound `None` for open, or a list of `DateWindow`. `None` scores the `[metrics]` window of the seal.
- metrics (Sequence[str] | None) – Names of the metric table. `None` means every metric a series pair can give. A network metric is refused, and so is a metric that needs consecutive days when `months` is set.
- months (Sequence[int] | None) – Calendar months, 1 to 12, that the paired periods must fall in.
- station (str | None) – Score only this station. `None` scores every observed station the run simulates.
**Returns:**: pandas.DataFrame – One row per station, variable, metric and window: `sim_id`, `run`, `station`, `variable`, `metric`, `window_name`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `months`, `value`, `n_samples`, `n_sim_nan`.
**Return type:**: DataFrame
** Run.score_network(output=None, window=None)[source]**: Score the stream-network criterion of this run again, as its trial scored it. No model is run. The release field, the mesh, the maps and the criterion recharge come from the store, and the settings from the network output the run sealed, or the defaults of that output when it sealed none. The value is the one a calibration trial gives at the same parameters and window.
**Parameters:**:
- output (str | None) – The sealed network output to read. `None` reads the only one, or the defaults.
- window (tuple[Any, Any] | Mapping[str, tuple[Any, Any]] | None) – `(start, end)` or `{name: (start, end)}`, ISO dates, either bound `None` for open. It picks the complete years of the two-bound mode. `None` reads the window the run was scored with, else every year. One state reads no window.
**Returns:**: pandas.DataFrame – One row per quantity: `sim_id`, `run`, `output`, `mode` (`one_state` or `two_bounds`), `window_name`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `bound` (`minimal`, `maximal`, a validation map, or empty), `year` (empty for the climatological value), `quantity` (`J_signed`, `D_so`, `D_os`, `D_optim`, `r_optim_valid`, `n_years_scored`, …) and `value`.
**Return type:**: DataFrame
** Run.stations(variable, *, source='simulated')[source]**: Return the sorted station ids carrying one variable, simulated by default. Lets a caller enumerate multi-station families (one `reach_id` station per SFR reach, gauge ids, …) before fetching each series with `timeseries()`. `source="observed"` lists the gauges that measure it.
** property Run.time_index: DatetimeIndex**: Datetime index aligned with the simulation’s stress periods. Length matches `run.n_timesteps`. Each stamp is the END of its period, as the solvers write it. The solver’s CF `/time` axis is read first; without it the stamps are rebuilt from the `period_start`, `period_end` and `time_unit` the run states about itself. A steady run without `[simulation.time]` records no step count and holds one state: its index is the one stamp the solver wrote on its axis, a clock with no calendar that starts at 1970-01-01, so every reader gets one stamp per stored state. Raises if the bounds are missing or a transient simulation has no timesteps.
** Run.timeseries(
variable,
*,
station=None,
period=None,
downsample=None,
n_out=None,
source='simulated', )[source]**: Return one time series, simulated unless `source` says otherwise.
**Parameters:**:
- variable (str) – Catalog variable name, such as `"discharge"` or `"head"`.
- station (str | None) – Station id stored in the timeseries table. Left `None`, it is the only station of the variable, or the whole catchment when it has one. A run with several observed piezometers or lakes stores a series for each, and the catchment has none for a head or a stage, so those reads need `station`; the error lists the ids.
- period (tuple | str | None) – Optional window, `(start, end)` or a year as text (`"2002"`). It keeps the stress periods it overlaps, as a field or a CSV export reads it: a simulated value by its stamp, `(lo, hi]`, an observation by its date, `[lo, hi)`. One date reads the period that date reads.
- downsample (str | None) – Optional decimation strategy. `"lttb"` runs Largest Triangle Three Buckets on the series; `"auto"` enables LTTB only when the series exceeds 50_000 points; `None` (default) returns the untouched full-resolution series.
- n_out (int | None) – Target sample count for `downsample="lttb"` or `"auto"`. Defaults to `5000`.
- source (str) – `"simulated"`, the default, or `"observed"` for the measurement of the same variable.
**Returns:**: pandas.Series – Time-indexed values with timezone-normalized UTC timestamps.
**Raises:**: KeyError – Raised when no matching time series exists.
**Return type:**: Series

** class RunSet(sim_ids, catalog, *, render=None)[source]**: Collection view over several simulations from one catalog. `RunSet` is returned by catalog queries that match more than one run. It behaves like a lightweight list of `Run` objects and adds cohort utilities: pivot parameter tables, read the metrics of each run under its rule, rank runs, compare one metric, export a wide DataFrame, and stack fields lazily. Runs scored under different rules (station, variable, window, rule version) are not ranked together unless asked (`mixed_windows=True`).
**Parameters:**:
- sim_ids (list[str]) – Ordered simulation ids in the group.
- catalog (Catalog) – Catalog used to resolve ids into `Run` objects and tabular data.
- render (Renderer | None) – The function that draws a figure of the set. Without one the set takes the one of its catalog, and `figure` is refused when there is none.
Examples

```
>>> group = catalog.find(project="my_project")
>>> group.count
>>> group.best("nse").summary()
```

See also
**`hydromodpy.results.run.view.Run`**: Per-simulation view yielded during iteration.
**`hydromodpy.results.catalog.facade.Catalog`**: Catalog that creates simulation groups.
** best(metric, *, mixed_windows=False)[source]**: Return the run with the best value for `metric`. Best follows the direction of the metric: the highest `nse`, the lowest `rmse`, the `pbias` closest to zero. The metric is read at the gauge of each run, in the window of its rule.
**Raises:**:
- ValueError – Raised when the group is empty, or when the metric has no declared direction (`UnrankedMetricError`).
- MixedWindowsError – Raised when the runs were scored under different rules (station, variable, window or rule version) and `mixed_windows` is false.
- KeyError – Raised when no run of the group carries the metric, for instance when no run declares a `[metrics] window`.
** compare(metric, *, mixed_windows=False)[source]**: Compare one metric across the runs of the group, best first. The metric is read at the gauge of each run, in the window of its rule (`metrics`). Best follows the direction of the metric.
**Parameters:**:
- metric (str) – Metric name, as in the columns of `metrics`.
- mixed_windows (bool) – Rank runs scored under different rules: another station, variable, window or rule version. Refused by default: such values are not comparable.
**Returns:**: pandas.DataFrame – `sim_id`, `name`, `project`, `solver`, `station`, `variable`, the window columns and `value`, best first. Runs without the metric are left out.
**Return type:**: DataFrame
** figure( name=None, *, request=None, draw=None, save=None, dpi=None, theme=None, engine=None, time=None, data=False, **options, )[source]**: Draw the registered `runset` figure name of this set, `ensemble_band` for one. The arguments are those of `hydromodpy.results.run.view.Run.figure()`. A figure of another subject refuses the set.
**Raises:**: hydromodpy.core.exceptions.CommandUsageError – If the set was not opened by `hydromodpy.open` or a project.
** filter(**criteria)[source]**: Intersect with another `catalog.find(**criteria)` call. Equivalent to `catalog.find(...)` but restricted to this group’s simulations. Useful for chainable exploration in notebooks.
** score(windows=None, metrics=None, months=None, station=None)[source]**: Score the stored series of every run again, on any window, after the fact. Each run follows `score()`, and the rows are stacked. The parameters of each run are added as columns, a name that clashes with a score column getting the prefix `param_`. A run that has no series at `station` or no seal gives no row, with a warning, and the call is refused when no run gives any.
** score_network(output=None, window=None)[source]**: Score the stream-network criterion of every run again, as their trials scored it. Each run follows `score_network()`, and the rows are stacked with the parameters of each run as columns. The maps of runs that share mesh, maps, recharge and settings are built once. A run that holds nothing to score gives no row, with a warning, and the call is refused when no run gives any.
** show(what, **options)[source]**: Read one thing of this set: `table` or `figure`.
** sort_by(metric, *, ascending=True, mixed_windows=False)[source]**: Return a new group ordered by the raw value of one metric.
**Parameters:**:
- metric (str) – Metric name, as in the columns of `metrics`.
- ascending (bool) – Sort from low to high when true.
- mixed_windows (bool) – Order runs scored under different rules. Refused by default.
**Returns:**: RunSet – New group containing the sorted subset that has the metric.
**Return type:**: RunSet
** table(name)[source]**: Return the table name of the set: `parameters`, `metrics` or `runs`. `parameters` is `parameters`, `metrics` is `metrics` and `runs` is `to_dataframe()` with every column. Any other name is refused with these three.
** timeseries(station=None, variable=None, source=None)[source]**: Return the stored series of every run, stacked, with `sim_id` and `run`. The columns are `sim_id`, `run` (the directory name), `station_id`, `variable`, `source` (simulated or observed), `time` and `value`. Only `timeseries.parquet` of each run is read, never a field. `station`, `variable` and `source` keep only the matching rows.
** to_csv(path)[source]**: Write `to_dataframe()` to a CSV file.
** to_dataframe(*, params=None, metrics=None)[source]**: Return a wide table joining metadata, parameters, and metrics.
**Parameters:**:
- params (list[str] | None) – Optional whitelist of parameter column names to keep after the pivot.
- metrics (list[str] | None) – Optional whitelist of metric column names to keep.
** to_xarray(variable, *, dim='run')[source]**: Return a lazy stacked `xarray.DataArray` of `variable` across sims. Each per-simulation Zarr store is opened via `Catalog.open_zarr()` and assembled into an `xarray.Dataset` by `SimulationZarr.to_xarray()` (dask-backed). Arrays are concatenated along `dim` whose coordinate values are the simulation ids. Nothing is read into memory until the caller materializes the array (`.compute()`, `.values`, slicing, etc.). Simulations that lack the variable are skipped, a store that cannot be opened with a warning; if none match, an empty `xarray.DataArray` is returned.
**Parameters:**:
- variable (str) – Public field name (as declared in the `hydromodpy.results.field_registry`).
- dim (str) – Name of the new stacking dimension (default `"sim"`).
** worst(metric, *, mixed_windows=False)[source]**: Return the run with the worst value for `metric`. The mirror of `best()`, with the same direction rule and errors.
** property count: int[source]**: Number of simulations in the group.
** property metrics: DataFrame[source]**: its metrics at the gauge, in the window of its rule. Columns: `sim_id`, `station` and `variable` of the headline NSE, the window it was computed on (`window_start`, `window_end`, `n_samples`, `metric_rule_version`), then one column per metric, named by the metric alone (`nse`, `kge`, `rmse` …). The scores come from each run’s `manifest.json`. A run without a seal, without a window or without a station has empty cells.
**Type:**: One row per run
** property parameters: DataFrame[source]**: Wide parameter table with one row per simulation.
** property sim_ids: list[str][source]**: Simulation ids in group order.

** classmethod of_run(run)[source]**: Return the session that promoted `run`, or None when no session did. The session is found from the lineage of the run (its `session_id`) among the `sessions/*/` of its project, and a kept trial under `sessions/<case>/trials/<n>` is in its own session. A session figure asked for on a run draws this session. The session opened here keeps the `read_config` of the run, so its best run validates its configuration as the run does.
** figure( name=None, *, request=None, draw=None, save=None, dpi=None, theme=None, engine=None, time=None, data=False, **options, )[source]**: Draw the registered `session` figure name of this session. ** profile()[source]**: Where the time of the search went, by step and by `reused` (`PROFILE_COLUMNS`). It adds the profile lines of every trial the journal holds, read from the last line of each trial. `lines` counts the lines added, `duration_s` sums their time and `max_rss_mb` is the peak of their memory. A trial read from the cost cache or written by a pre-release has no profile and adds nothing.

** table(name)[source]**: Return the table name of this session: `trials` or `profile`. `trials` is `trials` and `profile` is `profile()`. Any other name is refused with those two.

**Raises:**: SeveralCasesError – If the session calibrates several cases: read `best_by_case`.

| `to_dict` | method | Return the outcome as JSON: the cycles, `restart_from` and the warning to give. |
| `production_sim_id` | attribute | Id of the production run chained after the loop (`--then-run`), else None. |

** class SpinupResult(converged, cycles, restart_from, production_sim_id=None)[source]**: Outcome of a spin-up loop. `restart_from` is the converged (or last) cycle’s Zarr path, ready to feed a production run’s `[flow] restart_from`.
** antecedent_warning()[source]**: Return what to say before this state is used as an antecedent. A loop that ran out of cycles still hands back its last state, and a production run seeded from it produces a result that looks exactly like one seeded from a settled aquifer. Whoever uses it has to be told.
** to_dict()[source]**: Return the outcome as JSON: the cycles, `restart_from` and the warning to give. A cycle gives its `index`, `d_head` and `d_stage`. `warning` is `antecedent_warning()`, `None` for a loop that converged.
** converged: bool**: True when a cycle changed the heads and the lake stages by less than the tolerances. False when the loop ran out of cycles first.
** cycles: list[SpinupCycle]**: Every cycle that ran, in order.
** property n_cycles: int[source]**: Number of cycles that ran.
** production_sim_id: str | None = None**: Id of the production run chained after the loop (`--then-run`), else None.
** restart_from: str**: `fields.zarr` path of the converged cycle, or of the last one.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/Workspace.html -->
# `Workspace`

| Member | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `projects` | property | Names of the projects of the workspace, by name. |
| `root` | property | The workspace root. |
| `runs` | method | Return the sealed runs of every project, one row each, narrowed by each filter. |
| `score` | method | Run `RunSet.score` on the runs of every project, with a `project` column first. |
| `score_network` | method | Run `RunSet.score_network` on every project, with a `project` column first. |

** class Workspace(root)[source]**: Read-only view of a workspace: its projects and the sealed runs they hold. The runs are read from the `tables.parquet/simulation.parquet` row each sealed run carries (`hydromodpy.results.catalog.federation.read_workspace_runs()`), so no project index is needed. `workspace["<project>"]` opens one project as `hmp.open` does.
**Parameters:**: root (str | Path) – The workspace root, the folder of `workspace.toml` or of `projects/`.
**Raises:**: FileNotFoundError – If `root` holds neither `workspace.toml` nor `projects/`.
** runs(*, site=None, project=None)[source]**: Return the sealed runs of every project, one row each, narrowed by each filter. Columns are those of `simulation.parquet` plus `project_root`. The label is computed by a project index, so it is not a column here.
** score(*args, **kwargs)[source]**: Run `RunSet.score` on the runs of every project, with a `project` column first. The arguments are those of `hydromodpy.results.run.group.RunSet.score()`. A project with nothing to score gives no row, with a warning.
** score_network(*args, **kwargs)[source]**: Run `RunSet.score_network` on every project, with a `project` column first. The arguments are those of `hydromodpy.results.run.group.RunSet.score_network()`.
** property projects: list[str][source]**: Names of the projects of the workspace, by name.
** property root: Path[source]**: The workspace root.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/exceptions.html -->
# Exceptions and error codes

The classes of `hydromodpy.core.exceptions` all derive from `HydroModPyError`. Each one carries a `code` of the form `HMPY.Exxx`, a one-line `title()`, and `to_dict()`, which renders the failure as a typed problem object. A few errors are defined beside the code that raises them (last section), and some calls raise built-in exceptions such as `FileNotFoundError`. The hierarchy is at the top level of the package:

```
try:
    hmp.run("path/to/config.toml")
except hmp.ConfigError as err:
    print(err.code, err)   # HMPY.E100, or the code of a subclass
```

Catching a parent class catches its subclasses. The command line maps each class to an exit code: Exit codes. To look up a code you met, find its row in the table: `HMPY.E405` is one row.

<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-calibrate.html -->
# `hmp.calibrate()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp calibrate`
- Returns `CalibrationReport`, `CalibrationPlan`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** calibrate(
source,
*,
base=None,
phase=None,
dry_run=False,
preflight=True,
case=None,
method=None,
max_trials=None,
seed=None,
save_runs=None,
objective=None,
project=None,
workspace=None,
resume=False,
force=False,
report=True,
headless=True,
environment=None, )[source]**: Run the calibration a configuration declares, or say what it would run. A path with no `base` goes to `calibrate_a_file` and builds no project. A document in memory, or a path read against `base`, opens a `Project` and runs `Project.calibrate`. A configuration that declares `[[calibration.phases]]` runs each phase in turn. A script that calibrates with `parallel` above 1 needs the `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, because the workers start in spawn. `dry_run=True` runs nothing and writes nothing: it returns the `CalibrationPlan` of `calibration_plan(source, *, workspace=None, check=False) -> CalibrationPlan`, whose `phases`, `calibration`, `protocol` and `plan` say what the configuration declares and what a launch would write.
**Parameters:**:
- source (Source) – A calibration TOML file, a document as a mapping or JSON text, a validated `HydroModPyConfig`, or a run request, whose `set`, `phase`, `name`, `resume`, `force` and `dry_run` steer the call as the keywords do.
- base (PathLike | None) – The folder the relative paths of the document are read from, and the project the sessions are written in.
- phase (str | None) – Run only the named phase of a staged calibration.
- dry_run (bool) – Say what would run, and run nothing.
- preflight (bool) – With `dry_run`, run first the checks a launch runs, so a file they refuse raises. False reads the declaration only.
- case (str | None) – Name of the session of a calibration held in memory. A file names its case with `[simulation] name`.
- method (str | None) – The search of a calibration held in memory, over its `[calibration]`.
- max_trials (int | None) – The search of a calibration held in memory, over its `[calibration]`.
- seed (int | None) – The search of a calibration held in memory, over its `[calibration]`.
- save_runs (str | None) – The search of a calibration held in memory, over its `[calibration]`.
- objective (str | None) – Name of the objective block to optimize.
- project (str | None) – Label of the project in the session record.
- workspace (PathLike | None) – The project root a file calibration writes in, over the folder of the file.
- resume (bool) – Continue an interrupted session.
- force (bool) – Run again a session identical to a completed one.
- report (bool) – Write the report of each session once the search is over.
- headless (bool) – Draw no figure while the calibration runs.
- environment (Environment | None) – The environment of the call. `None` builds the default of the machine.
**Returns:**: CalibrationReport or CalibrationPlan – What the calibration found, or with `dry_run` what it would run.
**Raises:**:
- FileNotFoundError – If the calibration TOML path does not exist.
- hydromodpy.core.exceptions.ConfigError – If the configuration cannot be read, the preflight refuses it, or an option of a calibration held in memory is given for a file.
- hydromodpy.core.exceptions.CalibrationError – If a phase is unknown, or the search fails.
**Return type:**: CalibrationReport | CalibrationPlan
Examples

```
>>> import hydromodpy as hmp
>>> report = hmp.calibrate("calibration.toml")
>>> plan = hmp.calibrate("calibration.toml", dry_run=True)
```

## Keyword arguments and command-line flags

The twin command is `hmp calibrate`.

| Keyword | Default | Command-line flag | Accepted by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `phase` | `None` | `--phase` | every form |
| `dry_run` | `False` | `--dry-run` | every form |
| `preflight` | `True` | no flag | every form |
| `case` | `None` | `--case` | every form |
| `method` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `max_trials` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `seed` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `save_runs` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `objective` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `project` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `workspace` | `None` | `-w``--workspace` | every form |
| `resume` | `False` | `--resume` | every form |
| `force` | `False` | no flag | every form |
| `report` | `True` | `--no-report`(the flag turns it off) | every form |
| `headless` | `True` | no flag | every form |
| `environment` | `None` | no flag | every form |

Flags of `hmp calibrate` with no keyword: `--list-phases`, `--expand`. To get their effect from Python, build the configuration object with the values you want, or write them in the TOML file.


<!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-check.html -->
# `hmp.check()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp check`, `hmp run`
- Returns `Diagnostic`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** check(
source,
*,
base=None,
partial=True,
inputs=False,
overlays=(),
set=None,
environment=None, )[source]**: Check a configuration, a draft or a file, and return every diagnostic it holds. A mapping is checked as it stands, as a form being filled would be, against the `base` its relative paths are read from: a mapping without one is refused, as `load()` refuses it. A path is read as `hmp run` reads it: the `base_config` chain, the project root, the name of the workflow. A `[sites]` project is expanded case by case, and each issue comes back at the key it reaches. A calibration with nothing to fix and nothing to fill is also read by its preflight.
**Parameters:**:
- source (str | PathLike[str] | Mapping[str, Any]) – A path to a TOML file, or the document as a mapping of sections.
- base (str | PathLike[str] | None) – The folder relative paths are read from. A mapping needs it.
- partial (bool) – True reports a required key not written yet as `to_fill`, which stops nothing. False reports it as an `error`, what `hmp run` refuses.
- inputs (bool) – True also reads the header of each input file the document names, and downloads nothing.
- overlays (Sequence[str | PathLike[str]]) – TOML files merged over a file, then dotted paths and their values, as `hmp run --overlay` and `--set`. A mapping refuses both.
- set (Mapping[str, Any] | None) – TOML files merged over a file, then dotted paths and their values, as `hmp run --overlay` and `--set`. A mapping refuses both.
- environment (Environment | None) – The bounds an input header may be read within. The default is the bounds of a bare `Environment`.
**Returns:**: list of Diagnostic – Empty when the document loads and every rule passes. A diagnostic of a file carries `line_number`.
**Raises:**: TypeError – When source is neither a mapping nor a path.
**Return type:**: list[Diagnostic]

## Keyword arguments and command-line flags

The twin command is `hmp check`.

| Keyword | Default | Command-line flag | Accepted by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `partial` | `True` | `--partial` | every form |
| `inputs` | `False` | `--inputs` | every form |
| `overlays` | `()` | no flag | every form |
| `set` | `None` | no flag | every form |
| `environment` | `None` | no flag | every form |

Flags of `hmp check` with no keyword: `--lang`. To get their effect from Python, build the configuration object with the values you want, or write them in the TOML file.

# `hmp.compare()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp diff`
- Returns `Comparison`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** compare(refs, *, variables=None, out=None, by='run', workspace=None)[source]**: Compare sealed runs, the first one as the reference. A reference is a run directory, a run name or a recipe of the project (its latest run of each case), or the run. `Comparison.table` sets the parameters and the metrics of the runs side by side.
**Parameters:**:
- refs (Sequence[Ref]) – The runs to compare, the reference first.
- variables (Sequence[str] | None) – The variables to compare. `None` takes those the runs share.
- out (PathLike | None) – Write the comparison to this folder.
- by (Literal['run', 'site']) – `"site"` compares the runs of each site the references hold and joins their scores; it needs `out` and returns the folder written.
- workspace (PathLike | None) – The project directory, or a folder inside it.
**Returns:**: Comparison or pathlib.Path – The comparison, or the folder written with `by="site"`.
**Raises:**:
- hydromodpy.project.compare.ComparisonReferenceError – If a reference names no sealed run.
- hydromodpy.project.compare.ComparisonCaseError – If the runs cannot be compared.
**Return type:**: Comparison | Path

# `hmp.example()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp example`
- Returns `ExampleEntry`, `ExampleEntry`, `InstallReport`, `InstallReport`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** example(
name=None,
*,
add=False,
workspace=None,
ref=None,
force=False, )[source]**: List the examples this build ships, show some, or install one, several or all.
**Parameters:**:
- name (str | Sequence[str] | None) – The example id, or a list of ids. Without it, every example.
- add (bool) – Install the examples: fetch what is missing from the content-addressed cache, check every file against its sha256, and write the configs under `projects/<directory>/` and the data under `data/<variable>/`.
- workspace (PathLike | None) – Workspace root an example is installed in. Defaults to `~/hydromodpy`.
- ref (str | None) – Git ref to fetch from. Defaults to `v` plus the installed version.
- force (bool) – Overwrite a file whose content differs from the manifest.
**Returns:**: tuple of ExampleEntry or ExampleEntry or InstallReport or tuple of InstallReport – One value for one id given as text, a tuple for a list of ids or for none.
**Return type:**: tuple[ExampleEntry, …] | ExampleEntry | InstallReport | tuple[InstallReport, …]
Examples

```
>>> import hydromodpy as hmp
>>> [entry.id for entry in hmp.example()]
>>> hmp.example("04", add=True).project_dir
>>> hmp.example(["00", "07"], add=True)
```

# `hmp.export()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp export`
- Returns `PublishedLine`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** export(
ref: str | PathLike[str] | Run | Session | RunSet | Project,
variable: str | list[str] | None = None,
*,
deliver: Literal[False] = False,
**options: Any, ) → list[Path][source]**:
** export(
ref: str | PathLike[str] | Run | Session | RunSet | Project,
variable: None = None,
*,
deliver: Literal[True],
**options: Any, ) → tuple[PublishedLine, ...]**: Export data of a run to files, or deliver what its `[[export]]` blocks name. The words of an `[[export]]` block and of `hmp export`: `variable` says what (a name, a list, or `"all"`), `time` or `period` when, `folder` or `file` where. The format follows the data unless `format` or the extension of `file` names one. Files land in `runs/<run>/exports/` and are recorded in `exports/index.json`.
**Parameters:**:
- ref (Ref) – The run: its directory, its name in `workspace`, or the run.
- variable (str | list[str] | None) – What to export.
- deliver (bool) – Send what the `[[export]]` blocks of the run name, and take no other word.
- workspace (PathLike | None) – The project directory, or a folder inside it.
- environment (Environment | None) – A `folder` or `file` must sit under the roots its bounds allow. `None` keeps the default of the machine, which checks nothing.
**Returns:**: list of pathlib.Path or tuple of PublishedLine – The files written, or with `deliver` the delivery lines.
**Raises:**: hydromodpy.core.exceptions.ExportError – If `variable` is missing, or `deliver` comes with another word.
**Return type:**: list[Path] | tuple[PublishedLine, …]
Examples

```
>>> import hydromodpy as hmp
>>> hmp.export("runs/transient_nwt", "all", workspace="~/ws/p")
>>> hmp.export(run, deliver=True)
```

## Keyword arguments and command-line flags

The twin command is `hmp export`.

| Keyword | Default | Command-line flag | Accepted by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | `None` | `--time` | every form |
| `period` | `None` | `--period` | every form |
| `format` | `None` | `--as` | every form |
| `folder` | `None` | `--to` | every form |
| `file` | `None` | `--to` | every form |
| `crs` | `None` | `--crs` | every form |
| `resolution` | `None` | `--resolution` | every form |
| `layer` | `None` | `--layer` | every form |
| `nodata` | `-9999.0` | `--nodata` | every form |
| `deliver` | `False` | `--deliver` | every form |
| `workspace` | `None` | `-w``--workspace` | every form |
| `environment` | `None` | no flag | every form |

Flags of `hmp export` with no keyword: `--list`, `--regen`. To get their effect from Python, build the configuration object with the values you want, or write them in the TOML file.

# `hmp.open()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp show`, `hmp export`
- Returns `Project`, `Run`, `Session`, `Workspace`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** open(path)[source]**: Open what a path stands for: a project, a run, a session or a workspace.
- a project directory, its `project.toml` or any folder inside it gives a `Project`, read only;
- a run directory gives a `Run`, partial before its seal (`record`, `checks`, `inputs` and `label()` refuse);
- a session directory (`sessions/<name>`) gives a `Session`;
- a workspace root (`workspace.toml` or `projects/`) gives a `Workspace`.
A run and a session are given `hydromodpy.project.show.render()`, so `run.figure(name)` draws. They are opened by `open_run_dir(path, *, read_config, render)` and `Session(path, *, read_config, render)`.
**Parameters:**: path (PathLike) – The directory or file.
**Returns:**: Project or Run or Session or Workspace – What the path stands for.
**Raises:**:
- FileNotFoundError – If the path does not exist, or stands for none of the above.
- hydromodpy.results.errors.RunNotSealedError – If the path is a run directory that wrote no facts.
**Return type:**: Project | Run | Session | Workspace
Examples

```
>>> import hydromodpy as hmp
>>> proj = hmp.open("~/ws/projects/bretagne_k")
>>> run = hmp.open("~/ws/projects/bretagne_k/runs/J0014010-base")
```

# `hmp.run()`

Found in the code
- Command line `hmp run`
- Returns `RunOutcome`, `PlanDraft`, `OverviewResult`
- Defined in `hydromodpy/project/api.py`
** run(
source,
*,
base=None,
set=None,
name=None,
force=False,
fresh=False,
resume=None,
from_step=None,
until_step=None,
dry_run=False,
frozen=False,
no_display=False,
headless=False,
environment=None, )[source]**: Run a simulation or an overview. What comes back follows the workflow of the configuration:
- a simulation gives its `RunOutcome`, whose `open()` gives the run, or `None` when no directory was claimed;
- an overview gives a `OverviewResult`;
- `dry_run=True` gives a `PlanDraft`, with nothing run and nothing written.
A calibration is refused, `calibrate()` runs it. A `[sites]` project is refused too, `Project.launch` runs it. A simulation identical to a completed run of the project (same resolved configuration, same name) is not computed again: its outcome names the completed run in `identical_to` and a warning says so. `force=True` computes it anyway.
**Parameters:**:
- source (Source) – A TOML file, a JSON run request, a document as a mapping or JSON text, a `HydroModPyConfig`, or a `RunRequest`.
- base (PathLike | None) – The folder the relative paths of the document are read from, and the project the run is written in. A file reads them from the project root above it. A mapping, JSON text or a request object is refused without one.
- set (Mapping[str, Any] | None) – Changes of the configuration, by dotted path (`--set`) or by a name of `hmp config targets`. Sealed in `lineage.overrides`.
- name (str | None) – Name of the run.
- force (bool) – Compute a run identical to a completed one, and claim a stale case.
- fresh (bool) – File what a previous attempt left under `attempts/<k>/` and start over.
- resume (str | None) – Name of an interrupted case to continue in place, `<chain>_w<N>` for a window of a chain.
- from_step (str | None) – Bounds of a partial run, names of pipeline steps.
- until_step (str | None) – Bounds of a partial run, names of pipeline steps.
- dry_run (bool) – Say what this configuration would run, and run nothing.
- frozen (bool) – Require frozen input data references: a project TOML answers to its lockfile, the `config.toml` of a run to the record of that run.
- no_display (bool) – Draw no figure. Neither enters the identity of the run.
- headless (bool) – Draw no figure. Neither enters the identity of the run.
- environment (Environment | None) – The environment of the call. `None` builds the default of the machine.
**Returns:**: RunOutcome or PlanDraft or OverviewResult or None – See above.
**Raises:**:
- FileNotFoundError – If the TOML path does not exist.
- hydromodpy.core.exceptions.ConfigError – If the document fails validation, declares a calibration or a `[sites]` project, takes an option its workflow refuses, or comes in memory without `base`.
- hydromodpy.core.exceptions.PipelineError – If a step raises.
- hydromodpy.core.exceptions.SolverError – If the solver fails.
**Return type:**: RunOutcome | PlanDraft | OverviewResult | None
Examples

```
>>> import hydromodpy as hmp
>>> outcome = hmp.run("run_transient_nwt.toml", name="baseline")
>>> run = outcome.open()
>>> plan = hmp.run("run_transient_nwt.toml", dry_run=True)
```

| `frozen` | `False` | `--frozen` | every form |
| `no_display` | `False` | `--no-display` | every form |
| `headless` | `False` | no flag | every form |

**options: Any, ) → dict[str, Any] | pd.DataFrame**: Read one thing of a run, a session, a set of runs or a project. `what` names a line of `hydromodpy.project.show.SHOWN`: `summary` (run, session, project) a dict of facts; `profile` (run, session) where the time went; `table` (run, session, set) the sealed table `name`; `field` and `series` (run) the variable `name` at `time`, `layer`, `sel`, `bbox`; `point` (run) the variables `name` in the cell `point` (`x`, `y`, `cell`, `depth`, `label`) at `layer` and the time step `time`; `rank` (project) the `limit` best runs on `metric` at `station`, the worst with `best=False`; `figure` (run, session, set) the figure `name` with `dpi`, `time` and the figure’s `options`; `report` (run, session) the report, with `preset`, `station`, `strict`. <!-- https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/objects.html -->
# Objects and how they relate

A run is a folder on disk: field arrays in Zarr, tables in Parquet, under `<project>/runs/<name>/`. The DuckDB index of the project is derived from those folders and can be rebuilt with `hmp catalog reindex`. The objects below are the ways Python looks at that folder.

| Object | What it is | You get it from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Catalog` | Read-only view of a project index. | built by the other objects |
| `Run` | Read one persisted simulation from a HydroModPy catalog. | `hmp.open()`, `Project.rerun()`, `Project.simulate()`, `Lab.run()`, `RunSet.best()`, `RunSet.worst()`, `Catalog.best()`, `Catalog.latest()`, `Catalog.worst()`, `RunOutcome.open()` |
| `RunSet` | Collection view over several simulations from one catalog. | `Catalog.find()`, `Catalog.rank()` |
| `Project` | Setup-once, run-many interface for HydroModPy simulations. | `hmp.open()` |
| `Lab` | Build, look at, change and solve a model in memory, one step at a time. | built by the other objects |
| `Session` | One calibration session, read from its directory. | `hmp.open()`, `RunOutcome.open()` |
| `Workspace` | Read-only view of a workspace: its projects and the sealed runs they hold. | `hmp.open()` |
| `RunOutcome` | What a finished run says, read from its directory. | `hmp.run()`, `hmp.replay()`, `hmp.status()`, `hmp.status()` |
| `PlanDraft` | A plan before it is written: its cases, and what is wrong with them. | `hmp.run()`, `Project.plan()`, `Project.simulate()` |
| `OverviewResult` | What an overview drew, and where it sealed it. | `hmp.run()` |
| `Diagnostic` | One finding of a check, at one key of the document. | `hmp.check()` |
| `CalibrationReport` | What one calibration found, with or without phases. | `hmp.calibrate()` |
| `CalibrationPlan` | What a calibration declares, with nothing run and nothing written. | `hmp.calibrate()` |
| `SpinupResult` | Outcome of a spin-up loop. | `hmp.spinup()`, `Project.spinup()` |
| `StatusReport` | The status of every case of the current plan. | `hmp.status()`, `Project.status()` |
| `Comparison` | The tables of one comparison and the data of its figures. | `hmp.compare()` |
| `PublishedLine` | One line of `published.jsonl`: where a copy went, or where a file goes. | `hmp.export()` |
| `PublishedProject` | What `publish_project` wrote, and the runs it left out with the reason. | `hmp.publish()` |
| `ExampleEntry` | One cataloged example: what it is, and every file it needs. | `hmp.example()`, `hmp.example()` |
| `InstallReport` | What one `hmp example add` actually did. | `hmp.example()`, `hmp.example()` |
| `DoctorReport` | The state of the machine: versions, packages and solver executables. | `hmp.doctor()` |

`hmp.open` gives what a path stands for: a `Project`, a `Run`, a `Session` or a `Workspace`. A `Run` reads the folder it names, and the seal in it says what the run is; the index only finds it.

A `Lab` is the exception: it holds a `Project` and builds and tries a model in memory, step by step. It writes no run folder while you work, and `lab.run` keeps the result as a run like any other.

## What `Run.read` returns

`run.read(name)` looks for `name` among the fields of the run, then among its time series, then among its geographic features. Each nature of variable gives one type, and `time=` never changes it:

| Nature | Type | Reading it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a field gives an `xarray.DataArray` with the dimensions `time`, `layer` and `cell` it has. One period in `time` removes `time`. | | |
| a time series gives a `pandas.Series` indexed by date. It takes `sel` and no `time`. | | |
| a geographic feature gives a `geopandas.GeoDataFrame`, one row per shape. It takes no `time`. | | |
| `"particles"` gives a `pandas.DataFrame`, one row per recorded position. It takes no `time`. | | |

To read by reference (id, unique prefix or name) instead of from a `Run`, call `proj.store.read(ref, name)` on the Catalog of the project.

## Going from one object to the next

```
proj = hmp.open("path/to/project")  # Project
run = proj["baseline"]              # Run
runs = proj.runs(site="nancon")     # RunSet: the completed runs of one site
best = runs.best("nse")             # Run, by a metric
```

## The words of the API

Each word has one meaning, in every function and every object.

| Word | Means | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | A `Run`: one sealed directory under `runs/`. | `run.read(...)`, `run.figure(...)`, `hmp.export(run, ...)` |
| `ref` | Text that names a run: an id, a unique prefix, a name or a selector such as `@latest`. | `hmp.compare([a, b]).table`, `proj[ref]`, `proj.store.read(ref, ...)` |
| `variable` | The name of a field, a series or a feature. | `run.read(variable)`, `run.field(variable)`, `run.timeseries(variable)` |
| `time` | The stress period or periods to read: an index, a date, `"first"`, `"last"`, or for `Run.read` a slice of indexes. | `Run.read`, `run.field`, `Run.figure`, `hmp.export` |
| `period` | A window of dates: `(start, end)`, or a year as text. | `run.timeseries`, `run.observed`, `run.budget`, `hmp.export`, `sel={"period": ...}` |
| `steps` | An inclusive range of period indexes, `(first, last)`. | `run.budget`, `proj.store.query_budget` |
| `layer` | A layer index, 0 for the top layer. | `Run.read`, `run.field`, `hmp.export` |
| `set` | Changes of a configuration: a dotted path, the grammar of `--set`, or a name of `hmp config targets`. | `hmp.run`, `proj.simulate`, `proj.plan`, `hmp.Project.rerun` |
| `from_step`, `until_step` | Names of pipeline steps. The names are frozen: `hydromodpy.core.pipeline_steps.STEP_NAMES`. | `hmp.run`, `proj.simulate` |
| `best` | One `Run`, the best by a metric. `proj.best_runs` gives the table of the best run of each site. | `runset.best`, `session.best`, `proj.runs().best`, `proj.store.best` |
| `parameters` | The table of the parameters of a run, or of a set of runs. | `run.parameters`, `runset.parameters` |

# Solvers

Every process a run can plan and the solver that carries it out, read from the solver registry of the code. Each row shows what the backend declares on its class: its category, the grid it builds on and the meshes it reads, the fields and tables it writes, and the traits of the model it supports (boundary kinds, model options and initial states). A trait a backend does not list is refused before the run. The row also gives the lines of the TOML file that select it, the executable it runs, the run it needs before it, and whether its results are read back into the catalog. What they solve is in The solvers of the aquifer.

The executables are downloaded by `hmp install-binaries` (see hmp install-binaries), or the first time a solver needs one.

# Theory

Theory covers what HydroModPy computes or decides: the rules it applies when it builds a model, the conversions from TOML to solver input, the methods it implements itself, and what it refuses. The equations of MODFLOW and of the literature are read at their source. A page gives external theory a few sentences and a citation, then says what HydroModPy does with it. Each page names the keys that set its terms. A whole file is walked through in example 04.

## Sources we build on

- MODFLOW 6 groundwater flow: Langevin et al. [2017]. Framework and IMS solver: Hughes et al. [2017]. Input guide: MODFLOW 6 input reference.
- XT3D on irregular meshes: Provost et al. [2017].
- MODFLOW-NWT: Niswonger et al. [2011], on Harbaugh [2005]. Input guide: MODFLOW-NWT guide.
- Mesh generation: Gmsh manual.

The solvers of the aquifer gathers the links package by package. Every citation is listed in the Bibliography.

## Same subject, four places

Take the soil reservoir. Each door says something different about it.

| Place | What it says | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User guide, the overview | What it means, in plain words | Part of the rain never reaches the water table: the soil keeps it and plants take it back. |
| `Reference` | Every key, generated | `ru`: capacity of the store, in mm, default and range. |
| Theory | What HydroModPy computes, with its assumptions | \(S_t = W_t - \mathrm{ETR}_t - X_t\), where \(X_t\) is the water above \(\mathrm{RU}\). |

# Boussinesq theory

This page gives the equations of the in-house Boussinesq solver, in the order the code applies them, with what they assume and where they stop being true. It does not say how to set up a run: the solvers and what each supports are in Solvers.

The solver is not a MODFLOW wrapper. It writes one mass balance per triangular cell of a 2D mesh, with the hydraulic head as the unknown. The equation behind it is the Boussinesq equation under the Dupuit assumptions [Boussinesq, 1877, Boussinesq, 1904, Dupuit, 1863]; a textbook treatment is [Brutsaert, 2005].

Note

Scope. The solver is chosen with `solvers` in a flow process. It runs one layer on a triangular mesh. It reads the conductivity and the specific yield, and nothing else about the ground. It builds recharge, wells, imposed heads on the sides, on the streams and on the ocean, and a top drain. A file that asks for another term is refused (see Limits). `solver.backend` is a plain string, `boussinesq` here. Set it as well as the process: only then is the file checked against what this solver lists in `supports` when it is read. The settings of the solve are the table `[solver.boussinesq]`.

## Notation

Every quantity is per cell \(i\), or per edge \(e\) between two cells, unless the table says otherwise. Lengths are in meters, times in seconds, rates in m/s. Every symbol of the site is on Notation.

The residual of a cell is in m3/s. The recharge and the two surface rates are in m/s, so they enter the balance multiplied by the area \(a_i\).

## From the Boussinesq equation to one residual per cell

The solver does not discretize the differential form of the equation. It integrates the balance over each triangle and writes the flux through each edge with a two-point formula between the centroids: a cell-centered finite-volume scheme with one head per cell. The space scheme is the descriptor `FV_TRI_CELL_CENTERED` in `hydromodpy/solver/boussinesq/catalog.py`.

The sign convention is the one of the code. A residual term that is positive removes water from the cell. Recharge and injection therefore enter with a minus sign. A converged solution satisfies \(R_i \approx 0\) in every cell that is not constrained.

### 1. Saturated thickness and transmissivity

The nonlinear solver may try a head below the bottom of the aquifer or above the land surface. The physical operators read it through a thickness that is always admissible (`saturated_thickness_from_head` and `transmissivity_from_head` in `assembly/fluxes.py`):

\[B_i(h) = \min\bigl(\max(h_i - z_{\mathrm{bot},i},\ 0),\ H_i\bigr), \qquad T_i(h) = K_i\,B_i(h)\]

The thickness is zero for a head at or below the bottom, and \(H_i\) for a head at or above the land surface. A head above the land surface does not add transmissivity. The mesh builder refuses a cell whose top is below its bottom: the message says `z_top_centroid must be >= z_bottom_centroid.`

### 2. Flow between two cells

Take an internal edge \(e\) shared by cells \(a\) and \(b\). `internal_edge_flux_from_head` defines one oriented flux, positive when water leaves \(a\) and enters \(b\):

(36)\[q_e = -\tau_e\,(h_b - h_a), \qquad \tau_e = K^{H}_e\,\bar{B}_e\,\frac{L_e}{d_e}\]

where \(K^{H}_e = 2 / (1/K_a + 1/K_b)\) is the harmonic mean of the two conductivities, and zero if either is not positive. \(\bar{B}_e = (B_a + B_b)/2\) is the mean of the two saturated thicknesses. The distance \(d_e\) is floored at a tiny positive value so that a degenerate edge does not divide by zero. The flux enters the two cells with opposite signs, so water is conserved across every edge.

The thickness of the edge is the arithmetic mean, not the thickness of the donor cell. The flux therefore does not fall to zero when the cell that gives water is dry. On a sloping substratum a dry cell can sit higher than its wet neighbor and be asked to give water it does not hold. That is the case the lower obstacle handles (see The lower obstacle).

Fig. 47 Left: the two cells of (36), the shared edge of length \(L_e\) and the distance \(d_e\) between the centroids. Right: cell \(b\) sits 6 m higher on the substratum and drains into \(a\), whose saturated thickness stays 5 m; the flow comes from `internal_edge_flux_from_head`. Look at \(B_b = 0\): with the mean thickness the dry cell \(b\) still gives water, where a donor thickness would give none.

### 3. Cells with an imposed head

The solver imposes a head on cells, not on edges. Three kinds of boundary resolve to a set of constrained cells \(j\), each with a head \(H^D_j\) per stress period (`forcing/dirichlet_support_resolution.py`):

- a side of the mesh (north, south, east, west): the owner cells of the boundary edges on that side;
- the streams: the owner cells of the edges the mesh tags as river;
- the ocean: every cell whose land surface is at or below the ocean stage of the period, as MODFLOW 6 builds its ocean CHD. A cell inside a wide sea is constrained like a cell on the edge of the mesh.

A boundary can also name a support of the mesh with `flow.bc.<name>.support_label`. The cells of that support are constrained instead of the default ones.

Two boundaries that give different heads to the same cell are refused (the message says `overlaps another prescribed-head BC on cell`). An outer edge that carries no boundary is a no-flow edge: no term couples it to anything.

On a constrained cell the head is overwritten by \(H^D_j\) before any flux is computed, and the row of the nonlinear system is replaced by the constraint itself (`resolve_boundary_head_inputs` and `finalize_boundary_constrained_residual` in `assembly/inputs.py`):

\[h_j = H^D_j, \qquad \text{solver row of } j:\ h_j - H^D_j = 0, \qquad \Phi^D_j = -R_j\]

\(R_j\) is the balance the cell would have had if it were free. The constraint carries \(\Phi^D_j = -R_j\), which is positive when water leaves the model through that cell. A constrained cell is a boundary, as in MODFLOW: its recharge, wells and drain do not act (`on_free_cells` in `assembly/inputs.py`), and a well placed there pumps nothing (the run warns). Its flux is the water its free neighbors send in or draw out, plus the change of its own storage when \(H^D_j\) changes between periods. The residual the run exports adds \(\Phi^D_j\) back: it is zero on a constrained cell, and its sum is the closure error of the run (`_balance_residual_m3_s` in `drivers/state.py`).

Because the head is pinned at the centroid of the cell and not on the edge, the solution at the boundary cell differs from the value on the edge by about the gradient times half a cell. The note at the top of `runtime_contract.py` records this choice and its size on the Dupuit test case. An edge form of the exchange exists for diagnostics only: the driver rebuilds it after the solve to export the exchange by edge (`assembly/boundary_flux_reconstruction.py`).

### 4. Recharge and wells

The recharge \(N_i\) is a rate per unit of area. It is constant over a stress period. It is either one number per period, the same on every cell, or one value per cell when the file loads a recharge field. The volume rate that enters the cell is \(a_i N_i\). A negative recharge is refused: the message says `must be non-negative.` A negative `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim` on a steady period is refused too, because this solver has no ETP package to take a deficit. A transient period keeps its own value. A steady period takes `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim` (Rain and evaporation: the forcing): the period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when `flow.first_period_steady` is true, as in MODFLOW.

A well is a volume rate \(\Phi^{\mathrm{well}}_i\), positive for injection and negative for pumping. It is placed on the triangle that contains its x and y coordinates, in the one layer of the model. A well outside the mesh is refused. A well in a layer other than the first, or addressed by a grid cell, is refused too. Wells that fall in the same triangle add up.

### 5. The top drain

The drain removes water only where the head is above the land surface (`drainage_outflow_from_head`):

\[q^{\mathrm{drain}}_i = C_i\,\max\bigl(h_i - z_{\mathrm{top},i},\ 0\bigr)\]

It is an outflow, and enters the residual with a plus sign. The conductance \(C_i\) is the value of `flow.bc.drainage.value`, the same for every cell in a given period. When that value is not positive, the code derives \(C_i = K_i\,a_i/b\) instead, with \(b\) the drain bed thickness `solver.drain_bed_thickness_m` (`derived_drain_conductance_m2_s` in `assembly/fluxes.py`). It is the derivation of both MODFLOW solvers (Drains and evapotranspiration at the top of the model), with the same \(b\), without their floor for a degenerate cell.

Two consequences follow.

- The drain is never off. A run with no drainage boundary passes a conductance of zero, which selects the derivation. A cell whose head rises above the land surface always loses water through \(K_i a_i/b\).
- On a cell supported by the ocean, the driver sets the conductance to zero to silence the drain (`apply_ocean_drainage_mask` in `drivers/forcing.py`). Zero selects the derivation, so these cells drain with \(K_i a_i/b\) instead of with the configured value.

The discharge that a calibration reads from this solver is the sum over the cells of this drain flow (`extract_discharge_history` in `calibration_extractors.py`). It does not include the release at the surface, defined below.

### 6. Storage and the time step

A transient run adds a storage term, with a backward Euler time scheme. The volume held by a cell is lower-bounded and not capped (`_stored_saturated_volume_m3` in `assembly/residuals.py`):

(37)\[M_i(h) = a_i\,S_{y,i}\,\max\bigl(h_i - z_{\mathrm{bot},i},\ 0\bigr)\]

and the term that enters the residual is

\[\frac{M_i(h^{\mathrm{new}}) - M_i(h^{\mathrm{old}})}{\Delta t}\]

Transmissivity uses the capped thickness \(B_i\); storage does not. Two reasons explain the difference. A head below the bottom must not give a negative volume. A head above the land surface, which the head-only closures allow, must keep the memory of the previous step: with a capped volume, the change of storage over the step would be lost.

Each stress period is split into `simulation.time.substeps_per_period` backward Euler steps of equal length \(\Delta t\), one by default. The forcing is constant over the period and is evaluated at the end of each step. The PETSc obstacle runtimes can refine each of these steps further (see Boussinesq engines and experimental closures).

A stamp closes its period (Time alignment of outputs and observations). A period exports the heads at its end, those of its last step, and the mean of the fluxes of its steps, weighted by their length: recharge, wells, drain, release at the surface, imposed heads and the edge fluxes. The internal steps of the PETSc obstacle runtimes (VI substeps, TS steps) are averaged the same way. MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT store the same quantities. With one step a period, the mean is the flux of that step, unchanged. The change of storage over the period, recomputed from the heads at both ends, then closes the budget with these means. A seepage mask built from the release marks the cells that released water during the period.

### 7. The residual of a free cell

For every free cell, the transient problem is the sum of the storage term, the internal fluxes, the drain, the release at the surface \(s_i\) (defined below), the recharge and the wells, all at the new time level (`_transient_raw_residual_from_spatial_terms`):

(38)\[R_i^{\mathrm{transient}}(h^{\mathrm{new}}) = \frac{M_i(h^{\mathrm{new}}) - M_i(h^{\mathrm{old}})}{\Delta t} + R^{\mathrm{int}}_i(h^{\mathrm{new}}) + q^{\mathrm{drain}}_i(h^{\mathrm{new}}) + a_i\,s_i(h^{\mathrm{new}}) - a_i\,N_i - \Phi^{\mathrm{well}}_i = 0\]

\(R^{\mathrm{int}}_i\) is the sum of the edge fluxes of the cell. The steady problem is the same residual without the storage term. The mixed closure takes \(s_i\) as an input instead of computing it (`_with_saturation_excess` in `assembly/residuals.py`).

## What happens at the surface and at the bottom

A cell can be full to the land surface, or empty down to the bottom. The head-only residual above needs a rule for the water that cannot be stored. The solver offers three families of rules. With the value `auto`, every runtime except PETSc uses the first, and PETSc uses the complementarity closure.

### The regularized partition

The `regularized_partition` closure keeps the head as the only unknown. It releases water at the surface by a smooth function of the depth of the water table, so that there is no sharp on and off at the moment the cell is full (`regularized_partition_surface_rate_from_balance` in `assembly/surface.py`). The depth of the water table below the land surface is

\[d_i(h) = H_i - B_i(h),\]

zero for a head at or above the top and the whole thickness for a dry cell. The sum of the fluxes through the edges of the cell is \(R^{\mathrm{int}}_i\) (step 2). The water that arrives at the cell, per unit of area and besides its storage, is the lateral inflow, the recharge and the wells, each with its sign, a pumping well being negative:

\[\gamma_i = \max\!\left(-\frac{R^{\mathrm{int}}_i}{a_i} + N_i + \frac{\Phi^{\mathrm{well}}_i}{a_i},\ 0\right)\]

and the release is

(39)\[s_i(h) = \exp\!\left(-\frac{d_i(h)}{\delta}\right)\gamma_i\]

The depth scale \(\delta\) is `solver.boussinesq.partition_release_depth_m`, 0.05 m by default. A cell with an imposed head releases nothing: its constant-head flux carries the water it receives. The law follows the regularized partition of seepage and subsurface flow of Marçais et al. [2017], smoothed over the depth of the water table in meters. The factor in front of \(\gamma_i\):

Fig. 49 The factor of (39), from `regularized_partition_surface_rate_from_balance`. The dots are the depths 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 and 1 m. Look at the left panel: with the default 0.05 m the factor is 0.37 one depth scale below the surface and 0.018 at 0.2 m. The right panel shows that at 1 m it is 2e-9, whatever the thickness of the aquifer. The dotted and dash-dotted curves are the depth scales 0.02 and 0.1 m.

A cell full to the surface releases the whole of what arrives, a water table 5 cm under the surface about a third of it, and a water table 1 m under the surface nothing that matters. As \(\delta\) goes to zero the law becomes the threshold of the complementarity closure below. A smaller \(\delta\) comes closer to that threshold and makes the Newton solve stiffer: near the surface, the release switches on and off with the sign of the arriving water. So the line search of the sparse runtime asks the L2 norm of the residual to fall, which a Newton step lowers, and not its largest entry, which one cell on that kink can hold. Convergence still reads the largest entry. If Newton still stops, that runtime solves again from a depth scale 16 times larger and halves it down to the one asked, each solve starting from the heads of the last. Only the solve at the depth asked can be the answer, so a run that converges directly does not change. This is a pragmatic law and not a model of overland flow. The four runtimes of this method use the same law.

### The complementarity closure

The `complementarity` closure turns the surface into an exact threshold. It adds one unknown per cell, the saturation excess \(q^{\mathrm{ex}}_i\), and replaces \(s_i\) by it. The head cannot rise above the land surface, and water is released only when the head is at the surface:

\[0 \leq q^{\mathrm{ex}}_i \;\perp\; z_{\mathrm{top},i} - h_i \geq 0\]

that is, both quantities are non-negative and their product is zero. If the head is below the surface, nothing is released. If something is released, the head is at the surface. The release is solved together with the heads, so the balance and the threshold hold at the same time.

The code does not solve the inequalities. It turns each pair into one equation with the Fischer-Burmeister function \(\phi_\mathrm{FB}(u, v) = \sqrt{u^2 + v^2} - u - v\), which is zero exactly when \(u \geq 0\), \(v \geq 0\) and \(u v = 0\). The rate is scaled by a rate \(q_s\) and the gap by a length \(h_s\), so that both arguments are of order one (`_complementarity_scales` and `_fischer_burmeister_residual_and_derivatives` in `runtimes/petsc_mixed_common.py`):

\[\phi_\mathrm{FB}\!\left(\frac{q^{\mathrm{ex}}_i}{q_s},\ \frac{z_{\mathrm{top},i} - h_i}{h_s}\right) = 0\]

The length \(h_s\) is the thickest cell of the mesh, and at least 1 m. The rate \(q_s\) is the largest of the recharge, the well rate per unit of area, the conductivity, and in a transient run \(S_y h_s / \Delta t\), with a floor of \(10^{-12}\) m/s. These scales are numerical. They change the conditioning of the system and not its solution. A constrained cell does not release: its unknown \(q^{\mathrm{ex}}\) is held at zero.

### The lower obstacle

The head must also stay at or above the bottom of the aquifer:

\[z_{\mathrm{bot},i} \leq h_i \leq z_{\mathrm{top},i}\]

The mixed closure enforces the lower bound with a second unknown per cell, \(q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i\), and a second complementarity:

\[0 \leq q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i \;\perp\; h_i - z_{\mathrm{bot},i} \geq 0\]

with the same Fischer-Burmeister form in the scaled variables. The three unknowns per cell are \((h_i, q^{\mathrm{ex}}_i, q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i)\): the system has three times as many unknowns as there are cells.

\(q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i\) is not a leak through the substratum. It is a numerical unmet demand. When a cell is empty, its balance may ask to remove more water than the aquifer holds. \(q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i\) cancels that excess so that the storage cannot go below zero. It enters the balance of the cell with the sign opposite to a removal (`_assembly_with_dry_deficit` in `runtimes/petsc_mixed.py`):

\[R_i \leftarrow R_i - a_i\,q^{\mathrm{dry}}_i\]

If a cell sits at \(h_i = z_{\mathrm{bot},i}\), the term offsets the remaining demand and does not add water through a physical boundary. It is not a flux of the water budget of the catchment.

The head-only closures have no explicit lower constraint: their storage is lower-bounded, and the run reports whether the accepted heads went below the bottom.

### One cell, by hand

The test `test_single_cell_pumping_activates_lower_obstacle` in `tests/validation/numerical/transient/test_boussinesq_drying_petsc.py` runs one isolated cell. Its area is 1 m2, the bottom is at 0 m, the top at 2 m, \(S_y = 0.2\). It starts at \(h = 0.1\) m, with no recharge, and a well pumps \(0.01\) m3/s for one step of \(\Delta t = 10\) s.

For a head above the bottom, the residual is

\[R(h) = \frac{0.2\,h - 0.2 \times 0.1}{10} + 0.01 = 0.02\,h + 0.008\]

It reaches zero at \(h = -0.4\) m, which is below the bottom: no admissible head balances the cell. At the bottom the storage term is \(-0.002\) m3/s and the residual is \(R = 0.008\) m3/s. The second complementarity gives \(h = 0\) and \(a\,q^{\mathrm{dry}} = 0.008\), so

\[q^{\mathrm{dry}} = 0.008\ \text{m/s}\]

which is the value the test asserts. The well asked for 0.01 m3/s, the aquifer could give 0.002 m3/s from storage, and the other 0.008 is the unmet demand.

Fig. 51 The cell of the test. Left: its residual against the head, from the assembly of the code. Without a floor on the storage (dotted), the balance reaches zero at \(h = -0.4\) m (cross), below the bottom. The code’s storage stops at the bottom, so \(R\) stays at 0.008 there and has no root. The obstacle subtracts \(a\,q^\mathrm{dry}\) (dashed) and puts the solution at \(h = 0\) (dot). Right: of the 0.01 m3/s pumped, 0.002 comes from storage and 0.008 is unmet. \(q^\mathrm{dry}\) is the value the test asserts, since the PETSc solve does not run at build time.

## Methods and engines

`solver.boussinesq.surface_interaction_model` picks the closure and `solver.boussinesq.backend` the engine; the pair resolves to one method. A closure that the backend does not implement is refused when the solve starts. The default `auto` runs the dense engine `local` up to 400 cells and the sparse engine `scipy_sparse` above, and logs which one runs. Asked by name, the dense engines `local` and `scipy` refuse a mesh of more than 400 cells; `scipy_sparse` has no such limit. `petsc` needs `petsc4py`, runs on Linux only, in serial, and is the only engine of the mixed closure. The engines step by step, the experimental closures and the diagnostics a run writes are on Boussinesq engines and experimental closures. What each solver supports is listed in Solvers.

## The starting state and the time loop

The transient driver loops over the stress periods. At each period it takes the forcing of the period and solves `simulation.time.substeps_per_period` backward Euler steps of equal length, each from the heads of the step before, as the previous state and as the initial guess. The forcing holds over the period, as in MODFLOW.

When `flow.first_period_steady` is true, the default, the first period is solved at steady state, as in MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT. It is one steady solve under the forcing of that period, with the recharge `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim` gives. The initial heads are its first guess only. The engine keeps its surface closure. The TS VI obstacle closure steps in time only, so that period takes the VI obstacle closure on the same PETSc engine. The next periods step in time from that state. A steady period holds one state from its start to its end, so the run reports no change of storage over it. When the key is false, the first period is a backward Euler step from the initial heads, like the others.

The initial heads come from `flow.ic.h.kind`. With `steady_state`, the solver first runs one steady solve with the same method, under the time mean of the recharge, each period by its length, or under the rate of `flow.ic.h.rate`, with the boundary heads of the first period. It starts the transient from the result. Cyclic spin-up and `flow.restart_from` are not implemented for this solver and the file is refused when it asks for them. In the code: `run_transient_runtime`.

## Limits

- Dupuit, one layer. The flow is horizontal and the head is uniform over the saturated thickness. The top and bottom are the values sampled at the centroid of the triangle. The solver reads one isotropic conductivity and one specific yield per cell, and no specific storage or anisotropy. Where this stops being true is on The groundwater flow problem. The solver reads no `[domain.layers]`, so a file or a calibration phase that asks it for more than one layer, or for layers by surfaces, is refused when it is read. A runtime override of the properties of a run sets K and Sy, and Kv, Ss, K22 and the angles of the K tensor are refused by name.
- Skewed cells. The two-point flux is accurate where the line between the two centroids is perpendicular to the edge. The solver has no correction for skewed cells.
- Triangles only. A mesh with another cell shape is refused: the message says `Boussinesq V1 currently supports only triangular cells`.
- Supported terms. Recharge, wells, side, stream and ocean imposed heads, and the top drain. A file that declares anything else under `[flow.sinks_sources]` or `[flow.bc]` is refused: ETP, lakes and reservoirs, stream routing, flow barriers. The soil reservoir is read by MODFLOW 6 only. The solver reads none of `solver.sink_fill`, `solver.drain_band_depth_m` and `solver.drain_conductance_floor_m2_s`, so a file that moves one off its default is refused. A transport solver in `[[simulation.process]]` is refused when the file is read, because none follows this solver. Each refusal names the key the file wrote and the solvers that honor it.
- Boundary bias. Near a boundary with a strong gradient, the head of a pinned cell differs from the edge value (step 3). Refine the mesh there to reduce it.
- Fixed steps. A time step that does not converge ends the run. The step length is fixed by the period and its sub-steps; the PETSc obstacle runtimes can refine each step further.
- What can be read back. The solver serves the head at a cell, the discharge over the domain, and the release per cell. It has no lake stage and no routed discharge, because it has no lake package and no stream reaches.
- Experimental. The cards of `solver.boussinesq.backend` and `solver.boussinesq.surface_interaction_model` are marked experimental, and the description of the obstacle closures says so too.
- Not a model of overland flow. The water released at the surface leaves the model. It is not routed downhill. Neither surface closure routes the water over the land.

The status of the solver against the analytic cases is on Validation. How it compares with MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT is on The solvers of the aquifer.

[simulation.time]

`# substeps_per_period = 1` : Number of solver time steps within each stress period, the one knob that buys transient accuracy. - >= 1 dev
**Path**: `simulation.time.substeps_per_period`
**More**: The default of 1 integrates a whole period in a single backward-Euler step, which is not a neutral choice: on a seasonally recharged hillslope drained by DRN cells it moves the monthly discharge by 4 to 28 % against a refined run, across the whole plausible bedrock range, and a calibration scored on discharge absorbs that into the fitted parameters. The right count compares the aquifer response time `tau = L^2 S / (K b)` with the period length, and the solver cost is linear in it; 30 gives daily steps inside monthly periods. Consumed by the MODFLOW backends as DIS NSTP / TDIS nstp, and by the Boussinesq backend, which solves each period in as many backward-Euler steps of equal length. Every solver stores one result per period: the head at the end of the period and each flux as the mean of its steps, weighted by their length.
**Accepted**: integer
**Valid range**: >= 1 (refused outside)
**Unit**: -

**Path**: `solver.boussinesq.partition_release_depth_m`
**More**: A cell whose water table lies d metres below the land surface releases at the surface the share exp(-d / depth) of the water it receives, its lateral inflow plus its recharge and wells: all of it with the water table at the surface, 37 % at one depth scale, 2e-9 at 1 m with the default 0.05 m. It stands for the microtopography over which seepage starts, and smooths the onset of seepage for the Newton solve. `# values = 0.0` : Recharge rate: one number, one number per stress period, or a table {period: value} that states every period, in the unit that 'units' names (mm/day by default). mm/day calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.values`
**More**: It is positive when water enters the aquifer; a negative rate leaves it, through the EVT package when negative_to_evt holds. A calibration reads its bounds in that unit too. Do not write it beside [data.recharge] or the soil section, which replace it.
**Accepted**: any value
**Unit**: mm/day
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

`# first_clim = "mean"` : Recharge rate of every steady stress period: every period of a steady run, and the first period of a transient run when flow.first_period_steady is true. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.first_clim`
**More**: 'mean' is the mean of the per-period rates, each weighted by its length; 'first' is the rate of period 0; a number is that rate, in the units of values. A transient period keeps its own rate. The same rule holds for one value per period and for one grid per period, under every solver. With negative_to_evt, the steady period takes the rule on the recharge part and on the deficit part, so its net rate is the one stated here. Boussinesq has no EVT and refuses a negative number.
**See**: flow.first_period_steady
**Accepted**: string or number
**Example**: `"mean"`, `"first"`, `2.0`

`# heterogeneous_source = ‹any value›` : Optional raw data source for heterogeneous (2D per-cell) recharge. dev
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.heterogeneous_source`
**More**: When set, the solver adapter discretizes FieldRecords onto the MODFLOW grid instead of using the scalar 'values' field. Expected: LoadResult with FieldRecords.
**Accepted**: any value

[flow.sinks_sources.wells.<name>]

`# flux = ‹number or list of number›` : Well rate, in the unit that units names (m3/s by default). calibrable
**Path**: `flow.sinks_sources.wells.<name>.flux`
**More**: One number for a constant rate, or one per stress period. It follows the sign of MODFLOW: negative when the well pumps, positive when it injects.
**Accepted**: number or list of number
**Unit**: m3/s
**Calibration**: yes, search space identity, sampling uniform, bounds belong to the site: write them in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`

[flow.bc.<name>]

`# value = ‹number or list of number›` : Boundary-condition value, scalar or one value per stress period.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.value`
**More**: On a head boundary it is the head in metres; left out with no forcing, the table only activates the boundary and no constant head is built. On a drainage boundary it is a conductance in m2/s, and it may be left out: the run then derives it from the conductivity, C = K * cell_area / solver.drain_bed_thickness_m, which keeps the drain proportional to K and makes K/R the quantity a network calibration searches. A zero or negative number selects that same derivation, so it does NOT mean a closed boundary; write a positive conductance to impose one.
**Accepted**: number or list of number

`# value = ‹number or list of number›` : Boundary-condition value, scalar or one value per stress period.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.value`
**More**: On a head boundary it is the head in metres; left out with no forcing, the table only activates the boundary and no constant head is built. On a drainage boundary it is a conductance in m2/s, and it may be left out: the run then derives it from the conductivity, C = K * cell_area / solver.drain_bed_thickness_m, which keeps the drain proportional to K and makes K/R the quantity a network calibration searches. A zero or negative number selects that same derivation, so it does NOT mean a closed boundary; write a positive conductance to impose one.
**Accepted**: number or list of number

`# support_label = ‹string›` : Name of a labelled group of cells or edges of a Gmsh mesh.
**Path**: `flow.bc.<name>.support_label`
**More**: The boundary then applies there instead of on the group its id selects. MODFLOW 6 and Boussinesq read it.
**Accepted**: string

[solver]

`# drain_bed_thickness_m = 1.0` : Metres. m > 0 expert
**Path**: `solver.drain_bed_thickness_m`
**More**: Thickness of the drain BED in the fallback conductance C = K * cell_area / bed_thickness, used when no drainage conductance is declared. A drain bed is the clogging layer at the bottom of a watercourse, decimetres to a metre; it is NOT the aquifer, and the layer thickness this used to borrow (tens of metres) has no physical relation to it. The value matters because it sets how much head the drain itself imposes to pass the recharge: dh = R * bed_thickness / K, independent of the cell size. For R = 439 mm/yr, 30 m gives 4.17 m of head at K = 1e-7 m/s and makes the drain the limiting resistance over two decades of a [1e-7, 1e-3] search; 1 m gives 13.9 cm and 0.1 m gives 1.4 cm. In this method the drain is a seepage face, so it must never limit: K and the recharge decide where water surfaces, not the boundary condition. Proportionality to K is preserved either way, so the K/R invariance the network criterion rests on is untouched. The value 1.0 is a convention with no measured source: no measurement and no document gives it, and it is kept as it is so that no earlier result moves. It stays in [solver], whatever the layer of the other drain keys. Write your own value when you have a measure.
**Accepted**: number
**Valid range**: > 0 (refused outside)
**Unit**: m
**Example**: `1.0`, `0.5`, `0.1`
