- `[data.etp] formula = "oudin"` or `"hamon"` computes the ETP from `[data.temperature]` instead of loading it. Every reader of the ETP receives it.
- `[recharge_estimates]` runs the recharge methods of ESPERE (BRGM) on the loaded data before the solver: Turc, Guttman and Zuckerman, Kessler, the Wallingford, Chapman and Maxwell and Eckhardt baseflow filters, the water table fluctuation, and the factor that would scale the run’s recharge onto the gauged volume. None enters the model. The run prints them beside its own recharge and writes the table `recharge_estimates`. The figures `recharge_estimates` and `water_balance_loop` read it.
- `[data.impervious]` gives the soil reservoir its sealed share cell by cell, from OCS GE of the IGN (`source = "ocsge"`, `year` pinned), from the built-up class of ESA WorldCover (`source = "worldcover"`), or from a file. `[data.curve_number]` does the same for the curve number from a file such as GCN250. Each cell reads the mean inside the catchment, in place of `impervious_fraction` or `curve_number`, and writing that value beside its map is refused. On the Nancon the sealed share is 3.95 % with OCS GE 2023 and 2.39 % with WorldCover 2021.
- `[data.recharge] formula = "turc"`, `"guttman_zuckerman"` or `"kessler"` gives a steady run its recharge: the mean over the complete years of the run of the yearly formula on the basin rain. A transient run is refused, since no share of the year is invented.
- `[recharge_estimates] soil_methods = "all"` runs every soil law on the run’s forcing, and `compare_loaded = true` loads `[data.recharge]` and `[data.runoff]` (SIM2 for instance) beside a soil run for the comparison only. Their monthly recharge and runoff, the run’s and the weather go to `recharge_estimates`, drawn by the new figures `recharge_signals` and `recharge_regime`. `hmp run --until prepare_solver` writes them without a solve.
- `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.soil] infiltration_ratio` sends only that share of the water leaving the soil to the aquifer, the RIPE of ESPERE; the rest runs off on the same day and reaches the discharge through the runoff of the run. 1, the default, changes nothing. The soil budget of `hmp run --until load_data` prints the ratio ESPERE takes from the gauge, the lowest yearly Wallingford baseflow index, for the user to copy: 0.70 on the Nancon over 2015-2020. `[data.infiltration_ratio]` gives it cell by cell from a file, or from OCS GE with one ratio per cover written in the section; HydroModPy ships no value per cover.
- `[data.curve_number]` builds the curve number from a land cover: `source = "ocsge"`, `"worldcover"`, or `"land_cover"` for a raster of a named legend (`cci`, `worldcover`, `clc`, or `custom`). Each class goes to one class of the ESA CCI legend and reads its GCN250 row (Jaafar et al. 2019) on the hydrologic soil group the section writes, a letter or a HYSOGs250m map. Sealed and built-up classes stay out, left to `[data.impervious]`; any row can be overridden under `classes`. On the Nancon with group C, OCS GE 2023 gives 74.2, WorldCover 2021 76.8, the GCN250 map itself 78.5.
- The OCS GE department archives now sit once per machine in the user cache, shared by the sealed share, the infiltration ratio and the curve number. A soil map larger than the catchment, such as the global GCN250, is now read only over the window of the forcing grid.
- A run scores `bfi_gap`, the baseflow index of the simulated discharge minus the one of the gauge, both by the Wallingford filter on the same days, and a calibration may weigh `bfi_error`, its absolute value, beside a fit such as `nse`. It asks whether the stream is fed by its aquifer in the share the gauge shows, and is blind to volume and timing. It reads daily discharge only: a monthly run leaves `bfi_gap` empty, and the criterion is refused outside a transient run with a daily step.
- `[flow.sinks_sources.recharge.scenario]` replaces the loaded recharge by its mean year, with dry years put in a row, to test a sequence of droughts.
- `source = "explore2"` reads a DRIAS Explore2 file of projected recharge or runoff under `[data.recharge]` and `[data.runoff]`.
- `hmp example add` takes several ids (`hmp example add 00 07 08`) or `--all`, and `hmp.example(["00", "07"], add=True)` or `hmp.example(add=True)` does the same from Python. Every id is checked before the first download. The catalog now ships the twelve examples 00 to 11: `python -m tools.dev examples manifest` takes every folder `NN_name` of `examples/projects/` that holds a `project.toml` and a `README.md`, so a new example needs no code. Under `--format json` the command writes one row per example, schema `hmp.example.add.v2`, with the new field `example_id`.
- `hmp catalog gc --solver-files-days DAYS`, and `Project.gc(solver_files_days=...)`, removes the `solver/` folder that `keep_solver_files` kept in the sealed runs older than DAYS. The rule is off by default, so the folders stay unless it is asked. The seal never lists them, so the run reads the same without them. On a daily run such a folder can weigh 5.6 GB, beside 195 MB for its `fields.zarr`.
- The Parquet views of the index (`timeseries`, `budgets`, `mass_balance` and the Parquet `metrics` and `provenance`) now read the kept trials of the sessions too, each row by its `sim_id`.
- `read_workspace_runs`, which reads the runs of several projects without any index, now gives `label` and `rule_version` for each run, computed on read as the index does.
- The sidecar of a sealed share, an infiltration ratio or a curve number built from OCS GE now gives the editions read, one per department, in `product_version`.

### Changed

- The index no longer stamps the `logs/` and `.hmp/` folders of a run, and reads a seal again only when its folder moved. The pulse a live run writes every 30 s made every read of the project write the index again. `Catalog.cases` now reads the status and the pulse of a live case on the disk.

### Fixed

- A folder that holds two chronicles of one station, such as `recharge_file_NANCON_..._M.csv` and `..._D.csv`, now stops the run and lists them. The loader used to read the first name in alphabetical order without a word. A chronicle of `NANCON_REA` is no longer taken for one of `NANCON`: after the id, a name holds nothing, a step, or two dates and a step.
- A network calibration whose best trial matches the map exactly, so that `D_so = D_os = 0`, now seals that trial. The parts of the cost the trial could not define, such as `D_so_over_D_os` or `catchment_mismatch` on a domain with no delineated catchment, are written `null` in `checks.calibrated_by.components`, where the seal refused the run before.
- `hmp check` now names, before the solve, the particle figures (`particle_tracks`, `residence_time_distribution`) a run without particle tracking will skip, and each map whose `pathlines` overlay will be drawn empty. Only the `pathlines` export was named so far, and a `[transport.modflow6_prt]` table with no transport entry in `[[simulation.process]]` went unnoticed until the end of the run.
- A `source = "url"` file whose address has no suffix, such as a WCS `GetCoverage` request, now takes the suffix the server names in `Content-Disposition` or `Content-Type`. It was cached as `.bin`, and Whitebox refused to read it as a DEM. The CRS stamp on a Whitebox output is skipped when the file already holds that CRS: rewriting it made Whitebox fail to read back some GeoTIFFs it wrote, such as a DEM served by GeoServer, on the first run of a project.
- The relief shade of a map now stops at the active cells. On a catchment with a concave outline it used to leave grey streaks across the bays, outside the mesh, and it shaded the inactive cells of the border.
- `hmp publish --package` and the example catalog now ship every data file a TOML names, wherever the key sits. A catchment polygon (`[geographic.catchment] polyg_shp_path`) and a file read by a boundary condition, such as the sea level of example 05, were left out, so the copy failed on a missing file. A shapefile now travels with its `.shx`, `.dbf`, `.prj` and `.cpg`; example 00 shipped its stream network as a lone `.shp`.
- A grid of `data/` that a larger one contains is no longer removed when a sealed run or a lockfile cites it. The skip of an identical run and `hmp run --frozen` failed once an enclosing catchment was fetched. `hmp data prune` removes the smaller grid once nothing cites it.

### Numbers

- With depth_model kind = “flat_substratum”, the aquifer bottom of a DEM pixel without data was set 1 m under the no-data value, so it stopped being read as no data. A mesh that samples the bottom (triangle, voronoi, a regular grid resampled from the DEM) blended it with the flat elevation on the cells next to the mask. With domain_extent = “watershed” these are the cells of the catchment edge: on a 31 km2 catchment at a flat bottom of 15 m, 768 of 779 edge cells had a bottom between -800 and -9 891 m, a column 100 times thicker than the 76 m of the others. A no-data pixel now keeps the no-data value and every sampled cell gets the flat elevation. A constant_thickness model and a regular grid on the DEM pixels do not change.
- map.drawn_by defaults to “crossing”: the mapped network is drawn on the cells as the data gives it, the rule of the paper, still cut to the catchment. It defaulted to “heads”, which kept only the stream heads of the map and drew the rest down the model’s own descent. A calibration with no pin on the protocol follows 1.4, which differs from 1.3 by this rule alone. A pin on 1.3, or map.drawn_by = “heads” in the network output, gives the heads rule back. A run that sealed no network output draws its network figures by the crossing rule too. A file of edition 2.0 that writes no drawn_by moves with it, at the request of the owner, so its K and costs change wherever heads and crossing draw different cells.
- On a mesh whose faces follow the lake shores but leave the ring open somewhere (an arm narrower than a cell, a wall that leaves the shore), a lake owns the cells its polygon covers for more than half of their area, each cell whole. It owned every cell the polygon touched, so a ring of land cells one cell wide joined the lake and had its top carved under the highest stage of the abacus. On a reservoir of 200.3 ha whose shore the faces cover at 99.45 %, the lake goes from 1 256 cells and 296.3 ha to 885 cells and 201.3 ha, and the cells it leaves keep their terrain and get their drain back. A mesh that closes every shore, and a mesh without lake faces, do not change.

## v2.0.0 - 2026-11-20

### What to do when you update

- A run or a session stored by a pre-release (2.0.0a5 and earlier) is refused. Run it again with this version.
- A file with a key that only a pre-release wrote is refused. The message names the current name of each such key the file holds. This version does not rewrite the file, so edit it with that list. `hydromodpy/config/prerelease_forms.txt` holds the forms.
- `hmp doctor --fix-config` still rewrites the keys that load with a warning.
- The `[display]` keys `figures`, `overrides`, `preset`, `cmap`, `backend`, `show`, `save` and `time` are refused, each with what to write. Write one `[[display.figure]]` table per figure, with its options as panel fields, and `theme` for the look. `dpi` now defaults to 300.
- A figure name of a pre-release, such as `piezometric_map` or `seepage_map`, is refused with the request that replaces it. The page “Figure requests” of the reference lists the 73 former names.
- A run sealed before this version still opens and draws with `run.figure(...)`. Its sealed config is refused when it is validated or replayed, so run the file again to replay it.
- `hmp export --regen figures` skips a figure that a pre-release recorded and gives the command that draws it now.
- A Python name or an hmp command that left is refused with the call that replaces it. tests/unit/architecture/surface/removed_names.tsv lists them.
- If you come from version 1, read `docs/source/get-started/from-v1.md`. The keys and commands that moved are listed in `docs/source/reference/changes.md`, “What changed in the TOML”.
- A file that does not say which calibration protocol it wants follows protocol 1.3.
- A run written by an earlier version keeps its label. A [[bug]] row of hydromodpy/schema/changes.toml labels exploratory only the runs whose quantities it names.
- `[[export]]`, `[[sites.export]]` and `[sites.summary]` name what they read with `variable`, the key `[[display.figure]]` writes, one name or a list. A file that writes `variables` still loads with a warning, and `hmp doctor --fix-config` rewrites it. `run.export` and `hydromodpy.export` take `variable=`.
- A second run of one name is `<name>_v2`, not `<name>.v2`. A folder `<name>.vN` of an earlier build still opens under its name. `[simulation] name` cannot end in `_v<N>`, and a file `calib_v2.toml` names its run `calib-v2`.
- The IGN DEM is two sources. `source = "bdalti"` fetches the 25 m BD ALTI and `source = "rgealti"` the RGE ALTI at 5 m, or 1 m with `resolution_m = 1`. A file that writes `source = "ign_geoplateforme_dem"` with `dataset` is refused, and `hmp doctor --fix-config` rewrites it.

### Added

- The HTTP server sends a file of a project with `GET /v1/<org>/<project>/files/<path>`, the path an answer gave: an export, a saved figure, a report or a tar from `publish`. A folder, an absent file and a path or a link that leaves the project are refused.
- `[flow.param.<id>.field_vertical_profile]` takes `depth_at = "top"`, `"middle"`, `"base"` or `"surface_then_base"` (the ground for the first layer, the base for the others), the depth at which each layer reads its profile, the middle by default as before. An exponential profile takes `characteristic_depth_high`, `ground_low` and `ground_high`: its decay length then goes linearly with the ground elevation from `characteristic_depth` to `characteristic_depth_high`, for a weathered zone that thins under the hills.
- `hmp.Lab("project.toml")` builds a model in memory one step at a time. `lab.advance()` plays a step, `lab.state` shows the objects built so far, `lab.steps` shows which steps are built, stale or pending, and `lab.set(K=5e-5)` changes a value so that only the steps that read it play again. `lab.force` puts an object the configuration cannot say, such as a mesh built by hand, and `lab.release` takes it back.
- `hmp.Lab(run)` opens a run from `hmp.open`, sealed or with its facts, in the lab, with the configuration the run kept. It builds nothing until `lab.advance`, and `lab.run` writes a new run in the same project.
- `hmp.run` and `Project.simulate` stopped from `setup_process` up to before `prepare_solver` now give a partial run instead of `None`, which `hmp.open` reads too. Its new `Run.steps` lists the steps done, and reading a field from it says how to resume.
- A how-to page, Run step by step, shows a run played by windows with a figure before the solve, and a run played again that gives back the run already done.
- `when = "after:prepare_solver"` and `"after:run_solver"` are accepted for a figure whose data is stored by then, such as the topography of a backend that builds a cell column. A figure asked earlier than its data is refused at the check, with the first step that fits.
- `hmp.Lab({...}, base=folder)` reads the dict as `hmp.Project` does, and keeps it as a draft when a section is missing, such as `[simulation]`. `lab.set` adds the sections one by one and plays the steps again from the start. `lab.advance` names the step and the section a draft lacks, `lab.run` and `lab.write_config` list what is missing, and no `Project` run starts from a draft.
- `lab.run()` keeps the solve of the lab when `run_solver` is up to date and nothing is forced, instead of solving again. The seal, the stored heads and the solve count in `profile.json` are those of `hmp.run` with the same changes. A project that keeps its solver files solves again.
- `lab.capture` records the local variables of a function while the model solves, `lab.run` keeps the model as a stored run, and `lab.write_config` writes the configuration with your changes. The lab plays in memory up to `run_solver`, and a run is refused while an object is forced.
- An input file can be named in the data folder of the workspace. `path = "workspace:regional_dem_aber.tif"` in `[[data.dem.sources]]` reads `data/dem/regional_dem_aber.tif`, and `path = "workspace:."` in `[[data.hydrometry.sources]]` reads the station folder `data/hydrometry/`. The folder is the role of the key, and the parameter reference gives it on the card of each key that accepts the form. A relative path still reads from the project root. The frozen `config.toml`, `config.resolved.toml` and the inputs of `manifest.json` write every file of `data/<role>/` in that form, and they follow the data folder that `[workspace]` gives.
- `when = "session"` draws a figure when a calibration session ends, into `sessions/<s>/figures/`. `when = "after:extract"`, `"after:derive"` and `"after:export"` draw during the run into `runs/<run>/figures/`. `hmp.show(ref, what="figure", name=...)` draws a variable or a preset on a run, a session or a set of runs.
- A figure is asked by the name of a variable: `run.figure("recharge")`, `run.figure("recharge", type="series", station="zone:catchment", cumulative=True)`. `[[display.figure]]` draws figures at the end of a run, and `[display.presets.NAME]` names a request of your own. `run.figure(..., data=True)` and `hmp show --figure NAME --data DIR` give the tables behind the figure, and `--engine` names the engine.
- The variable `travel_time_to_exit` maps the time the water of each cell takes to reach the end of its pathline, in years, for a run that tracked particles. Each recorded position of a pathline gives a sample, a cell takes the mean of its samples, and a cell no pathline crosses is interpolated from its neighbours. With backward tracking the value is the age of the water. Draw it with `run.figure("travel_time_to_exit", overlays=["outline", "network", "seepage", "pathlines"])`. The `pathlines` overlay draws 250 lines at most. The `particle_tracks` figure takes `variable`: it then draws the map of that variable under thin dark lines, as in `preset = "particle_tracks"`, `variable = "travel_time_to_exit"`, and a figure drawn by a Python function receives `variable` when its signature declares it.
- A section of a water table fills the saturated zone and the unsaturated zone, draws the land surface and the water table as one thick step per cell crossed, on any mesh, and frames them closely when the aquifer is deep. It marks the seepage cells of its period on the land surface, and its title gives the period, the way the line runs and the vertical exaggeration. A section is drawn flatter than a map. The overlays `seepage` and `pathlines` draw the seepage cells and the particle paths over any map, and `lake`, `wells` and `seepage` follow the `time` of the panel. The `particle_tracks` figure draws the seepage and pumping cells where the paths end, takes `time`, and colours each line along its way by the age of the water, from its release to where it leaves the aquifer. The lines released outside the catchment are thin and grey, and beyond 350 lines of a kind one in n is drawn. A log colour bar that spans more than two decades labels its decades only.
- A site file placed on top of a shared calibration file names its own case. The case of a calibration is now named by the first `[simulation] name` met from the file that is run down to the file that writes `[calibration]`. Before, only the file that writes `[calibration]` could name it, so several site files on one shared calibration all took the same case and piled up as `.v2`, `.v3`.
- A calibration on the stream network reads back in full. `hmp show` on its session writes the value of each parameter at the best trial of the phase that moved it, with its unit, and names the calibrated variable `network` where it said `discharge`. The session report draws `network_agreement` and `downslope_distance` for the best run. The page of a promoted run gives its calibration cost, and `run.table("calibration")` or `hmp show RUN --table calibration` lists the parts of that cost, such as the two distances. A map of `network_agreement`, `downslope_distance` or `simulated_active_network` that lists no overlay leaves the mapped reaches off, because they covered the cells.
- A run on Windows no longer stops with `HMPY.E000` and a bad file descriptor when it writes a durable JSON document such as `outcome.json`. The write flushed the staged file through a handle opened for reading, which Windows refuses. The handle is now opened for writing.
- `hmp run` on a calibration file draws the figures its `[display]` asks with `when = "session"`, such as `root_search`. Only `hmp calibrate` drew them, so the same file gave fewer figures by `hmp run`, with no warning.
- The `bdtopage` source downloads again. The Sandre service stopped serving the GeoPackage pages the source asked for, so every box that was not in the cache failed. The pages are now asked as GeoJSON, which gives the same reaches, geometry and values, and a page that is not in Lambert-93 is refused.
- A run exports the tracks of its particles as the vector layer `pathlines`: one line per particle that moved, with its travel time in years (`travel_yr`), as a GeoPackage or a Shapefile. `[[export]] variables = "pathlines"`, `run.export("pathlines")` and `hmp export <run> pathlines` write it.
- `lab.read("head")` reads a variable of the solve of a lab, before any run is written: the water table of every cell, the discharge of the catchment, the saturated thickness and the release per cell. It solves first when the model is stale. The solvers answer `head` on every cell for it, through the port a calibration trial reads, on MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT.
- At the Python prompt, the objects of a lab and of a run print a short summary and no longer their arrays: `lab.state`, its mesh, model, properties, geometry, flow, domain, catchment and configuration, and `run.mesh`. A mesh says how many cells it has, its area and its extent, whether its cells form a regular grid and where its arrays are. The mesh of a lab and the mesh of a run answer the same calls: `n_cells`, `cell_centers()`, `cell_areas()` and `structured_shape`.
- A map and a section take `limits = [low, high]`, the colour limits in the unit drawn. Values beyond take the end colours, and the colour bar is pointed on that side. A map takes `line`, the trace of a section, and draws it dashed. A water-table depth map uses a pale `jet`, blue for a shallow water table and red for a deep one. The `seepage` overlay fills its cells in black, and the `pathlines` overlay draws every line up to 2000.
- A variable can now be drawn as a section, against another variable, as a distribution or by group, with `type=`: `run.figure("head", type="section")` cuts the layers along a line from the outlet, `run.figure("topography", type="xy", variable=["topography", "watertable_depth"])` plots two fields cell by cell, `run.figure("discharge", type="distribution", station="GAUGE", cumulative=True, observed=True)` gives the flow duration curve, `run.figure("budget", type="groups", station="zone:catchment", reduce="mean")` draws the mean budget as bars, and `run.figure("discharge", type="groups", by="month", station="GAUGE", observed=True)` draws the monthly regime as boxes. Use a station of your run in place of `GAUGE`.
- The interactive engine draws the frames `map`, `series` and `volume` as an HTML file that loads plotly.js from a CDN, up to 100 000 cells. Try `run.figure("watertable_depth", engine="interactive", save="depth.html")` or `hmp show RUN --figure watertable_depth --engine interactive --to depth.html`.
- The frame `volume` draws the block of a variable in 3D, with `type="volume"`. It has the interactive engine only.
- Five derived cell fields are variables like the others: `simulated_active_network`, `network_agreement`, `downslope_distance`, `depression_fill_depth` and `package_cells`. `run.figure("package_cells", reduce="max")` maps the boundary package that acts in each cell, and `run.figure("simulated_active_network", type="series", station="zone:catchment")` gives the share of the catchment that flows. `type="table"` prints the `simulation.*` columns with their labels, and `against="<run name>"` on a map draws the difference to another run of the project.
- `run.figure("simulated_active_network")` now draws the map of the variable of that name, which is what a name that both paths know does. Its old options are refused with the list of panel fields. `network_agreement` and `downslope_distance` follow the comparison the run scores (seepage and closure, no visible flow), so they give the counts of `seepage_network_confusion_map`, while `simulated_active_network` keeps the visible flow of the sealed output. A trials panel never mixes two phases, takes the cost label of its phase and says how many trials it shows out of how many the session ran.
- Five presets and twelve special figures are drawn by name. The presets are `hydrograph`, `residuals`, `water_budget`, `watershed_id_card` and `network_expansion`, and a preset has holes you fill with the panel fields it lists: `run.figure("hydrograph", variable="stage", station="lake:1")` or `hmp show RUN --figure hydrograph --opt station=NANCON`. The specials are `sfr_longitudinal_profile`, `observed_network_heads`, `network_comparison`, `flow_directions`, `recession`, `residence_time_distribution`, `particle_tracks`, `lake_abacus_comparison` and `ensemble_band` (a set of runs), and `calibration_progress`, `calibration_landscape` and `root_search` (a session). A special takes only `station` and `time` when its function declares them, and a subject of another kind is refused with the kind expected.
- These names are now also presets or variables, so `run.figure(name)` and `hmp show --figure name` draw the new figure: `hydrograph`, `residuals`, `water_budget`, `watershed_id_card`, `recession`, `residence_time_distribution`, `particle_tracks`, `sfr_longitudinal_profile`, `lake_abacus_comparison`, `ensemble_band`, `calibration_progress` and `calibration_landscape`. An option of the old figure (`normalize`, `log_y`, `figsize`…) is refused with the fields the new one accepts and what to write instead when one replaces it. A score line of a series panel on dates now writes the scoring window under the axis.
- A calibration session is drawn from its trials: `session.figure("trials.cost", type="series")` gives the cost against the trial number, and `session.figure(request={"variable": ["trials.parameter", "trials.cost"], "type": "xy", "facet": "parameter"})` gives one panel per searched parameter, on a log axis when the parameter was searched in log space.
- `[display] theme` names the look of the figures (`default`, `print`, `dark`). It replaces `preset`, which is refused. A figure drawn without `theme` takes the one of the `[display]` the run was sealed with.
- `config.resolved.toml` writes `edition`, the set of defaults the run used, `"2.0"` today. A resolved file without it reads as edition 2.0. A file may write `edition` at its root, and a value this version does not serve is refused with the editions it serves.
- The register of changes is listed on a generated page, `docs/source/reference/changes-register.md`, one table per kind of row.
- `python -m tools.changes_changelog` writes the `Numbers` block of `CHANGELOG.md` between two comments from the register, and exits with 1 when the block differs.
- `tools/docs/snapshots/fields-2.0.0.json`, so the page of TOML changes compares that snapshot with the tree.
- `[solver.modflow_nwt]` and `[solver.boussinesq]` take `wall_clock_limit_s`, the wall-clock budget of one trial of a parallel calibration, as MODFLOW 6 does with `[solver.modflow6.runtime] mf6_api_timeout_s`. Unset, a trial keeps the built-in 14400 s.
- A flow adapter declares `face_flow` among what it writes, and the GWT one declares `concentration/*`.
- A transport whose flow does not write `face_flow` is refused when the file is read, with the flow solvers that write it.
- `[simulation.results] keep_face_flows = true` under a flow solver that does not write `face_flow` is refused when the file is read, with the flow solvers that write it.
- `[simulation.results] keep_face_flows` keeps the flow between each pair of connected cells under MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT, as `face_flow` with `connection_cells`.
- `Project.gc()` and `hmp catalog gc` measure the project and remove the scratch of dead attempts, what the earlier attempts of sealed runs hold beside their `outcome.json`, the products past the cap that the dry run lists, and the field store of kept trials that reached the project more than 90 days ago, all but the best; `--trial-fields-days` sets the age. The mesh of a trial stays for its replay, a session with no single best keeps every trial, and a project whose `project.toml` does not read is collected from its tree with its product store left as it is.
- MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT write `face_flow`, one value per connection of two active cells and positive from the smaller flat index to the larger, with `connection_cells`, the two cells of each connection. The diagonal of MODFLOW 6 `FLOW-JA-FACE` is never kept.
- Series names have the shape `time` in the field registry, and a backend declares the series it writes in `writes`. The linear reservoir declares `discharge`, `reservoir_storage` and `budgets`, and writes the unit the registry gives, `m` for the stored depth.
- source = “url” for the data variables read from one file. https, or http with a sha256. The URL only fills the data cache, and the run reads the file.
- `hydromodpy.model.supports` holds the closed set of traits a solver backend lists in `supports`: the boundary kinds, the fields of `ModelOptions` and the initial states `head_rule`, `steady_start`, `cyclic_start` and `prior_state`.
- `solver.sink_fill = true`, `solver.drain_band_depth_m` and `solver.drain_conductance_floor_m2_s` away from their defaults, and `[flow.sinks_sources.etp]` are refused under Boussinesq, which reads none of them.
- A transport run behind a steady start whose heads did not converge stops with `SolverDivergedError`, where it used to start with a warning. The replay of a sealed run still warns.
- MODFLOW 6 can rerun a solved model for a new K or Sy. It copies the input files of the solved run, rewrites only NPF and DRN for K, STO for Sy, and the file of the properties, and the result is bit-identical to a new build. A start from a steady or cyclic solve, a change that turns XT3D on or off, a change of the drain cells, other binaries or another shared forcing folder still rebuild.
- `[solver.boussinesq] exchange_mesh` names a mesh bundle folder that the Boussinesq solver reads as its cells, with their conductivity and storage. It is a developer option for the validation cases. A relative path is read from the folder of the TOML file.
- The `catchment` mesh engine meshes the catchment as one polygon cell, for a global model. It declares the `lumped` capability, and a solver that accepts any planar engine does not read it.
- `MeshRequest` carries the catchment outline. The planner fills it for a lumped engine only, so the hash of every other request is unchanged.
- The `center_kind` attribute of a mesh can say `interior_point`, the center of the one cell of the `catchment` engine, a point inside it from shapely’s `point_on_surface`.
- The terrain port accepts the conditioning method `"provided"`, and `ConditionedDem.provided(path)` wraps a DEM that another tool conditioned. Both engines route it like any conditioned DEM, and `condition_dem` refuses it with `TerrainRequestError`. The port does not check that the DEM has no depression.
- `hmp run`, `hmp calibrate`, `hmp spinup`, `hmp export`, `hmp data get` and `hmp campaign array` take `--credentials PATH`, `--allow-host HOST` (repeatable) and `--max-download-bytes N`, and the command builds the `Environment` of the call out of them.
- The Python verbs `run`, `calibrate`, `spinup` and `export`, and `Project`, `open_project` and `Project.launch`, take `environment=`, an `Environment` from `hydromodpy.project.environment`; `None` keeps the default, so a run with it does exactly what it did before.
- A `credentials.toml` file outside any project, with one `[[host]]` block per address prefix and a password written in clear or read from a file, chosen for a destination by its longest matching prefix.
- A source whose declared host is not allowed by the bounds of the call is refused before any connection, with the refusal naming the option or argument that widens the list.
- `Model.native_recharge` carries the forcing at the step of its source, in m/s, cut to the window of the run, beside the period view the meshed backends read.
- The field registry holds the station series of `timeseries.parquet` as descriptors of shape `time`: the catchment series, the lake and reach states, and the rates that land in m3 s-1; `VARIABLE_UNITS` is read there no more.
- A solver backend can read the recharge at the step of its source, not only the mean of each period.
- A solver backend whose native step is shorter than a period of the time grid is refused when the document is read.
- The linear_reservoir solver backend, a global model on the one-cell catchment mesh, solved exactly on every piece of constant recharge. It starts from the steady state of its recharge, and a negative recharge is refused.
- A document that writes [flow.param] or [domain.depth_model], or calibrates one of their entries, is refused under a solver backend that reads no aquifer property, such as linear_reservoir.
- A calibration protocol states the observables its stages read. A backend that declares one of them unavailable is reported as unsupported, and a backend that no case of the repository runs is reported as expected to work but untested.
- The export vocabulary lists the simulated series `lak_connection` and `reservoir_storage`, which the time-series registry now holds.
- `hydromodpy.config.check.check(document, partial=True)` checks a whole or a partial configuration section by section and returns every `Diagnostic` at once: the dotted path, a stable code, a severity (`error`, `warning` or `to_fill`) and what the validator said. A required key that is not written yet is `to_fill`. The phrase of each code is in `hydromodpy/schema/phrases.toml`, in English and in French.
- `hmp.check(source, partial=True, inputs=False, environment=None)` checks a project file or a document from Python and returns its list of `Diagnostic`. On a file it gives the line of each key, and once the file has no error and nothing left to fill it adds the findings of the calibration preflight.
- `hmp check --partial` checks a draft, where a missing required key is `to_fill` and refuses nothing. `--inputs` reads the header of each input file, of every case of a `[sites]` project too, and `--lang fr` writes the phrases in French.
- `hmp.check(..., inputs=True)` reads the header of each input file the document names. A local file is opened in a rasterio `Env` of the call. A URL goes through the head-only resolution of `core.io.fetch` under the bounds of the call, then GDAL reads the final URL by `/vsicurl/`, so GDAL never sees the first URL, and a URL without bounds is refused. A DEM must declare a projected CRS in metres, a square pixel and a grid that is not rotated, and the outlet must fall on a valid cell.
- `hmp run` accepts a `.json` request, the serialized form of `RunRequest` (schema `hydromodpy.request.v1`), and takes `--base`, the folder its relative paths are read from. A Docker run is the same command inside the image.
- `hmp.run`, `hmp.calibrate` and `hmp.spinup` take a dict or JSON text with `base=`, through the same loader as a TOML file, and `Project(config, base=)` does the same.
- `hmp.calibrate` and `Project.calibrate` take `force=`. Without it, a calibration that a completed session of its case and of the same solution key answers gives back the report of that session, read from its folder, `extra["identical_to"]` naming it, and nothing runs. `hmp run` on a calibration file does the same and says so, and `hmp run --force` searches again.
- `hmp project new` creates `inputs/` and `configs/` in the project.
- A product store under `.hmp/products/` keeps the meshes and the output of the soil reservoir, keyed by what they read and by the code that computes them. A run, a resume and the trials of a calibration ask it first.
- `[workspace] products_cap_mb` caps the store, 5000 by default. The oldest products go first, never one a running attempt cites.
- A run writes `products.json`, the products it read in order, when its solver step is prepared. A verb called after a run never rewrites it.
- A stored product that cannot be read is discarded and built again. A resume whose cited product is gone builds and stores it under the key of its current inputs.
- `[[data.dem.sources]]` takes `state = "conditioned"` for a DEM another tool filled or breached. HydroModPy skips its own conditioning, still computes the D8 directions and the accumulation, and refuses an aggregation, a crossing notch or a conditioning method beside it.
- A DEM declared conditioned that keeps cells with no lower neighbour gives a warning with their count, and the run store records it.
- The DEM is checked before the terrain chain: a projected CRS in metres, a grid that is not rotated, square pixels within 1 %, a cell size from 1 to 250 m, elevations from -500 to 9000 m, and an outlet on a valid cell.
- `hmp stop REF` and `hmp.stop(ref)` ask a running run or calibration session to stop, by the flag `.hmp/stop.json` of its folder. The run reads it between two steps, between two runs of its plan, and, through libmf6 or Boussinesq, between two time steps. An executable is never killed, so the stop waits for the end of its solve. A stopped run ends `aborted` with `StopRequested`, its process exits with 130, and `hmp run --resume` takes it up from the step it stopped in.
- A calibration session stops when `<session>/.hmp/stop.json` appears, between two batches of trials, and ends aborted with the date of the request as its error. Reopening the session removes the flag.
- `[simulation.time] window_length` cuts a long transient run into windows that end on a stress period end, and `window` picks one or plays them all. Each window is a sealed run named `<name>_w<k>` that starts from the final state of the one before, recorded as its input `initial_state`. A resume names the chain or the window that stopped, with or without the file, and the frozen `config.toml` of a window replays it from that input.
- Every run writes `final_state/`, its last heads, lake stages and SFR reach stages in double precision, sealed with the run. A restart and the next window read it first.
- Every run writes `profile.json`, the time and memory of each step, solve, figure and export, with the age of the process and what was rebuilt from an earlier attempt or read from the project store. A run stopped through its flag keeps the profile of what it did.
- `hmp catalog show` prints a Profile block read from `profile.json` (total time, start-up, solve of each run of the plan, three longest steps, what was reused), and `show_simulation` returns it under the `profile` key. A run of a pre-release says it has no profile and prints the solve time of its seal.
- The README of a sealed run says what a replay costs, read from `profile.json`.
- `hmp replay REF` and `hmp.replay(ref)` play a sealed run or a published copy again and class it: bit when every value hashes the same in double precision, deviation otherwise. `--strict` refuses a deviation.
- The seal of a run gives the digest of the values of every field, every column of a quantity and the final state, taken in double precision before a field is rounded for storage.
- An `[[export]]` block takes `deliver_to`, local or UNC folders or files and `ftp://`, `ftps://` or `sftp://` addresses (sftp through the `sftp` extra, with `host_fingerprint`). Once the run is sealed each file is copied there through `<name>.part`, three attempts each, and every address is checked before the run computes.
- `hmp export <run> --deliver` and `hmp.export(run, deliver=True)` send again what is not delivered, and every file whose bytes changed since.
- A resumed delivery checks each destination against the allowed hosts and folders as the run does, gives a `failed` line for a refused one, and warns of a clear `ftp://` password.
- A file of `exports/` that cannot be read gives a `failed` delivery line without sha256 or bytes, and `hmp export <run> --deliver` exits 1.
- A calibration delivers the promoted run of each case, only once the session is `completed`, and logs a warning when it delivers nothing.
- The refusal of an address no `[[host]]` block answers advises a `prefix` with the port of the address.
- An `sftp://``key_file` may hold an ed25519, ECDSA or RSA private key.
- `session.json` names, for each phase, the options, the seed, the seed of each restart and the libraries of its optimizer, in an optional `optimizer` block. A `session.json` of a pre-release has none and still reads.
- The trial frame of a session (`Session.trials`) gains `batch`, `rule`, `window`, `solve_s` and `reused`, and `Session.profile()` sums where the search spent its time, by step and by `reused`.
- The method text of a run, `hydromodpy.results.method.method_text`, and its label sentence, `label_text`, in English and in French. The text has five paragraphs: the run, its data with each licence, its calibration, its quality with each check passed, failed or unknown, and its limits. Every sentence is a row of `phrases.toml`.
- A sealed run keeps `mesh/open_water` and `mesh/catchment_cells` beside the mean recharge it already kept. They are the open water and the outline cells the stream criterion read.
- `hydromodpy.results.derive.views.budget_over(run, term, polygon=None, *, crs=None, split=False, name=None)` totals a per-cell budget term over the catchment or any polygon, per time step. With `split=True` it gives the inflow and the outflow, each element counted on its own. A field in m3/s stored per cell outside `budget/`, such as `release_flux`, is summed the same way.
- `TERM_FAMILIES` and `family_terms` of `hydromodpy.core.budget.terms`, so `budget_over(run, "storage")` sums `storage_ss` and `storage_sy` under MODFLOW 6 and reads `storage` under MODFLOW-NWT and Boussinesq.
- `inflow_outflow` of `hydromodpy.core.budget.flux`, the one split of a per-cell budget into inflow and outflow.
- `hmp show SESSION` prints the summary of a calibration session: the trials by status, the best trial, the bounds it reached, why the search stopped and the path of its report. A run goes to `hmp catalog show`.
- `hmp calibrate` writes the report of each session directory it leaves, `sessions/<s>/report/`. `hmp calibrate --no-report` and `hmp.calibrate(..., report=False)` skip it, and a report that fails warns without failing the calibration.
- The seal of a data overview writes `tables.parquet/data_inventory.parquet` and lists the loaded inputs in `inputs.json`. Its stats card, station table and page are drawn from those rows.
- `Run.read`, `Run.table`, `Run.figure` and `Run.show`; `Session` and `RunSet` get `table`, `figure` and `show`. A figure is drawn by the renderer the object was opened with.
- `to_dict` on `StatusReport`, `PlanDraft`, `PublishedProject`, `PublishedLine`, `SpinupResult`, `InstallReport`, `ExampleEntry` and `Comparison`, and two returned types, `CalibrationPlan` and `DoctorReport`.
- `hmp ls --disk` lists runs and sessions from their directories, `hmp ls --plan` says where a `[sites]` plan stands, `hmp show` reads a profile (`--profile`), a cell (`--point`), a ranking (`--rank`), a figure (`--figure`), a report (`--report`) and a sealed table (`--table`), `hmp config figures` lists the figures, and `hmp catalog trash REF` moves a run to the trash.
- `hydromodpy_server`, a thin HTTP layer on the verbs, outside the wheel. It serves one space per organisation, runs each run in its own process, takes a file upload into the project inputs, and needs an authenticating proxy in front. `python -m hydromodpy_server --root ROOT` starts it, and the Docker image carries it.
- A run played inside the HydroModPy image seals the image tag and digest in `provenance.json`, and a replay in another image names the digest change in its lineage. The image installs every extra and the solver binaries at build time, and keeps the versions of its build in `/opt/hmp/constraints.txt`.
- A run refuses a field or a table that its backend does not declare in `writes`, and a simulated series that the series registry does not describe.
- `cutoff_wall_flow`, `groundwater_level`, `groundwater_depth`, `water_level` and `lake_level` have their series descriptor and unit.
- The page of each package lists its modules with the first line of their docstring, generated when the docs are built (directive `hmp-module-table`). A module without a docstring fails the strict build.
- A science map links each theory page to the modules that compute it, their unit tests and the validation cases, read from the pages and the tests when the docs are built (directive `hmp-science-map`). A theory page without a `hmp-tested-by` block, or a prefix in it that is not a module, fails the strict build.
- One how-to page, `plug-into-a-port`, lists every port with what a plugin declares, how it registers and the tests that cover it, read from the registries (directive `hmp-port-table`).
- `python -m tools.docs.check_readmes` computes the permitted READMEs from the layer matrix and the registries, and refuses any other README under `hydromodpy/`, a README that is too long, a bullet with a bold label, a dash used as punctuation, a closing summary or French.
- `python -m tools.docs.check_refs` also checks that a repository path between backticks in a README of a package or on a contributor page exists.
- The README of a run says what the run does not give: a change in time on a steady run, the state inside a stress period otherwise, the flow between cells unless `keep_face_flows` is set, and a residence time without particle tracking. It gives that setting only when the solver of the run writes the flow and the run is not a kept calibration trial.
- The main CI plays the scenarios in parallel, gates the line and branch coverage of each sub-package of `hydromodpy` from one table, `tools/ci/coverage_floors.toml`, checked by `tools/ci/coverage_floors.py`, and on each push proves that the test functions a change removes lose no covered line, branch or killed mutant of their modules. The table replaces the 45 coverage report lines and the four coverage jobs of the main CI.
- `tools/ci/proof.py` with `select`, `prove`, `range` and `week`: it picks the test functions a change removes and the tests that stand for them, then runs `tools/ci/removal_proof.py check` to prove that no line, branch or killed mutant of their modules is lost. A change that also edits `hydromodpy/` is refused. A push is proved commit by commit against each parent, a pull request as one change.
- `python tools/ci/local.py list|run` replays the Linux, Python 3.13 steps of the CI workflows on a local machine. It plays each identical test command once, lists every other step as not played locally with its reason, and writes one log per step and a `status` file.
- Weekly jobs replay the frozen MODFLOW 6 gmsh run with one and four BLAS threads and keep its field-scale gaps and the processor as an artifact, prove the test removals of the week at the package scope, and play every Windows proof, the server path and two runs in two processes on Windows.
- The Docker image is published on each version tag to `ghcr.io/hydromodpy/hydromodpy`, with `latest` only outside pre-releases, and a small run plays and replays at the bit inside each image the CI builds.
- Contributors: `tests/regression/frozen_documents/v2.0.0-pre/` keeps the documents of a pre-release that `frozen_runs` does not hold (publication, install index, plan, lockfile, sidecars, data caches, trial series, the six documents of a sealed job, site catalog), written on a synthetic island by `python -m tools.freeze_documents`, and a test reads each one with the readers of this version.
- A page for users of version 1, with the table of old keys and commands.
- A `NOTICE` file with the licences of PyHELP and of the data, and `version` in `CITATION.cff`.
- `hydromodpy_version_min` in `workspace.toml` is enforced.
- A sha256 for each file of a run. `hmp doctor` reports a sealed file that is missing or changed.
- `--format table|json|csv` on the commands that print a result, and a `HMPY.Exxx` code at the start of each error line.
- JSON Schemas for `manifest.json`, `provenance.json` and the output of `hmp calibrate`.
- A transient Boussinesq run writes a `storage` budget term, so its domain budget closes.
- `[calibration] validation_window = {start, end}` keeps dates apart from the search. Each trial is also scored on them, under `validation.cost`. The promoted run stores the period and the score in `checks.calibrated_by`.
- `[metrics] window` minus the validation window is the default calibration window. A validation window that overlaps it, leaves a bound open or has no dated record is refused by name.
- `Project.calibrate()` takes `protocol`, `case`, `resume`, `dry_run`, `workspace`, `project`, `project_label`, `metric_fn` and `objective` by name on every route. `dry_run=True` returns the plan.
- `flow.sinks_sources.recharge.factor` multiplies the recharge in force. The default of 1 changes nothing. A calibration reaches it as `recharge.factor`, searched in log space between 0.5 and 2.
- `vka` can be calibrated under MODFLOW 6 as `[calibration.parameters.vka]`, in log space. It is not offered when the project declares `Kv`.
- `hmp campaign promote CASE` without `--trial` lists the five best completed trials. `hmp config targets` shows the search space, the draw and the default bounds of each target.
- `hmp check` refuses `normal` sampling on `lhs` and `optuna`, and a calibrated recharge factor when the run has no recharge to multiply.
- `docs/source/reference/outputs.md` lists every field array and every station series a run stores, with its path, unit and dimensions, read from `hydromodpy/results/field_registry.py`.
- In the docs, the `{default}` role writes the default of a TOML key from the registry, and `python -m tools.docs.check_page` refuses a cited path of the repository that does not exist.
- The report of a run draws 15 figures and the report of a session 4, with new file stems (`network_agreement`, `generated_network`, `flowing_frequency`, `water_budget`, `hydrograph_log`, `watertable_elevation`, `calibration_landscape`, `scatter_one_to_one`, `lake_stage` and the others `report.json` lists). Three pairs of former figures are merged. A figure the run cannot feed, such as `generated_network` on a run with no generated network, is not drawn and the log says why. `lake_stage` of a best run takes its lake from the run, and is skipped with the reason when the run holds more than one.
- `hmp config figures` lists what can be drawn, one row per name with its kind, frame, label, unit and status. `--kind frame|preset|special|variable` keeps one kind and `--run RUN` says what that run can draw. The JSON schema is `hmp.config.figures.v3`.
- A preset written in the `[display.presets]` of a project file is found by name on a run that already exists, so `hmp show RUN --figure NAME` draws it without a new run.
- The overview, cohort and comparison images take the new look (the `[display] theme`, 300 dpi, absolute kilometre ticks on the overview maps). The observed network is drawn in a light blue over a relief, where the dark blue was lost in the valleys.
- `quicklook` refuses a per-cell field and names the call that draws it, `run.figure(name)`.
- A flow parameter (K, Sy, Ss and the others of `[flow.param]`) can be read from a GeoTIFF that holds its own value in each pixel. Declare the raster by name under `[[data.property_map.sources]]` (`name`, `path`) and write `kind = "raster"` and `map = "<name>"` in `[flow.param.<id>.field]`, with the `unit` of the pixels. Each cell takes the mean of the pixels it covers, whatever its shape (regular, triangle or Voronoi), geometric for a conductivity and arithmetic for the others unless `mean` names `arithmetic`, `geometric` or `harmonic`. A map in another CRS than the mesh is read where it lies, without resampling. An active cell the map does not cover is refused with the name of the map, and a calibration of a parameter read from a map is refused before the first run.
- `base_config` takes a list of files, such as `base_config = ["sites/nancon.toml", "experiments/steady.toml"]`, and each of them may inherit others. A file two bases inherit is read once. For each key the most derived file that writes it wins, and two files that do not inherit each other must agree, or the file is refused with both names and both values. The items they add with `__append` are all kept, bases first. `hmp config resolve FILE --origin` writes each value of the merged file with the file that set it.

### Changed

- A TOML key renamed after 2.0.0 keeps loading, with a warning, until 3.0, so a file written for 2.0.0 loads in every 2.x. Inside the 2 line a stable key moves and is never removed, and `changes.toml` refuses a row that would remove one. A key that only a pre-release wrote keeps its delay and is refused from 2.2.0. Old Python names and old `hmp` commands keep the rule of two minor versions.
- An overlay that inherits a file the run file also inherits no longer applies that file again over the run file. The file is read once, and the values of the run file hold.
- The banner of a calibration protocol names its departures from the paper on one line, with the value of each, and `-v` says how each one departs. It took about forty lines.
- A transient run whose `[flow.param]` declares no `Sy` or no `Ss` takes `Sy = 0.05` and `Ss = 1e-5 1/m` as homogeneous fields, with a warning that names them, where MODFLOW refused it. Declare `[flow.param.Sy.field]` and `[flow.param.Ss.field]` to set other values.
- A NetCDF export opens in QGIS as a mesh with its CRS and every field. A model of one layer writes its fields without a `layer` dimension, so `ds["head"]` is `(time, n_face)` there. The `crs` variable carries `epsg` and `wkt` for MDAL, and `idomain` is a 32-bit integer, since MDAL dropped the whole mesh on a byte. QGIS also lists the file as rasters one row high: open the mesh. `layer` of `[[export]]` is a user key.
- `hmp.run` with `until_step`, played again with the same request, gives back the sealed run with the same solution key, or the partial run that already reached that step, instead of opening a new version. The check reads the run and claims nothing, and `outcome.json` now records the solution key for it.
- The seal names the attempt that wrote it, as `outcome.json` does, also when `prepare_solver` ran in an earlier attempt or window.
- A run stopped at `prepare_solver` now stores the ground of every cell (`mesh/topography`) when the flow backend builds a cell column, so its grid draws on the relief before the solve. The extractor writes it again after the solve, so a lake bed carved by MODFLOW 6 is the ground the run keeps. The stored bytes of a completed run do not change.
- The top and the bottom of every cell are built once at `prepare_solver`, on `Model.geometry.column`, and the MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT and Boussinesq builds read them instead of sampling the DEM again. The stored topography and heads are byte-identical. `TopSamplingConfig` moves to `hydromodpy.model.domain.top_sampling_config`, and a flow backend declares `cell_column`, `None` when it reads none.
- `hmp.open`, `RunOutcome.open()` and `Project.simulate(until_step=...)` give a partial `Run` for a run that wrote its facts but is not sealed yet. It reads and draws, and `record`, `checks`, `inputs` and `label()` still refuse until the seal. A run directory that wrote no facts is still refused.
- Figures have a new default look. A map carries its variable and unit as a left title and the time drawn as a right title, where a whole month reads `January 2017`. Its frame is bare with a scale bar in place of the km coordinates, the relief shades it, and the network and the catchment outline are drawn by default. A figure of one map takes the height of its map. Elevations use hypsometric tints, water levels blues to greens, and a water-table depth reads blue where the water is shallow. A mask leaves its class 0 undrawn, and `reduce = "frequency"` leaves the cells at zero undrawn. A section of a water table draws its lines through the cell centres, the ground in brown and the water in blue. It is cut under the water table when the aquifer is more than twice thicker than the ground above it, and a note gives the elevation of the base. `bbox` sets the window of a section, distances then elevations. The legend of a map or of a section sits inside the axes.
- A map keeps its relief and its scale bar when a figure writes its own `overlays`. The list replaces the outline, the network and the outlet only, so `overlays = ["mesh", "outline"]` no longer drops the shading and the scale, and `overlays = []` draws the map with these two alone.
- The example projects ask their figures with `[[display.figure]]`. A figure with `when = "session"` in a run file is not drawn by `hmp run`. Three example figures changed in kind: the concentration boxplot of example 09 reads in kg/m³ without its 50 mg/L line, and the water table depth maps of examples 00 and 06 no longer overlay the seepage cells or the particles, which `overlays = ["seepage", "pathlines"]` draws. Six example scripts still call a former figure name and are refused with the request to write: `run_manual.py` of examples 00, 01, 02, 03 and 05, and `build_concentration_animation.py` of example 09.
- The frozen runs of `tests/regression/frozen_runs` and `tests/regression/frozen_replay` are written again by their tools. Their values are those of 2.0.0rc1, except `mass_balance.percent_error` and `budget_pct`, which follow the change `mass_balance_percent_error_rounded`.
- The register of changes is `hydromodpy/schema/changes.toml`, read by `hydromodpy/schema/changes.py`. It lists each bug fix and each rule that moves a number, each default that moves with an edition, and each key that moves. The migration of a configuration is its rows of `document = "config"`, the label of a run reads its bugs, and the `Numbers` section of this changelog is generated from it. `hydromodpy/results/known_issues.toml` is removed.
- The maps of `hmp diff` and of the run comparison show a variable in its display unit, so a recharge reads in mm/day where the old maps used the stored unit.
- `[[simulation.process]] type`, which `hmp init` of a pre-release wrote, loads with a warning under its name `kind` and is refused from 2.2.0.
- `hmp run --frozen` no longer counts as a difference a key that the sealed `config.resolved.toml` does not write, when the replay holds it at its default. `lineage.drift` of a rerun lists such keys under `new_at_default`.
- A known bug of a data source declasses only the runs whose `config.toml` declares that source, through the token `source@<section>_<source>`. The three Hub’Eau bugs of a pre-release name `source@hydrometry_hubeau`, so a run that declares no Hub’Eau hydrometry keeps its label.
- `label_of` and `labelled_identity` of `hydromodpy.results.record.label` take the folder of the run, whose `config.toml` says the sources the run declared.
- The refusals of calibration keys, `flow.param` ids, `[export]` tables, `[flow.bc.<family>.<id>]` tables and sgrid keys of a pre-release of 2.0 name every key with its current name and say that this version does not rewrite the file. `renamed_to` of `hydromodpy.calibration.config_terms` takes the old key first.
- The refusal of a key only a pre-release wrote carries one fault per key in `details`, each with its JSON pointer, and the file in `source`.
- The sidecar reader applies the rows of `schema/changes.toml` marked `document = "sidecar"` instead of renaming `custom` to `file` in code.
- A transport backend receives the frozen `Model` of its flow, its options, the run slot of its flow and the `SolverRun` of that flow, through `build(model, options, slot, upstream=())`. It no longer reads the setup, the configuration or the run store.
- MODFLOW-NWT writes its flow-transport link file when a later run of the plan reads `face_flow`, and no longer looks for a run named `mt3dms` in the plan.
- The concentration of a transport run is stored under `concentration/<species>`, named by `spc_name`. Runs written by a pre-release still read.
- The calibration catalog lists the calibrable options of the backend that runs. `vka` is found that way.
- Every data source that goes to the network now does it under the bounds of the call, with its allowed hosts, byte ceiling and timeout: OpenStreetMap, EU-Hydro, BD Topage, SHOM, the two crossings sources, Hub’Eau piezometry, water quality and intermittency, and the area check of the gauge. Before, each opened a client under the default bounds.
- `hydromodpy.data.sites.importers.rows_from_hubeau` takes `bounds`, the bounds of the call for the station search and the BD Topage snap.
- The setup step resolves every [data] file and url source under the bounds of the call before the run is named, so allowed_roots holds for every section and not only for the DEM.
- Lake geometry, abacus and bathymetry are read by their data readers and bound by lake id again, and a cutoff wall or flow barrier line_path is read from the project root.
- GeographicConfig.from_outlet, from_dem and from_polygon lose their ignored dem argument.
- Every download goes through hydromodpy.core.io.fetch, with a client made for each call and the bounds of the call: allowed hosts, a byte cap of 2 GiB by default, and no private address unless the host is allowed by name. Redirections are followed by hand and checked at each hop.
- source = “custom” is now source = “file” in every [[data..sources]]. hmp doctor –fix-config rewrites it, and a sealed run reads it.
- A relative path is read from the project root only. A bare file name is no longer looked up in the workspace data folder, and a path that starts with a URL scheme is refused.
- The refusal of a bare file name gives the workspace name to write, `workspace:<name>`, when the file is in the folder of its variable.
- `[[mesh.refinement_zone]] path` is read as every other input file. A relative path is read from the project root, `workspace:<name>` reads `data/refinement_zone/<name>`, and a bare name is refused with the form to write. It was looked up in `data/refinement_zone/`, then in the data folder, then beside the configuration. A run tracks the layer with its digest and freezes it in that form.
- `hmp publish --package` reads a station folder whose files are named `<variable>_file_<id>_...`, as a run does, and no longer looks a file it does not find up in `data/<variable>/`.
- The lake and wall files are read by hydromodpy.data, and the binders of hydromodpy.model receive geometries and tables.
- `hydromodpy.analysis.compare` is now `hydromodpy.project.compare`, and `hydromodpy.examples` is now `hydromodpy.project.examples`. The rows behind `hmp example list` and `show` are `hydromodpy.project.examples.rows`.
- `masstransfer` of MODFLOW-NWT moved to `hydromodpy.solver.modflow_nwt.mt3dms.masstransfer`.
- `hydromodpy.solver.modflow_nwt.modpath._resolvers` is now the public module `hydromodpy.solver.modflow_nwt.modpath.resolvers`.
- The code behind `hmp catalog`, `data`, `lock`, `privacy`, `project`, `viz` and `workspace` moved from `hydromodpy.cli._workers` into the package each verb serves (`results.catalog.listing`, `results.catalog.liveness`, `results.catalog.privacy`, `results.catalog.indexer`, `results.catalog.federation`, `data.request.cache_verbs`, `data.workspace.folders`, `project.lock`, `display.catalog_figures`). The old paths are gone. Every command prints and exits as before.
- `find_workspace`, `find_data_workspace` and `find_workspace_root` moved from `hydromodpy.cli.helpers` to `hydromodpy.core.workspace.resolve`. `path_size` moved to `hydromodpy.core.io.filesystem`, `project_root_at` and `sites_project_root` to `hydromodpy.core.state.result_dirs`, and `remove_for_good` to `hydromodpy.results.trash`.
- `hmp run script.py` now says to run the script with `python`.
- `hmp dev test`, `hmp dev run-script` and `hmp dev examples` left the wheel. In a source checkout, run `python -m tools.dev test`, `python -m tools.dev run-script` or `python -m tools.dev examples manifest`. `hmp dev` answers with the new form.
- `hydromodpy.model` is new. It holds what a solver receives: `domain` (from `spatial.domain` and `spatial.lake_bed`, whose modules are now `model.domain.lake_bed_abacus` and `lake_bed_regrid`), `properties` (from `spatial.field`, with `physics.flow.physical_properties` and `property_ids`, and `solver.base.properties` now `model.properties.property_table`), `forcing` (from `spatial.forcing` and `physics.forcing`, with `physics.base.forcing` now `model.forcing.dated_forcing`, `physics.flow.time_forcing` now `model.forcing.time_forcing` and `physics.hydrology.synthetic.forcing` now `model.forcing.synthetic`), `boundaries` (the boundary conditions and the binders of `physics.flow`, with `binders.payloads` now `model.boundaries.binder_payloads`), `sinks_sources`, `initial` (`physics.flow.initial_conditions` as `initial.config`, `solver.base.initial_conditions` as `initial.heads`, and `simulation.spinup_config`), `time` (`regime`, `history_contract`), `soil` (`physics.hydrology.soil_reservoir` and `simulation.soil`) and `transport`.
- `Flow` is now in `hydromodpy.model.flow`. `FlowConfig` and its TOML loader are one module, `hydromodpy.model.flow_config`, which also holds `from_toml_section`, `normalize_bc_payloads` and `resolve_forcing_paths`. `physics.contracts`, `physics.base.payloads`, `physics.base.process_spatial`, `physics.flow.runtime_config` and `physics.flow.toml_examples` are modules at the top of `hydromodpy.model`.
- `hydromodpy.physics` and `hydromodpy.simulation` are gone, with every name their package files exported. Import a name from the module that defines it. `hmp.physics` and `hmp.simulation` no longer open a package.
- The plan, the planner, the plan runner and the `[simulation]` models moved from `hydromodpy.simulation` to `hydromodpy.solver.base`: `plan`, `planner`, `runner`, `transport_runs`, `simulation_config` (was `planning.config`), `observation_config` and `results_config`.
- `simulation.post_run` is now `hydromodpy.workflow.steps.run_outputs`, `simulation.catchment_aggregation` is `hydromodpy.results.derive.catchment_aggregation`, and `simulation.observation_ingest` is `hydromodpy.data.ingest.observations`.
- `spatial.geographic.structure_binders` is now `hydromodpy.model.domain.structure_binders`. `hydromodpy.spatial` no longer exports `Domain`, `DomainConfig` and `FieldParam`.
- The schema exported for a bare model class is named after its new module, for example `urn:hmp:schema:model.properties.physical_properties.FlowPhysicalProperties`.
- The config schema digest that a lockfile records changes once, because two descriptions name a module that moved. `hmp lock verify` reports it and still passes.
- `hydromodpy.mesh` is new. It holds what `hydromodpy.spatial.mesh` held: the mesh request and the `[mesh]` config, the planner, the engines, the cells and the exchange formats. Import `hydromodpy.spatial.mesh.<module>` as `hydromodpy.mesh.<module>`. `planning`, `engines`, `cells`, `io` and the modules at the top keep their names.
- The mesh objects moved from `hydromodpy.spatial.mesh.model` to `hydromodpy.mesh.planar` (`HydroMesh`, `PlanarCellMesh`, `CellType`, the geometry, the quality report and the regular grid), so the folder no longer reads like `hydromodpy.model`.
- `watershed_cell_mask` moved from `hydromodpy.spatial.geographic.delineated_catchment` to `hydromodpy.mesh.cells.in_polygons`, next to the cell mask it calls.
- `hydromodpy.spatial` no longer exports `CellBlock`, `CellType` and `HydroMesh`. Import them from `hydromodpy.mesh.planar.hydro_mesh` and `hydromodpy.mesh.planar.cell_types`.
- The entry-point group of mesh engines is still `hydromodpy.mesh.engine`.
- `hydromodpy.catchment` is new. It holds what was left of `hydromodpy.spatial` once `model` and `mesh` had their own package: `terrain`, `delineation`, `drainage` and `administrative`, unchanged inside, and the geographic pipeline in three parts. `algorithms` was `spatial.geographic.core`, and also holds `dem_metadata`, `geographic_paths` and `river_network_config`. `synthetic` was `spatial.geographic.synthetic`, with `synthetic_config`. `preprocess` is the rest of `spatial.geographic` (configuration, cache, pipeline, store ingestion, subbasin, regional flow job), with `pipeline_steps`. So `hydromodpy.spatial.geographic.core.pipeline_steps` is now `hydromodpy.catchment.preprocess.pipeline_steps`, and `hydromodpy.spatial.geographic.synthetic_config` is now `hydromodpy.catchment.synthetic.synthetic_config`.
- `RasterSupport`, `Surface`, `PreparedSurfaceSampler` and the geology source protocol are now in `hydromodpy.catchment.raster_support`, `surface`, `surface_sampling` and `protocols`. `spatial.job_inputs` is now `hydromodpy.model.domain.job_inputs`, next to the `domain-build` worker.
- `hydromodpy.spatial` is gone, with every name its package file exported. Import a name from the module that defines it. `hmp.spatial` no longer opens a package.
- `hydromodpy.catchment.terrain` no longer re-exports the terrain port. Import `TerrainEngine`, `CappedBreach` and the other port names from `hydromodpy.catchment.terrain.port`, and the two engines from `numpy_engine` and `whitebox_engine`. The entry-point group of terrain engines is still `hydromodpy.terrain.engine`.
- The bundled `departement.gpkg` moved with `administrative` to `hydromodpy/catchment/administrative/`.
- The solver backends read a frozen `hydromodpy.model.model.Model`: the geometry, the properties as profiles, the boundaries, the recharge, the ETP, the wells, the lakes, the SFR networks, the barriers, the start state, the time and four `[solver]` options. The `prepare_solver` step builds it once per run with `model_from_flow` and puts it on `setup.model`. `Modflow6`, `ModflowNwt` and `Boussinesq` keep it in `inputs` and never change it.
- `Modflow6` and `ModflowNwt` no longer take the geographic object, and their `pre_processing(model, options)` takes the `Model` in place of the flow, the domain and the cell mesh. `Boussinesq(model=..., runtime=...)` reads the `Model` and the `[flow.runtime]` options.
- `Flow` loses the fifteen Boussinesq settings it copied from `[flow.runtime]` (`runtime_backend`, `surface_interaction_model`, `partition_release_depth_m`, `runtime_max_iterations`, `runtime_tol_residual_inf`, `runtime_tol_state_update_inf`, `vi_substeps_per_period`, `vi_substep_on_failure`, `vi_max_adaptive_substeps`, `ts_vi_steps_per_period`, `ts_vi_adapt`, `ts_vi_dt_min_fraction`, `ts_vi_dt_max_fraction`, `ts_vi_type`, `ts_vi_snes_type`) and the unread `initial_condition_types` and `boundary_condition_application_domains`. Boussinesq reads `[flow.runtime]`.
- The start of a run is one of five records of `hydromodpy.model.initial.state`: `HeadRule`, `SteadyStart`, `CyclicStart`, `PriorState` and `SolvedState`. The models of the steady start and of a spin-up cycle are `steady_variant` and `cycle_variant` of `hydromodpy.model.model`, which return a new model. They replace `steady_flow_copy_for_initialization`, `cyclic_flow_copy_for_initialization`, `flow_uses_steady_state_initial_condition`, `flow_uses_cyclic_spinup` and `resolve_head_initial_condition`.
- `hydromodpy.model.initial.config` and `spinup_config` are one module, `hydromodpy.model.initial_config`. It also holds the `[flow.ic]` strategy readers (`initial_state_of`, `steady_state_strategy_of`, `cyclic_spinup_strategy_of`), which leave `hydromodpy.model.initial.heads`. `heads.py` keeps the numpy kernels and gains `restart_start_heads`.
- The soil reservoir modules other than the kernel move to `hydromodpy.model.forcing`: `soil.config`, `soil.columns`, `soil.grids`, `soil.recharge` and `soil.budget` are now `forcing.soil_config`, `soil_columns`, `soil_grids`, `soil_forcing` and `soil_budget`. `hydromodpy.model.soil` keeps `kernel`.
- The earlier run that `flow.restart_from` names is read once, before the solve, by `hydromodpy.results.storage.prior_state`. A run solved on another mesh is refused there with the same message as before, and the lake stages of the restart come from the `PriorState` of the model. `verify_restart_mesh`, `read_restart_lake_stages` and `read_final_head` move there from `hydromodpy.solver.modflow6.builders.initial_conditions`, with `written_step` and `reoriented_rows` from `hydromodpy.solver.modflow6.support.written_grid`, which is gone.
- `map_flow_properties`, `resolve_flow_property_arrays`, `require_positive_conductivity` and `require_positive_storage` take `profiles=` instead of `flow=`. A per-cell property override is set with `Model.with_properties`, which refuses a name that sets no property, and a `properties` key in the per-run overrides of the run context is refused by name.
- `ensure_flow` moves from `hydromodpy.solver.base.runner` to `hydromodpy.workflow.steps.data`. The runner no longer builds a `Flow`, and a flow run without the `Model` of the `prepare_solver` step stops with a `ConfigError` that names the step.
- `build_preprocess_options`, `require_cell_mesh` and `run_flow_model` read `setup.model` instead of `setup.flow`, `setup.domain`, `setup.cell_mesh` and `cfg.solver`. `channel_exits_for_build` takes the `ChannelRasters` that `channel_rasters_for_run` chooses, `run_basin` and the catchment functions take a `CatchmentGeometry`, `networks_route_drainage` takes a `Model`, `resolve_first_period_steady` takes `model=` and `step_persist_params` takes the parameter profiles of the `Model` instead of a `Flow`.
- The MODPATH and MT3DMS models read the DEM grid and the catchment polygon from `Model.geometry` through the MODFLOW-NWT solver. `get_geographic` of `hydromodpy.solver.modflow_nwt.modpath.resolvers` is replaced by `get_raster` and `get_catchment`.
- The auxiliary steady solve of MODFLOW 6 and MODFLOW-NWT always starts from the top of the model. It started 0.01 m below the top when `[flow.runtime]` set `backend = "petsc"` and `surface_interaction_model = "vi_obstacle"`, two Boussinesq settings. See the recipe `modflow_steady_start_ignores_boussinesq_runtime` of `changes.toml`.
- Every plugin surface (solver backends and extractors, data sources, mesh and terrain engines, trial evaluators) resolves through one registry class, `hydromodpy.core.plugin_registry.PluginRegistry`, with the calls `register`, `get` and `names`. A registry keys a class on one or more of its attributes joined by `_`, and an entry-point name is compared with that join and never split. The entry-point groups keep their names.
- Each registry module exposes its registry object and no module function: `solvers` and `extractors` in `hydromodpy.solver.base.registry`, `data_sources` in `hydromodpy.data.source.registry`, `mesh_engines` in `hydromodpy.mesh.registry`, `terrain_engines` in `hydromodpy.catchment.terrain.registry` and `evaluators` in `hydromodpy.calibration.evaluation.registry`. Write `mesh_engines.get(name)`, `terrain_engines.create(name)` or `evaluators.register(cls)` where the module functions `get`, `create`, `register`, `unregister` and `load_plugins` were called, `mesh_engines.names()` for `list_*_ids()`, `mesh_engines.names(shipped_only=True)` for `builtin_*_ids()`, `name in mesh_engines.names()` for `is_registered(name)`, and `evaluators.get(name).evaluator_id` for `resolve_id(name)`.
- A solver backend declares on its adapter class `name`, `process_type`, `accepted_meshes`, `geometry`, `writes`, `reads`, `supports`, `options`, `category`, `native_step`, `mutable` and `requires`. `solver_name` becomes `name`, `capabilities` is split into `writes` and `supports`, and the category moves from the extractor to the adapter. The registry refuses a backend that lacks one of them or declares one with the wrong type, and names it.
- An unknown solver key raises `SolverInputError` instead of `KeyError`.
- The category a run records in its manifest is the one its solver backend declares. The shipped backends keep theirs, and a third-party backend records its own where it recorded none.
- The refusals of `flow.restart_from` and of a cyclic spin-up read the traits `prior_state` and `cyclic_start` in the `supports` of the backend, and their message names the trait.
- `primary_solver_for_simulation` of `hydromodpy.workflow.steps.prepare_solver.facts` is now `primary_run_for_simulation` and returns the process type with the solver.
- The solver catalog of the reference shows what each backend declares (category, grid, meshes, what it writes and the traits it supports) in place of the capability names.
- `solver.backend` is a string, the name of a registered flow solver, for example `solver.backend = "modflow6"`. The table form `[solver.backend] kind = "..."`, and `kind = "custom"` with `name`, still loads with a warning, and `hmp doctor --fix-config` rewrites it. An unknown name is refused with the names this installation serves. A run under a plugin solver no longer lists `solver.backend` among its experimental keys.
- The settings of a flow solver are written under `[solver.<name>]`: `[modflow6]` is now `[solver.modflow6]`, `[modflownwt]` is now `[solver.modflow_nwt]` and `[flow.runtime]` is now `[solver.boussinesq]`. The old tables load with a warning, and `hmp doctor --fix-config` moves them. A plugin solver gets its own table, checked by its options class. A run sealed with the old tables reads back in silence, and `hmp run --frozen` compares them where they are now.
- `config.resolved.toml` holds the settings table of the flow solver the run used and the tables the file wrote, not the table of every shipped solver. A table of a solver that did not run counts for no drift on a replay.
- A name in `[[simulation.process]] solvers` is refused when the file is read if no solver of that process serves it, with the names this installation serves.
- A key the chosen flow solver does not honor is refused when the file is read, from the supports the solver declares, and the refusal names the solvers that honor it. A sealed run still reads and only warns. The K tensor, the pass-through cells of `[domain.layers]` and a layering under Boussinesq are now refused with `IncompatibleCapabilitiesError`, like a boundary, a restart or a soil reservoir the solver does not read.
- A transport solver is refused when the file is read if its `requires` does not name the flow solver of the run, with the flows it follows. A MODFLOW 6 flow with MODPATH or MT3DMS used to be refused only when the plan was built.
- An unknown key of `[flow.bc]` is refused with the seven boundaries the table holds, `drainage` included.
- The metric names a file may write come from one table, `hydromodpy.core.scoring.metric_table.METRIC_SPECS`.
